title: Biomedical Flight Controller (BME)
description:
Title:

Biomedical Flight Controller (BME)

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers and dreamers and we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

On the Human Health and Performance Contract we are at the forefront of safeguarding astronaut health, ensuring human performance, and advancing technologies for human space exploration.

We are seeking an International Space Station (ISS) and Gateway Biomedical Flight Controller (BME) at the NASA Johnson Space Center (JSC) in Houston, TX.

What You’ll Do: 

In this role, you play a role in supporting the International Space Station (ISS) as a Biomedical Flight Controller (BME) and the Gateway program as an Integrator. Overall, this Gateway BME will split half of their time between the two projects for 36 months, after which the employee and their managements will re-assess the division of support.  

The general function of the Biomedical Flight Controller (call-sign: BME) is to ensure astronaut health and safety by providing operational and technical support as representatives of the Human Health & Performance (HH&P) Directorate at NASA Johnson Space Center (JSC). The BME provides this support on console in the Mission Control Center (MCC) for the ISS, as well as off-console through various project assignments, meeting support, and other mission support roles. The BME is the primary Crew Health Care System (CHeCS) representative to the MCC flight control team; CHeCS includes all hardware/software in the CounterMeasures System (CMS), Environmental Health System (EHS), Health Maintenance System (HMS), and private video teleconferencing (for routine medical checkups, remote telemedicine support, and psychological support of family/friends). A large portion of the job corresponding to flight operations involves responding to new situations as they arise, thinking on your feet, and relying on your training to react in a real-time, fast-paced operational environment. Incumbent will perform other assignments and duties as required.

While not supporting console in MCC, this BME will serve as a Human Health and Performance (HHPC) Integrator for the Gateway program.  The position is part of a team of integrators and subject matter experts (SMEs) who work together to ensure Gateway adequately incorporates and implements NASA standards into vehicle/mission design. Working closely with other integrators, the Integrator will obtain and maintain technical knowledge across all human health and performance disciplines and engage SMEs for the details. HHP disciplines include crew health, environmental factors, medical operations, physiology, anthropometry, strength and biomechanics, maintenance and housekeeping, safety, habitability and architecture, information management, and displays and controls.  The position will participate in designated meetings and working groups as a mechanism for monitoring the incorporation of HHP design consideration in vehicle design. The Integrator will monitor how well HHPC requirements are met, ensure that issues of unmet or under met requirements are documented, communicate the status of these issues to the HMTA/HHP team, and prepare materials for communicating awareness or escalating issues as needed. The position will interface with HMTA and HHP NASA management as well as with Program personnel. 

Position may eventually include working console in MCC for Gateway operations.

You will:

Provide Flight Controller operational and engineering support from the Flight Control Room (FCR) and Multi-Purpose Support Room (MPSR) in the Mission Control Center (MCC) as it pertains to Medical Operations.
Monitor biomedical, environmental, and other crew-related data during all mission phases.
Perform and manage data/communications uplink and downlink in support of crew health and medical operations.
Provide technical support to the crew and flight control team for the Crew Health Care System (CHeCS).
Coordinate and conduct private video teleconferencing between the crew and their medical support team and family members on the ground.
Adhere to the Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) shift schedule for MCC Flight Controllers, which generally runs three (3) 9-hour shifts per  24-hour day. The majority of these shifts will be week-day only.  Though it is sometimes required to support MCC shifts as needed on weekends and holidays in support of mission duties.
Follow Space Station issues and provide/coordinate medical input when needed. Provide technical expertise to the Flight Surgeon in responding to crew health issues.
Perform duties as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for assigned CHeCS hardware, MCC console specialty project, and/or flight control documentation; SME duties include, but are not limited to:
Participate in pre-flight design & requirements reviews, provide operational insight and expertise, and prepare for operational execution of new CHeCS hardware
Write, submit, validate, and maintain operational procedures for CHeCS equipment and crew medical activities
Update requirements, activity planning documentation, and technical reference documentation as necessary
React to any anomalies/issues related to CHeCS equipment and crew medical activities to provide MCC console personnel with resources necessary to address or workaround the issue
Communicate/collaborate/coordinate with other mission support personnel to assess on-going operations, equipment anomalies, and plans for activities utilizing equipment
Assimilate information from various sources and act as liaison with representatives from Flight Surgeon, Engineering, Training, Exercise Specialists, Laboratory and Science communities that support CHeCS equipment and requirements
Assist in the coordination of manifest, stowage, packing, and unpacking inputs for CHeCS hardware
Follow structured Space Station certification training program to meet specific training milestones in a timely manner. Meet all requirements to obtain Space Station Flight Controller certification for supporting MCC operations. Continue proficiency training following MCC certification.
Must be able to work well both individually with a high degree of initiative and self-starter motivation, as well as in group environments that at times may require acting as the sole Medical Operations representative on a team.
Completion of a standard flight controller physical examination and government background check are required.
Represent all HH&P requirements during the design phase.
Represent HH&P at design milestones (i.e., SRR, PDR, CDR).
Review verification and certification of vehicles, hardware, and software in development.
Maintain a broad knowledge of all HH&P requirements and engage Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) for the technical details and direction.
Integrate of HH&P operational activities.
Document and tracking concerns and decisions.
Develop and executing a plan for documenting operational processes.
Coordinate technical subject matter experts (SME), as needed.
Provide insight into compliance with HMTA mandatory standards.
Inform HMTA decisions by participating in Program activities
Coordinate and participating in Program document and design reviews
Develop corresponding summary assessments and following up on resulting actions
Develop requirements mapping from HMTA standards to Program documents and corresponding gap analysis
Review and assessing integrated test and analysis activities
Formulate, summarizing, and representing an HH&P position based on subject matter expertise for Program reviews
Develop position papers and/or requirements interpretations for human health and performance issues
Disseminate information to HH&P management and subject matter experts

What You Bring:

You bring experience leading a team of experts in different fields towards a common goal.  You use your experience and judgment to support both the ISS and Gateway programs in real-time operations and planning. You comply with KBR’s Safety, Health and Environmental Plan, Quality Plan, and all safety policies and procedures, and complete all assigned training.

Your Qualifications:

Bachelor of Science Degree in Biomedical Engineering or a related Engineering/Sciences field
Desired
A background in physiology or associated coursework
Prior experience in the spaceflight industry
Mission Control or other operational experience
Experience with human systems requirements/verification

Your Skills:

Communication (both verbal and written)
Problem solving
Critical thinking
Leadership
Organizational skills

What to Expect

This position is expected to be 100% on site and 100%in person. Occasional travel may be required.

description:
Title:

Airfield Manager

KBR’s Mission Engineering Division delivers complex technical solutions and expert support to the U.S. Department of Defense, specializing in modeling and simulation, cyber transformation, air vehicle mission integration, and lifecycle support. As a trusted partner with a proven history in mission technology, KBR collaborates closely with clients to develop innovative and effective solutions. With a strong ethical framework, KBR prioritizes data security, privacy, and responsible information management to ensure mission success.

The Airfield Manager is responsible for ensuring the daily safety, security, and operational efficiency of the private-use airfield at Reese National Security Complex (RNSC).

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Direct and coordinate daily aircraft movements, including fixed-wing, rotary-wing, unmanned, and experimental aircraft. Manage airfield access and scheduling for tenants, research teams, and visiting aircraft. Monitor and maintain airfield readiness, including runway, taxiway, and apron conditions.
Ensure compliance with applicable FAA, DoW, ICAO, and RNSC operational standards. Conduct routine safety audits and risk assessments. Develop and implement emergency response protocols tailored to dissimilar aircraft operations. Maintain wildlife and environmental compliance plans.
Serve as the primary liaison between RNSC, LRRA, aerospace tenants, TTU research teams, and regulatory agencies. Facilitate communication and coordination for joint operations, testing schedules, and infrastructure use. Direct the planning and coordination of airfield events and use.
Oversee maintenance of airfield infrastructure including lighting, signage, and navigational aids. Coordinate with engineering and maintenance teams for repairs, upgrades, and capital improvements.Track and report on airfield asset conditions and operational needs.
Documentation and Reporting Maintain accurate records of aircraft operations, inspections, incidents, and maintenance. Prepare operational reports for RNSC leadership and regulatory bodies. Support grant applications and compliance documentation with relevant operational data.'
Personnel Management Train and supervise ground operations staff and contractors. Ensure personnel are briefed and certified for handling dissimilar aircraft and research protocols. Escort vendors, contractors, and visitors on and off the airfield
Strategic Planning Contribute to long-term planning for airfield development, tenant expansion, and research integration. Assess future operational needs based on evolving aerospace and defense-related activities

Must be a US Citizen. DOD Secret clearance 
Bachelor’s degree in Aviation Management, Aeronautical Science, or related field (Master’s preferred).
Minimum 5 years of experience in airfield operations or airport management.
Familiarity with FAA Part 139, DoW airfield standards, and experimental aircraft operations.

Excellent computer skills, specifically with security systems, badging programs, and access control technologies

The Mission Ahead

title: Senior FMS Program Analyst
description:
Title:

Senior FMS Program Analyst

Program Summary

KBR’s Missile, Aviation, and Ground Systems (MAGS) division delivers mission engineering solutions for critical U.S. Army programs, specializing in aviation and ground systems, integrated air and missile defense, and threat and target systems. As a trusted partner of the U.S. Department of Defense, MAGS provides innovative, technology-driven solutions to enhance national security. With a global presence and a strong ethical framework, KBR ensures secure, effective, and mission-ready capabilities worldwide.

Job Summary

Join the Program Acquisition Executive, Fires – SHIELD Project Office in a dynamic, fast-paced environment supporting critical international defense programs. As a Senior FMS Program Analyst, you will lead the end-to-end management of foreign partner programs, ensuring seamless execution and alignment with U.S. Army objectives. The SHIELD Project Office requires a Senior Engineer to support the National Advanced Surface to Air Missile System (NASAMS) team. The position involves working with the Prime Contractor to develop, integrate, and test all aspects of the NASAMS architecture prior to fielding on behalf of Foreign Military Sales (FMS) cases.   The candidate will assess NASAMS FMS customer requests for country-unique hardware and software requirements.  This may include implementing Cross Domain Solutions, unique data links, A/B interfaces between sensors and command and control, as well as voice communication devices.  The NASAMS senior engineer will ensure all USG and FMS partner data is appropriately protected within the offered architecture.  This individual will provide the USG with risk, technical feasibility assessments, and insights into the reasonableness of cost estimates from the Prime Contractor. 

Roles and Responsibilities 

Candidates must have in-depth knowledge of National Advanced Surface to Air Missile System (NASAMS) including overall architecture, functional, technical, and operational knowledge of the system and the system's Major End Items (MEIs).  Technical and performance knowledge of the sensors and effectors used in the NASAMS system is a must. 
Candidates must possess proven experience assessing the solutions and requirements defined by Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)/suppliers for technical integration of the Radio Frequency (RF) and Electro-Optical (EO) sensors into the NASAMS architecture, as well as requirements to meet country-specific needs.
Candidates must possess a proven track record with communications with NASAMS MEIs as well as communications up to Higher Echelon Headquarters.
Candidates should have experience engaging with international customers to understand, define requirements, and align NASAMS capability to develop Letter of Request (LOR) for Pricing and Availability (P&A) and LOR for Letter of Acceptance (LOA). 
Candidates must have a proven track record of having actively participated in System Requirements Reviews, Preliminary Design Reviews, and Critical Design Reviews during program execution.   
Candidates must have experience with technically managing suppliers during program execution.
Candidates should have a multidisciplinary background including software, program management, and engineering.
Candidates must have actively engaged with customers to support and represent programmatic and technical issues.
Candidates must have experience in evaluating OEM and supplier technical and cost proposals to identify risks and opportunities to support the development of the FMS case and the execution of the program.
Candidates should have a degree in Engineering. Program Management certification is a plus.
A working knowledge of the defense acquisition process, budget, and the timeline of various countries is strongly desired.
Knowledge of Patriot Air Defense and HAWK/HAWK XXI Air Defense along with International Air Defense systems is desired to assist the program office.
Experience working with the NASAMS team, the Program Office, and other US government stakeholders is desired.
Candidates must be willing to travel and support all phases of program development and execution.  

Basic Qualifications 

Bachelor’s degree (BS) in Engineering or Science
Minimum 20 years of experience
Alternate Education and Experience – Master of Science degree with 18 years; or Doctorate with 16 years.
Active security clearance
Ability to travel up to 20%

description:
Title:

Strength and Conditioning Specialist (National Capital Region)

THIS POSITION OFFERS RELOCATION

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!  

KBR is a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers; but we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.  We maintain a highly qualified workforce to help care for service people and astronauts across the world.  We attract the best minds because our expertise thrives on creativity, resourcefulness, and collaboration. That is how we supply our clients with cutting-edge solutions and services. 

We are seeking a stellar Special Operations Strength and Conditioning Specialist that will establish and administer effective strength and conditioning protocols designed to maximize the physical performance of SOF personnel, with the priority on SOF Operators and Direct Combat Support personnel.  

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:  

Demonstrate and provide instruction and guidance on physical training, exercises, movements, and injury avoidance. 

Design, administer, evaluate, and document the effects of physical training protocols for SOF personnel in garrison, TDY/TAD, or deployment, under the supervision of the HP program manager and/or coordinator.  

Coordinate training programs with the HP staff to ensure a safe and expeditious return to training of SOF personnel recovering from injury.  

Refer all personnel with an apparent new or undiagnosed medical condition to a medical provider for evaluation and treatment.  

Communicate and collaborate with sports medicine professionals and/or bridge coordinator to ensure a smooth transition from rehabilitation to performance based activities. Will also collaborate with mental performance and performance nutrition to ensure a holistic approach to human performance. 

Assist the HP program Manager and/or Coordinator in developing facility standard operating procedures, guidelines, and training protocols including the safe use of strength and conditioning equipment.  

Participate in periodic meetings to review and evaluate physical training programs and identify opportunities for improvement. If a meeting occurs outside of regular working hours-unable to attend a meeting, the SCS is responsible for reviewing the information disseminated in meetings.   

Participate in periodic in-service training for members of the HP staff and/or POTFF staff as appropriate.  

Attend required training in accordance with guiding instructions. Commands will allow attendance at the necessary conferences or courses to complete the continuing education units required to maintain professional certifications.  

Perform administrative duties such as maintaining records of utilization, workload, conducting or participating in education programs, and participating in clinical staff quality assurance functions.  

Develop and promulgate training materials as requested and required by the HP program Manager and/or Coordinator.  

Assist with supply inventories and provide input regarding supply needs for the HP program.  

Proficiently utilize computers, software, and technologies as required and requested by the HP program Manager and/or Coordinator and required by USSOCOM HQ and its POTFF staff. 

Maintain 100% compliance with local mandatory command training requirements. 

Advise the chain of command and/or HP program manager and/or coordinator on strength and conditioning, administrative matters, purchasing of supplies and equipment, and supplemental fiscal requests. 

Required Education/Experience/Skills/Training:  

Position requires U.S. Citizenship. 

Must have a DoD Secret Clearance or the ability to obtain one. 

Bachelor’s Degree in an accredited exercise science, health science, or physical education-related discipline. 

Possess and maintain current certification by the National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA) as a Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist (CSCS) or the Strength & Conditioning Coach Certified (SCCC) through the Collegiate Strength & Conditioning Coaches association (CSCCa). Maintenance of one of these certifications shall be an enduring element of the requirement. 

Minimum of 5 years or more of demonstrable accumulated experience (continuous and sustained experience preferred) of developing long and short-range planning and coordination of sport/mission specific performance programs resulting in attributable results with individual athletes and groups of athletes at the levels of NCAA Collegiate, Olympic, professional sports, and/or SOF Operators in the accompanying, respective settings.  Paid, full-time experience as a government civilian or contract employee at United States Combat Arms, Air Force Special Warfare, and Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD)  communities may be counted towards minimum qualification requirements, provided this experience was gained within the most recent, continuous 3 years, as a directly-embedded staff member, on-site with the respective Army, Navy, Air Force and/or Marine Corps entities. 

Fluent oral and written communication skills in English.  

Current certification in basic Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) to include Automated External Defibrillator (AED) training. 

Physical proficiency to demonstrate all prescribed exercises / techniques and to hike over rough terrain and function in austere environments.  

Must be able to lift and manipulate loads and weights up to 25 kilograms. 

Desired Education/Experience/Skills/Training:  

Prior military and/or SOF experience.  

Master's degree in an accredited exercise science, health science, or physical education-related discipline.

Must comply with Safety, Health and Environmental plan, policies and procedures.

description:
Title:

Management Analyst

KBR’s Mission Engineering Division delivers complex technical solutions and expert support to the U.S. Department of War, specializing in modeling and simulation, cyber transformation, air vehicle mission integration, and lifecycle support. As a trusted partner with a proven history in mission technology, KBR collaborates closely with clients to develop innovative and effective solutions. With a strong ethical framework, KBR prioritizes data security, privacy, and responsible information management to ensure mission success.

KBR is seeking a Management Analyst to support program and operational performance by providing analysis, reporting, and coordination across business, technical, and customer-facing activities. The ideal candidate is organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast-paced, matrixed environment while producing high-quality deliverables that support leadership decision-making. In this role, you will support program management and operational execution by analyzing data, tracking performance, maintaining program artifacts, and coordinating cross-functional actions. You’ll build and maintain reporting products, support planning and scheduling activities, and help ensure deliverables are completed on time and aligned to customer and contract requirements.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Support program and business management activities including planning, coordination, and execution tracking.
Collect, validate, analyze, and interpret data to support program performance, status reporting, and leadership decisions (e.g., metrics, trends, variances, action items).
Develop and maintain recurring and ad hoc reports (dashboards, scorecards, briefings, weekly/monthly status).
Maintain key program artifacts such as action item trackers, meeting minutes, schedules, risk/issue logs, milestone trackers, and deliverable registers.
Coordinate with cross-functional stakeholders (program management, engineering, logistics, finance, contracts, HR, and customer counterparts) to ensure alignment and timely completion of tasks.
Support process improvement efforts by documenting workflows, identifying gaps, and recommending enhancements to increase efficiency and compliance.
Prepare professional communications including presentations, correspondence, decision memos, and executive-ready briefings.
Ensure accuracy, consistency, and confidentiality of program data and documentation in accordance with company policy and contract requirements.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:  

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Management, accounting, economics, marketing, or a related  business field. Equivalent experience may be considered in lieu of a degree, depending on contract requirements.
Experience: 3+ years experience supporting program operations, analysis, management consulting, PMO support, or similar functions.
Security/Clearance: Active Secret clearance. Must be a US Citizen.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Experience supporting a DoD or Federal Program Office (e.g., NAVAIR/NAVSEA/USAF/Army).
Experience with CUXS programs.

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! 

Program Summary

KBR maintains and manages Army prepositioned stocks at the Army Field Support Battalion - Charleston (AFSBn-CHS) land site to include all logistics and maintenance operations. The KBR APS-3 Program is managed and executed at Goose Creek in support of the Army’s power projection doctrine and resources.  The contract provides maintenance of APS-3 stocks (Class II, IIIP, IV, VII, IX) to ensure that unit sets are configured and maintained at optimal readiness.  KBR also provides maintenance services and logistical support for other Army programs, IAW individual scope of work contract requirements.

Job Summary

KBR is seeking an experienced Power Apps Platform Developer to work on-site to join our team in Goose Creek, SC. This position develops, maintains, and optimizes our database systems. The position collaborates across KBR’s department managers and section supervisors, and the US Government (KBR’s customer). This role requires proficiency in PowerApps. description:
Title:

Cloud Management Dashboard Intern

BELONG. CONNECT. GROW. with KBR.

Around here, we define the future. We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

Role Overview

At KBR, we are dedicated to advancing technology and providing innovative solutions to our clients. We are looking for a talented and motivated individual to join our team and help us lead the way in hybrid environment instrumentation at an enterprise scale.

As part of KBR, you will have the opportunity to develop and enhance the tools and dashboards that are crucial for the success of various teams, including DevOps, Security, and Systems Administration/Engineering. Your contributions will directly impact how we manage and monitor complex systems, ensuring efficiency and security across our operations.

This is a hands-on role where you’ll develop how hybrid environments are instrumented at enterprise scale and contribute code and dashboards that are used by real teams (DevOps, Security, Systems Administration/Engineering).

*** Three years of continuous U.S. residency required ***

Responsibilities

Data Ingestion & Integration

Write scripts and REST/API calls to collect data from cloud accounts as well as on premises sources such as Kubernetes and vCenter.
Write scripts and REST/API calls to collect cost and security information to aggregate and process.

Aggregation & Processing

Normalize disparate data (metrics, events, billing, security findings) and publish to a centralized data location for display.
Implement basic ETL steps: shape, label, and enrich data to support drill‑downs and multi‑tenant views.

Dashboards & Visualization

Build dashboards that show high‑level health/capacity and enable drill‑down to specific services, clusters, nodes, or costs.
Performance, Security, and Cost
Track SLIs/SLOs (latency, availability, saturation), security posture (e.g., misconfigurations, vulnerabilities), and cloud/on-prem costs.
Prototype recommendations/remediation hints (e.g., right‑sizing, idle resource cleanup, patch drift).

Minimum Qualifications

Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, or related field.
Foundational knowledge of AWS (can identify common services/resources; understands CloudWatch/CloudTrail concepts).
Comfortable writing scripts in to call REST/JSON APIs, or to scrape and process data.
Basic exposure to Kubernetes (pods, services, namespaces) and Prometheus/Grafana (metrics, queries, panels).
Familiarity with Linux, containers, and Git-based workflows.
Strong problem-solving, curiosity, and willingness to learn enterprise tooling.
*** Three years of continuous U.S. residency required ***

Primary Tools & Technologies

Metrics & Visualization

Prometheus – Metrics collection and alerting (can integrate with AWS workloads)
Grafana – Dashboarding and visualization (including Amazon Managed Grafana)
Amazon CloudWatch – Metrics, logs, dashboards, and alarms

AWS Services

CloudWatch – Core observability (metrics, logs, dashboards)
CloudTrail – API activity tracking
AWS Config – Resource compliance and configuration history
Cost Explorer / CUR (Cost & Usage Reports) – Cost monitoring and optimization
AWS X-Ray – Distributed tracing for applications
AWS OpenSearch Service – Log aggregation and search
AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) – Instrumentation for metrics and traces

Languages

Python – Automation, data processing, API integration
PowerShell – Windows-based automation (if applicable)

Automation / IaC

Terraform – Infrastructure as Code
AWS CloudFormation – Native IaC
GitHub / GitLab – Version control and CI/CD

APIs / ETL

REST / JSON – API integration
AWS SDKs (boto3 for Python) – AWS automation and data extraction
Lightweight ETL – For transforming CloudWatch/Cost data into dashboards

*** Three years of continuous U.S. residency required ***

Equivalent education and/or experience will be considered.

Title:

Sr Operations Research /Systems Analyst

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Come join the ITEA award winning TRMC BDKM team and be a part of the team responsible for revolutionizing how data analysis is performed across the entire Department of Defense

Key Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will be part of the KBR team supporting the Test Resource Management Center’s (TRMC) Big Data (BD) and Knowledge Management (KM) Team working on BD and KM systems supporting DoD Test Ranges and various acquisition programs.

Data Driven Analysis: Candidate will support our customers with insights gained from analyzing DoD Test & Evaluation data. Responsible for enabling the development of data-driven decision analysis products through the innovative application, and promotion, of novel methods from data science, machine learning, and operations research to provide robust and flexible testing and evaluation capabilities to support DoD modernization. Candidates should have a passion for discovering insights hidden in large data sets and working with stakeholders to improve business outcomes through the delivery of high-quality products.
Data Mining: Must have strong experience using a variety of data mining and data analysis methods, accessing data stored in a variety of data storage paradigms, developing models using common statistical and machine learning modeling approaches, using and creating custom algorithms, implementing analysis workflows in Python or R, and writing reports and documentation.
Analytic Experience: Responsible for providing analytic consulting services, supporting analytic workflow and product development and testing, promoting the user adoption of methods and best practices from data science, conducting applied methods projects, and supporting the creation of analysis-ready data.  The candidate should be skilled at identifying opportunities for process or workflow optimization.
Customer-Facing Experience: Candidate will be the face of the CHEETAS Team and will be responsible for ensuring stakeholders have the analytical tools, data products and reports they need to make insightful recommendations based on your data driven analysis. 
Stakeholder Assistance: The ideal candidate is adept at collaborating with technical and non-technical stakeholders to identify analytic requirements and analysis questions that can be informed through the aggregation and analysis of large data sets collected during test events or exercises.
Communication: Proven ability to drive decisions through successful communication, in written or presented form, of their data-based insights. Must have the ability to effectively communicate at both a programmatic and technical level. 
Technical Support: The successful candidate will have extensive technical expertise in methods from operations research and experience working on Department of Defense problems. The candidate will have reach-back support from the software engineering, data science and system administration teams.  While onsite, candidate will be responsible for running and operating CHEETAS (and other tools); demonstrating these tools to stakeholders & VIPs; conveying analysis results; adapting internally-developed tools, notebooks and reports to meet emerging needs; gathering use cases, requirements, gaps and needs from stakeholders and for larger development items providing that information as feature requests or bug reports to the CHEETAS development team; and performing impromptu hands-on training sessions with end users and potentially troubleshooting problems from within closed networks without internet access (with support from distributed team members).  
Independent Work: Successful candidates must be self-motivated and capable of working independently with little supervision / direct tasking.  The candidate should have experience using a variety of methods and models to test the effectiveness of different courses of action.

Work Environment:

Location: Remote
Travel Requirements: This position will require travel of 25% with potential surge to 50% to support end users located at various DoD labs and ranges located across the US.  When not supporting a site, this position can work remotely or from a nearby KBR office (if available and desired). 
Working Hours: Standard, although you potentially may be the only team member physically on-site providing support, you will not be alone. 

Basic Qualifications:

Security Clearance: Active TS/SCI clearance
Education: An advanced degree in operations research, engineering, applied math, statistics, computer science or information technology with preferred 12+ years of experience within DoD. 
DOD Specific Experience: Candidates with 5-10 years of DoD experience will be considered on a case-by-case basis. 
Experience: Previous experience should include working with end users, gathering requirements and refining/operating data analysis tools or products to meet user needs.  Previous experience should include developing and interpreting the results of analytic products with DoD specific data types.

Qualifications Required:

Experience using scripting languages (Python and R) to process, analyze and visualize data.
Experience using notebooks (Jupyter Notebooks and RMarkdown) to create reproducible and explainable products.
Experience using interactive visualization tools (RShiny, pyShiny, Dash) to create interactive analytics.
Experience generating and presenting reports, visualizations and findings to customers.
Experience using analysis methods, including supervised and unsupervised methods, to work with time series and geospatial data.
Experience working with Windows, Linux, and containers.
Experience querying databases using SQL.
Ability to make insightful recommendations based on data driven analysis and customer interactions.
Ability to effectively communicate both orally and in writing with customers and teammates.
Ability to speak and present findings in front of large groups.
Ability to document and repeat procedures.
Ability to train novice end users on the use of tools.
Should be self-motivated to design, develop, enhance, reengineer or integrate software applications to improve the quality of data outputs available for end users.

Preferred Qualifications: 

12+ years of DOD experience
Experience as a military ORSA.
Experience working in government / defense labs and within their computing restrictions.
Knowledge of military force structure and/or tactical messaging.
Experience working with major DoD experimentation events, such as Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) events.
Experience working with major DoD acquisition programs, such as Joint Strike Fighter (JSF).
Knowledge of the Test and Training Enabling Architecture (TENA), the Joint Mission Environment Testing Capability (JMETC) and distributed testing and training.
Knowledge of DoD cybersecurity policies.

$150,000 - $225,000

Title:

Sr Operations Research / Systems Analyst

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Come join the ITEA award winning TRMC BDKM team and be a part of the team responsible for revolutionizing how data analysis is performed across the entire Department of Defense

Key Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will be part of the KBR team supporting the Test Resource Management Center’s (TRMC) Big Data (BD) and Knowledge Management (KM) Team working on BD and KM systems supporting DoD Test Ranges and various acquisition programs.

Data Driven Analysis: Candidate will support our customers with insights gained from analyzing DoD Test & Evaluation data. Responsible for enabling the development of data-driven decision analysis products through the innovative application, and promotion, of novel methods from data science, machine learning, and operations research to provide robust and flexible testing and evaluation capabilities to support DoD modernization. Candidates should have a passion for discovering insights hidden in large data sets and working with stakeholders to improve business outcomes through the delivery of high-quality products.
Data Mining: Must have strong experience using a variety of data mining and data analysis methods, accessing data stored in a variety of data storage paradigms, developing models using common statistical and machine learning modeling approaches, using and creating custom algorithms, implementing analysis workflows in Python or R, and writing reports and documentation.
Analytic Experience: Responsible for providing analytic consulting services, supporting analytic workflow and product development and testing, promoting the user adoption of methods and best practices from data science, conducting applied methods projects, and supporting the creation of analysis-ready data.  The candidate should be skilled at identifying opportunities for process or workflow optimization.
Customer-Facing Experience: Candidate will be the face of the CHEETAS Team and will be responsible for ensuring stakeholders have the analytical tools, data products and reports they need to make insightful recommendations based on your data driven analysis. 
Stakeholder Assistance: The ideal candidate is adept at collaborating with technical and non-technical stakeholders to identify analytic requirements and analysis questions that can be informed through the aggregation and analysis of large data sets collected during test events or exercises.
Communication: Proven ability to drive decisions through successful communication, in written or presented form, of their data-based insights. Must have the ability to effectively communicate at both a programmatic and technical level. 
Technical Support: The successful candidate will have extensive technical expertise in methods from operations research and experience working on Department of Defense problems. The candidate will have reach-back support from the software engineering, data science and system administration teams.  While onsite, candidate will be responsible for running and operating CHEETAS (and other tools); demonstrating these tools to stakeholders & VIPs; conveying analysis results; adapting internally-developed tools, notebooks and reports to meet emerging needs; gathering use cases, requirements, gaps and needs from stakeholders and for larger development items providing that information as feature requests or bug reports to the CHEETAS development team; and performing impromptu hands-on training sessions with end users and potentially troubleshooting problems from within closed networks without internet access (with support from distributed team members).  
Independent Work: Successful candidates must be self-motivated and capable of working independently with little supervision / direct tasking.  The candidate should have experience using a variety of methods and models to test the effectiveness of different courses of action.

Work Environment:

Location: Remote

Travel Requirements: This position will require travel of 25% with potential surge to 50% to support end users located at various DoD ranges & labs located across the US.  When not supporting a site, this position can work remotely or from a nearby KBR office (if available and desired). 
Working Hours: Standard, although you potentially may be the only team member physically on-site providing support, you will not be alone. 

Basic Qualifications:

Security Clearance: Active TS/SCI clearance
Education: An advanced degree in operations research, engineering, applied math, statistics, computer science or information technology with preferred 12+ years of experience within DoD. 
DOD Specific Experience: Candidates with 5-10 years of DoD experience will be considered on a case-by-case basis. 
Experience: Previous experience should include working with end users, gathering requirements and refining/operating data analysis tools or products to meet user needs.  Previous experience should include developing and interpreting the results of analytic products with DoD specific data types.

Qualifications Required:

Experience using scripting languages (Python and R) to process, analyze and visualize data.
Experience using notebooks (Jupyter Notebooks and RMarkdown) to create reproducible and explainable products.
Experience using interactive visualization tools (RShiny, pyShiny, Dash) to create interactive analytics.
Experience generating and presenting reports, visualizations and findings to customers.
Experience using analysis methods, including supervised and unsupervised methods, to work with time series and geospatial data.
Experience working with Windows, Linux, and containers.
Experience querying databases using SQL.
Ability to make insightful recommendations based on data driven analysis and customer interactions.
Ability to effectively communicate both orally and in writing with customers and teammates.
Ability to speak and present findings in front of large groups.
Ability to document and repeat procedures.
Ability to train novice end users on the use of tools.
Should be self-motivated to design, develop, enhance, reengineer or integrate software applications to improve the quality of data outputs available for end users.

Preferred Qualifications: 

12+ years of DOD experience
Experience as a military ORSA.
Experience working in government / defense labs and within their computing restrictions.
Knowledge of military force structure and/or tactical messaging.
Experience working with major DoD experimentation events, such as Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) events.
Experience working with major DoD acquisition programs, such as Joint Strike Fighter (JSF).
Knowledge of the Test and Training Enabling Architecture (TENA), the Joint Mission Environment Testing Capability (JMETC) and distributed testing and training.
Knowledge of DoD cybersecurity policies.

At KBR, we partner with government and industry clients to provide purposeful and comprehensive solutions with an emphasis on efficiency and safety. With a full portfolio of services, proprietary technologies and expertise, our employees are ready to handle projects and missions from planning and design to sustainability and maintenance. Whether at the bottom of the ocean or in outer space, our clients trust us to deliver the impossible on a daily basis.

This Project Manager is a key role and will be responsible for delivering assigned packages of work using the NEC4 form of contract as directed by the Senior Project Manager.  The packages of work vary in complexity and may include civils, structural, M&E or marine engineering.

Risk management.

Demonstrable project management experience within multi-million-pound infrastructure construction, refurbishment and replacement programmes of work, within a complex regulated environment (preferably Nuclear).

Coach and mentor junior team members to continuously improve the quality of delivery.

Title:

Market Sector Director – Buildings

KBR is seeking an accomplished and visionary Market Sector Director – Buildings to lead our national Buildings segment. This senior leadership role sits at the forefront of our Infrastructure Solutions Australia business, driving strategic growth, sector leadership, and exceptional delivery outcomes across a diverse and high‑value portfolio.

As a key member of our leadership team, you will lead and implement the Buildings market strategy across all market sub-segments - Health, Education, Corrections, Aviation, Events, Commercial, Industrial, land‑development sectors etc – also spanning all engineering, specialty and advisory disciplines. You will also take ownership of client relationships, project portfolio performance (including profit and loss), and ultimately own the success of one of KBR’s most strategically important market segments.

About the Role

The Market Sector Director – Buildings is responsible for leading and governing a multi‑disciplinary, national portfolio encompassing multiple smaller projects through to larger major programs exceeding $1B in capital value. This role requires someone motivated to lead and grow a team and an existing successful business for the longer term; it is ideally suited to an executive level thinker capable of both shaping long‑term strategy and driving short‑term delivery excellence.

You will:

Develop and implement a multi‑year sector strategy to expand KBR’s market presence and drive profitable growth.
Lead business development, identify new opportunities, and secure new contracts—often personally acting as Project Director or Bid Leader for strategic pursuits.
Build and sustain relationships with senior‑level government and private‑sector stakeholders, representing KBR as a thought leader within the industry.
Oversee the successful delivery of the buildings project portfolio, ensuring commercial, risk, schedule, safety and client‑satisfaction outcomes are achieved.
Shape a high‑performance culture, attract and retain top talent, and champion KBR’s values across our Australian offices.
Drive financial performance, ensuring revenue, job income, overhead recovery, and business unit  income targets are consistently met or exceeded.

Key Skills & Experience

We are seeking a leader with:

Proven credibility in the buildings sector or broader property or built environment, ideally at the executive level.
Capability to lead complex, multi‑disciplinary teams across multiple states.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including P\&L accountability.
Demonstrated success in strategy development, client engagement, and winning significant work.
A track record of delivering complex projects and navigating risk in high‑value portfolios.
Advanced leadership capabilities including influencing, inspiring others, facilitating change and coaching teams.

Why Join KBR?

At KBR, you will shape the future of infrastructure in Australia while being part of a global organisation delivering some of the most significant engineering, technology, and advisory projects worldwide. You’ll play a pivotal role in leading and growing a major business unit, supported by a high‑performing national team and international expertise.

You will enjoy working with a high-performing team, who live and breathe KBR’s outcome-focused culture, centered on our Values;. As a leader you can make a genuine impact.

Industry leading salaries, reviewed annually

Growth and promotion opportunities

If you are a strategic thinker, a respected industry leader and passionate about shaping the future of Australia’s built environment, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now or reach out directly for a confidential discussion.

description:
Title:

Logistics Analyst

Program Summary

KBR’s Missile, Aviation, and Ground Systems (MAGS) division delivers mission engineering solutions for critical U.S. Army programs, specializing in aviation and ground systems, integrated air and missile defense, and threat and target systems. As a trusted partner of the U.S. Department of Defense, MAGS provides innovative, technology-driven solutions to enhance national security. With a global presence and a strong ethical framework, KBR ensures secure, effective, and mission-ready capabilities worldwide.

Job Summary

KBR is a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace. The Senior Logistics Specialist position in support of KBR’s Government Services mission impacts a wide range of customer operational, project or service activities. Therefore, the position requires a person who has a strong knowledge of Logistics Best Practices and how their own area integrates with others. The person in this position must have the ability to build relationships with employees and stakeholders across all levels of an organization, must have the ability to solve complex problems, have a very high degree of initiative; and must be a dependable and highly organized team player who can communicate effectively and efficiently on all levels of an organization.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Provide Logistic and Programmatic support to Air and Missile Defense Programs.
Provide logistical analysis and technical input across multiple projects in support of the US Government Customer.
Analyzes, organizes, plans and administers various phases of day-to-day provisioning, spares, or maintenance/repair activities for one or more basic programs using established procedures.
Analyzes basic contractual documents, technical data, customer usage data, customer maintenance practices, customer operation characteristics, and related reports for assigned contracts to determine spares provisioning or maintenance/repair requirements.
Performs technical studies to refine project requirements.
Conducts research and identifies actions and logistical projects assigned to area of responsibility, coordinates assignment of all tasks, and monitors compliance and completion.
Initiates coordination between resource managers/supervisors/subordinates and ensures all necessary reviews and approvals are received.
Develops improvements to complex workflows, processes, and management practices and provides logistically sound recommendations to support programmatic decisions made by senior leadership.
Participates in Integrated Product Team Meetings, Working Groups, and Program Reviews to represent Customer’s logistics interest.
Collates information and provides written reports to Customer regarding salient meeting content.
Conducts frequent interface with senior leadership and the U.S. Government customer.
Supports completion of administrative needs, taskings, and evaluations.
Organizes and coordinates the planning and production of activities associated with assigned projects.
Serves as primary customer contact for assigned area of responsibility.

Basic Qualifications 

Requires a Bachelor's Degree
Requires 10+ years of relevant experience.
Must currently possess or have the ability to obtain a SECRET security clearance within six months of hiring.
Must be able to support the mission with up to 25 percent travel.

Preferred Qualifications

Ten or more years of experience working with or in support of the Patriot Air and Missile Defense Weapon System.
Preferred 10+ years of relevant DoD logistics-related experience.
A current SECRET security clearance at time of hiring.
Five or more years of experience with working DoD related Foreign Military Sales (FMS) projects.

KBR is seeking an Administrative Coordinator to support student management/accountability operations at SWESC/Naval Station Great Lakes.  This is a full-time, onsite role with shifts available from 4:30am-1:30pm OR 1pm-9pm.  This position provides administrative and program support in a professional office environment. The role focuses on coordination, recordkeeping, reporting, and customer service support to ensure smooth daily operations and accurate student accountability for continuous training improvement and effectiveness. The ideal candidate will collaborate with civilian, government-contract, and active-duty personnel to support communication, scheduling, and administrative processes for student management and training activities.

Perform data entry/verification in designated student accountability databases (e.g., PowerApp Learning Site database) and housing systems (e.g., EMH), as required.

Maintain and verify student records in internal data systems by reviewing rosters, identifying discrepancies, and ensuring information accuracy.
Prepare, generate, and submit routine reports related to student status, room assignments, and accountability in accordance with established timelines. Support student check-in and check-out processes by issuing and tracking keys, maintaining logs, and ensuring required documentation is completed and filed appropriately.
Monitor shared inboxes and communication channels for student requests, scheduling updates, medical and dental notifications, academic changes, and other administrative items, routing information as needed. Assist with weekly room inspection coordination by posting results, updating internal systems, and tracking follow-up actions as required.

CPR certification.
Strong organizational, communication, and customer service skills.

The Logistics Specialist serves as a critical on-site resource supporting the Surface Warfare Schools Command (SWSC) N79 Damage Control Firefighting Directorate and other SWSC directorates in the San Diego. This role is responsible for procuring essential training resources by reviewing and processing Purchase Requests (PRs), tracking funding documentation, and ensuring requests align with established supply guidelines. You will optimize resource allocation through inventory, supply, and financial analyses and provide data-driven recommendations that help sustain training execution and Fleet readiness.

Roles and Responsibilities

Provide direct logistics, supply, and financial training requirements support for SWSC N79 and the San Diego region schoolhouse/courses of instruction.
Review funding request documents, track their progress between SWSC N79 and NAVFAC, and maintain clear status visibility for stakeholders.
Plan, schedule, and coordinate supply and material flow, including inventory storage and movement from supplier to customer to meet required timelines and specifications.
Prepare, submit, process, and track procurement requests and purchases, ensuring accuracy and completeness throughout the lifecycle.
Validate Purchase Requests (PRs) for compliance with Supply Center guidelines prior to submission and follow-through.
Coordinate with internal teams to ensure customer requirements are met and logistics support aligns with training demand.

Prepare logistics support documentation and source data (e.g., logistics support plans, user support summaries, post-production support plans, and implementation plans) to support operational needs.
Implement and maintain logistics plans, databases, and support files to support fielding of new systems or major modifications; apply logistics principles to specialized solutions and lead execution within the logistics discipline.
Attend N8 departmental meetings and training as required and perform other duties that support or improve N8 Department execution in support of the N78 Directorate.

Basic Qualifications 

Must be a U.S. citizen with an active Secret Clearance (or ability to obtain and maintain).   
High School Diploma/GED and a minimum 6 years of experience in DoD logistics or supply management.
Demonstrated experience preparing, reviewing, processing, and tracking procurement requests/purchases, including ensuring PRs align with established guidelines prior to submission.
Experience planning and coordinating supply/material flow, inventory handling, and delivery coordination to meet schedule and requirements.

Experience navigating Navy supply/procurement research websites and tools (e.g., One Touch Support, FEDMALL, PIEE, GSA Advantage, IGC, etc.).
Understanding of the Government Commercial Purchase Card (GCPC) program and processes.
Familiarity with DoD governing instructions, publications, notices, messages, and memorandums.
Experience in a military or educational setting and familiarity with Surface Warfare Officers School operations or similar training institutions.

title: Senior Appian Developer - QA
description:
Title:

Senior Appian Developer - QA

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! 

Program Summary

Are you passionate about developing solutions to increase automation and innovation? KBR is a leading provider of science, technology, and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world. We leverage technology to deliver innovative solutions that meet the complex demands of our diverse clientele.

Job Summary

Written as a Paragraph (4-5 sentences)

As an Appian Tester, you will be responsible for validating the functionality, performance, and security of Appian applications. This role focuses on creating and executing test plans, identifying defects, and ensuring that applications meet business requirements and quality standards. You will work closely with developers, Business Analysts, and stakeholders to support both production releases and new development projects, ensuring seamless user experience and robust application performance.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Written as Bullet Point List (5-10 bullets)

Test Planning: Develop comprehensive test plans, test cases, and test scripts for Appian applications based on business and technical requirements.
Functional Testing: Execute manual and automated tests to validate workflows, interfaces, and integrations within Appian.
Defect Management: Identify, document, and track defects using tools such as Azure DevOps or similar platforms; collaborate with developers to ensure timely resolution.
Regression Testing: Perform regression testing for new releases and updates to ensure existing functionality remains intact.
Performance Testing: Validate application performance under various conditions and recommend optimizations where necessary.
Collaboration: Work closely with Business Analysts and developers to clarify requirements and ensure accurate test coverage. Participate in meetings with stakeholders if necessary to get clarification on flow of operations.
Documentation: Maintain detailed test documentation, including test results, defect logs, and quality metrics.

description:
Title:

Senior Test and Evaluation Engineer

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

Senior Test and Evaluation Engineer

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.

Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.

Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in successfully getting mission capability on orbit and shaping the future of space reconnaissance.

Position Description/Job Responsibilities:

KBR is seeking a Senior Test and Evaluation Engineer to work with our team to supporting the United States Space Force Space Training and Readiness Command (STARCOM) Test and Evaluation Squadrons (TES) at Schriever SFB in Colorado Springs, CO. An active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility is required.

Applicants should have experience in acquisition lifecycle and multiple phases of the test and evaluation process. Strong applicants will have experience with contractor or developmental testing, operational testing, and live-fire testing, particularly testing of space systems, and the role of modeling and simulation (M&S) and hardware-in-the-loop (HWIL) in a test campaign. Experience in evaluating both small subsystems' test results and major system program results is highly desired. In addition, applicants should have familiarity with major DoD acquisition programs as part of the Space Force acquisition process. Successful applicants should be adept at breaking complex systems into functional elements and determining test objectives applicable to each. Test Engineers/Operations Analysts must have the ability to self-teach to stay current with the best T&E and M&S tools and techniques for evaluating capabilities. Additionally, they must understand the advantages and limitations of differing techniques for solving a particular problem.

Responsibilities:

Assist in the planning, coordination, and execution of space systems tests & experiments
Design, develop, and execute advanced test/experimentation programs and processes to conduct assessment of space systems
Apply optimal scientific and statistical tools such as design of experiments to increase test efficiency and produce actionable test results
Create/review test engineering documentation to include test plans, Test Information Sheets, Safety Packages, Data Analysis. Management Plans, Technical and Safety Review Board Briefs, Test Readiness Briefs, Test Cards, and Test/Analysis Reports as required
Perform analysis on pre-test predictions, including those obtained through M&S and HWIL, to design test events and profiles, define data collection requirements, and develop go/no-go criteria to meet test objectives
Work with programs to perform reviews of systems, sub-systems, and components to ensure the data management and analysis plan (DMAP) provides proper data collection for real-time and post-mission data processing, evaluation, and analysis to meet test/experimentation objectives
Set up data analysis requests, process data, perform data quality control review and anomaly resolution, and analyze data as per the data analysis plan
Execute simulations to predict or evaluate system effectiveness or suitability under relevant operational conditions and scenarios
Monitor the gathering of M&S data and guide test result evaluation to determine if system configurations and architecture meet customer specifications and performance expectations
Create Test Reports/Presentations of complex data sets
Create/enhance data analysis tools

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s Degree preferably in Operations Research, Engineering, Math, Probability, Statistics or Science
10+ years of demonstrated Systems &/or Test Engineering experience with space, ground, operations, and sustainment segments of DoD
A SME-level understanding of test, evaluation and experimentation and the distinctions between developmental, operational, and integrated test
Comfortable with methodologies including modeling and simulation, laboratory testing, open-air testing, and live-fire testing and supporting skills such as modeling and simulation, system decomposition, design of experiments and response surface methodologies, regression testing, and validation of models and simulations
Team mentality to provide integrated engineering/analysis support for design reviews, test planning working groups, test card prep, disciplined test execution, and collaborative authorship of post flight reports
Willingness to accept changing and evolving roles & responsibilities in support of customer requirements and needs
Aptitude and patience to process and analyze complex system test/experimentation data
Technical expertise in one or more of the following areas: Space-related data communications, EO/IR/RF Sensors, Spacecraft GNC, Space system Architectures, Space Battle Management and Control, Cyber
An active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility is required

Desired Qualifications: 

Master’s Degree in Operations Research, Engineering, Math, Probability, Statistics or Science with 10+ years of demonstrated experience
Space Weapons officer (W13S/13S), with understanding of joint operations environment, and/or Offensive/Defensive space tactics &/OR graduate of specialized T&E training (e.g., USAFTPS Space Test Course)
DoD Acquisition Professional Development (ADPD) Test and Evaluation Level 3 certification
Experience within the DoD or as a Defense Contractor working in test and evaluation
Knowledge of orbital mechanics and astrodynamics
Space operations and/or orbital mechanics
Statistical techniques for approaching complex problems with large amounts of data
Application of operations research techniques and supporting skills such as database query languages, design of experiment and response surface methodologies, scripting language programming, and development of appropriate models and simulations

Work Location: Onsite at Schriever SFB, CO

The salary range for this position is approximately $155,000 -$165,000.  

The offered rate will be based on the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, abilities and/or experience and in consideration of internal parity.

title: Senior Research Scientist
description:
Title:

Senior Research Scientist

BELONG. CONNECT. GROW. with KBR.

Around here, we define the future. We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

Job Description:
 

The Intelligent Systems Research and Development Support (ISRDS) contract supports NASA Ames Research Center in developing and infusing advanced technology into NASA missions. Our scientists, engineers and technologists support research and development of critical enabling technologies for all of the NASA Mission Directorates. This KBR-led team has supported technology development for NASA space exploration missions such as LADEE, VIPER, Biosentinel, Starling and TESS, supports payload development for the International Space Station, and develops robotics and autonomous operations technologies for lunar and planetary exploration, and performs research in materials modeling (including quantum materials) and quantum computing.


KBR is looking for a Senior Research Scientist to support the Quantum Artificial Intelligence Lab (QuAIL) at NASA Ames.  This person must have a strong expertise in quantum algorithms development, quantum simulation, quantum error correction and a deep understanding of the physics behind quantum algorithms. We are looking for a candidate with at least 6 years of experience in exploring quantum computing including hardware experience and classical simulators of quantum systems.


This person will lead independent research through numerical and theoretical analysis, exploring quantum error-correction, quantum algorithms, for near-term applications on quantum devices, as well as early fault-tolerant and utility-scale architectures. This person must be skilled in both numerical and analytical evaluation of the performance of quantum and classical algorithms and architectures comparing different quantum and quantum-classical hybrid approaches with each other and with state-of-the-art classical alternatives.


This individual must have demonstrated experience leading a team of researchers in quantum computing, and in leading technical proposal efforts.

*** Must be U.S. citizen or green card holder ***

Responsibilities:

Will lead the ISRDS task in Quantum Computing
Will serve as primary interface with the Ames Quantum Artificial Intelligence laboratory (QuAIL)
Will lead research on quantum error-correction and quantum algorithms
Will lead research on fundamental quantum mechanisms and their use in quantum computation
Will supervise researchers in quantum computation
May support and lead other related tasks in quantum sciences, data sciences and AI-based technologies

REQUIRED Skills and Traits:

Ph.D. in Physics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
6+ years of experience in quantum computing
Demonstrated ability to lead small teams
Strong interest in management and leadership development
Excellent oral and written communication skills

*** Must be U.S. citizen or green card holder ***

title: Logistics Clerk
description:
Title:

Logistics Clerk

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! 

Program Summary

KBR’s Global Asset Management (GAM) group provides comprehensive manufacturing and supply chain solutions globally, serving both commercial and government clients. With a wide range of services including Government Property Management, Production Maintenance, and Equipment Tracking, GAM is dedicated to ensuring excellence in every aspect of the supply chain and asset management process. This commitment ensures the seamless operation of our clients' enterprises across diverse locations.

Job Summary

The Logistics Clerk is responsible for coordinating and expediting the movement of materials, parts, and assemblies. This role involves establishing and communicating deadlines for deliverables, as well as verifying the accuracy of incoming and outgoing shipments. The clerk maintains relevant records, stamps identification information and shipping instructions on containers, and arranges for the distribution of materials upon arrival. They inspect products for quality and quantity to ensure they meet specifications, working diligently to adhere to schedules and support customer satisfaction.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Work with relevant departments to manage and organize inventory, ensuring accurate tracking and timely replenishment of supplies.
Maintain records related to receipts, movements, and kitting of materials for consumption.
Arrange for the distribution of materials upon arrival, including processing receipts, recording inductions into SAP, notifying material inspectors, managing put-aways, and updating inventory records.
Conduct visual inspections to ensure material receipts meet approved physical standards and that accompanying paperwork is accurate and compliant with customer requirements and specifications.
Maintain records of equipment movements, ensuring accurate documentation for inventory control.
Safely operate forklifts (sit-down and reach) and other equipment to move materials and equipment within the premises.
Collaborate with team members to ensure the smooth transfer of goods, delivering them timely and accurately to designated areas.
Perform routine inspections and maintenance on equipment to ensure proper functioning.

Basic Qualifications 

High school diploma or equivalent.
Ability to lift heavy objects, both individually and as part of a team, and perform physically demanding tasks.
Must be able to obtain a forklift certification.
Basic knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
Must be a U.S. Citizen.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in shipping and receiving, safety protocols, organization, and equipment operation.
Experience with SAP.

description:
Title:

Assistant Program Manager – Test & Evaluation (T&E) 

KBR’s Mission Engineering Division delivers complex technical solutions and expert support to the U.S. Department of War, specializing in modeling and simulation, cyber transformation, air vehicle mission integration, and lifecycle support. As a trusted partner with a proven history in mission technology, KBR collaborates closely with clients to develop innovative and effective solutions. With a strong ethical framework, KBR prioritizes data security, privacy, and responsible information management to ensure mission success.

 The Assistant Program Manager – Test & Evaluation (T&E) supports the planning, coordination, execution, and reporting of developmental and operational test activities across the program lifecycle using NAVAIR procedures. In this role, you will help ensure test scope, resources, schedules, documentation, and execution align with acquisition strategy, technical requirements, and government guidance. You will collaborate closely with engineering, logistics, contractors, government stakeholders, test organizations, and end users to validate and verify system performance prior to fielding. This is an on-site position in Lexington Park, MD, with travel required, supporting mission-critical aviation programs.

Roles and Responsibilities

Assist in developing Test and Evaluation Master Plans (TEMPs), test plans, test procedures, and data collection requirements to support developmental and operational testing across the program lifecycle.
Coordinate with developmental test (DT) and operational test (OT) agencies to align overall test strategy, schedules, and execution priorities.

Coordinate test readiness reviews (TRRs), test events, and field activities, including range scheduling, instrumentation needs, test resources, and test article configuration planning.
Support on-site test execution as required and serve as a liaison with test teams to resolve issues quickly and maintain schedule and quality.
Collect, analyze, and validate test data and results; support test report development, deficiency reporting, and corrective-action tracking with traceability to requirements.

Support acquisition documentation and milestone decision activities by providing T&E inputs, schedules, and execution status to stakeholders.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, Program Management, or related field or equivalent relevant experience in lieu of a degree.

Demonstrated experience supporting developmental and/or operational testing (DT/OT), including test planning, coordination, execution support, and reporting. Prior experience supporting NAVAIR aviation programs in a T&E environment, including use of NAVAIR procedures/policy.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a STEM or management field.
DAWIA/FACP/PM certifications (T&E, Engineering, Program Management).
Experience working with integrated product teams (IPTs) and government-led test programs.
Experience with major range and test facility bases (e.g., NAVAIR, ATEC, AFOTEC, MDA, DOT&E).
Proficiency with MS Project, Jira, DOORS, or equivalent tools.

Program Summary

KBR Assurance Services (KAS) delivers full life cycle professional and technical solutions that improve operational readiness and drive innovation. KBR’s areas of expertise include engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity.

Our people make the world a more productive, efficient, and fascinating place. And that’s only the beginning.

Job Summary

In this position, you will serve as the engineer for AS9102 First-Article Inspections (FAIs). You will assign, track, and manage assignments in the Greer, SC area. You will be required to work directly with the customer and KBR to meet quality standards and schedule expectations.

Roles and Responsibilities
Reviews and conducts First Article Inspections (FAIs).
Provide onsite and remote support at Customer/Supplier sites.
Assign, track, and manage First-Article Inspection assignments of the KBR team.
Coordinate with customers to determine schedule, requirements, and specific needs for projects and inspections.
Ability to use AS9102 FAI generating software.
Provide estimates, quotes, and feedback to customers during the proposal process.
Conducts tests, inspections, audits, and validations to ensure process compliance with contract, KBR and customer requirements and specifications for design, engineering, products, equipment, maintenance, and services.
Conducts source inspections, evaluations and/or surveillance of vendors, suppliers, and subcontractors.
Knowledge and ability to use inspection tools, measuring and test equipment.
Conducts sampling inspections in accordance with approved plans and procedures.
Supports and actively participates in root-cause-analysis.
Conducts follow-up audits to review the effectiveness of implemented corrective actions.
Collects and uses statistical data for the monitoring and evaluation of trends.
Maintain and update QMS documents and quality contents as needed.
Provides training and tutoring to other engineering personnel, suppliers, and contract personnel in First-Article Inspection, Six Sigma techniques, Manufacturing Process Control, variation reduction, etc.
Provide technical leadership to coordinate implementation of advanced quality processes including statistically based variation reduction, control planning, mistake proofing, and Manufacturing Process Control.
Prepare and present metrics associated with quality trends and related improvements within the customer base.
Prepare progress reports, program reviews as needed, to assure the highest quality and cost effectiveness.
Provides activity and status reports to management.

Ability to prepare AS9102 First Article Inspections, including ballooned drawings and Forms 1, 2, and 3, and support related FAI activities such as reviews, measurements, and expediting.
