Experience conducting root cause and corrective action (RCCA) activities in collaboration with quality and manufacturing engineering.

Experience in leading teams focused on problem solving and improvements.

Good communication skills both written and oral with the ability to provide a clear vision of the strategy and processes for key stakeholders.

High level of analytical ability to identify and evaluate appropriate courses of action for definition and resolution of complex problems.

Proven track record of working closely with suppliers preferred.

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!  

KBR is a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers; but we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.  We maintain a highly qualified workforce to help care for service people and astronauts across the world.  We attract the best minds because our expertise thrives on creativity, resourcefulness, and collaboration. The Special Operations Clinical Psychologist will provide technical expertise, guidance, and direct clinical service in the area of operational psychology to special operations forces (SOF).

• May develop, plan and initiate resiliency programs for preventing and treating behavior health issues to support all aspects of a service member readiness and resiliency.

• Practice within the guidelines of their state licensing board, American Psychological Association Ethical Principles and Code of Conduct, and MTF privileges.

• Successful completion of an Internship/Residency in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association. 

• A minimum of two (2) years of experience within the past five (5) years in the independent practice of clinical work in a mental health setting. 

• Providers must be able to meet clinical competency requirements specified in the Service-specific credentialing instructions. 

• Licensure: Current, full, active, and unrestricted license to practice as a psychologist in any U.S. State, the District of Columbia, Guam, Puerto Rico or U.S. Virgin Islands. 

• Obtain practice privileges from the servicing military medical treatment facility.

title: Database Developer
description:
Title:

Database Developer

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.

Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.

Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Job Summary:

The DoD International AIMS Program Office (DoD AIMS PO) is responsible for the testing and evaluation of Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) systems, ensuring interoperability for all DoD, NATO, and coalition partner weapons systems. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) Avionics Engineering Division (AFLCMC/EZA) provides avionics systems engineering leadership and technical support to program offices to design, develop, manufacture, integrate, test, and deploy weapon systems. The KBR team provides support to DoD AIMS PO, facilitating the testing and evaluation of all IFF and Mark XIIB systems/subsystems. The KBR team is primarily located at the DoD AIMS PO at Robins Air Force Base (AFB), Georgia.  The incumbent of this position will function as an integral DoD AIMS PO Database Developer and Web Designer responsible for developing and maintaining a classified address assignment database. The incumbent will work within the development team supporting environments in cloud-based database applications (MongoDB preferred). As a Database Developer and Web Designer, you will evaluate customer requirements, address complex technical challenges in cloud-native development environments, manage the full application lifecycle from initial deployment through ongoing maintenance, and be able to define, generate, and review project requirements while providing detailed documentation. The ideal candidate will have strong experience with cloud-native database applications, including infrastructure security and management. You must be comfortable working in a dynamic, fluid environment with direct stakeholder engagement. Familiarity with DoD 5000.02 acquisition policies and processes is preferred, but not required.

Roles and Responsibilities:

Develop and maintain a cloud-native database in a classified DoD environment used for tracking and assignment measures.

Lead or support initial application deployment and infrastructure spin-up activities, including environment configuration and security hardening.

Assist the government customer in developing milestone schedules, integrating multiple development stages, performing schedule risk analysis, building projections of schedule outcomes, and developing reports or presentations.

Work within a cross-functional team to integrate development activities into achievable project milestones.

Communicate findings to management and stakeholders through briefings, written reports, and verbal presentations.

Collaborate directly with stakeholders to gather requirements and provide technical guidance.

Define, generate, and review project requirements with detailed technical documentation.

Implement and maintain database security protocols, backup procedures, and disaster recovery processes.

Work Environment:

Location: On-site

Travel Requirements: 0-20% minimum travel

Working Hours: Standard 40 hours per week.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, or related technical field. In lieu of degree, four (8) years of related professional experience is required

2+ years of backend development experience with JavaScript/Node.js

2+ years of experience with MongoDB or other NoSQL databases

Experience with SQL databases (Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, or PostgreSQL)

Possess or obtain IAT Level II certification (Security+, SSCP, CySA+, GSEC, CCNA-Security, CND, or GICSP) within 12 months of employment start date

Proficiency with Git version control

Experience with front-end technologies: React, HTML, CSS

Strong understanding of database architecture, design patterns, and optimization

Excellent communication skills with demonstrated ability to work directly with stakeholders.

Must possess a Secret security clearance or higher.

Desired Qualifications:

Experience with greenfield application deployment and initial infrastructure spin-up (standing up new applications from scratch)

Experience with Continuous Monitoring and Authorization to Operate (ATO) processes

Application security experience, including implementation of security controls, vulnerability remediation, and security best practices

Knowledge of cloud security frameworks and compliance requirements (FedRAMP, DoD IL4/IL5)

Experience with project management and collaboration tools (Trello, Jira, Confluence)

Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and DevSecOps practices

Experience with containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes)

Knowledge of API development and RESTful service design

Ready to Make a Difference?

 If you’re excited about making a significant impact in the field of space defense and working on projects that matter, we encourage you to apply and join our team at KBR. Let's shape the future together.

Provides expertise and focus for integrating Amazonas Nexus, mPower constellation, and other commercial satellite networks and leased transponders within the broader DoD SATCOM enterprise.

Experience with; DoD and Service Teleports and Gateways, allocation processes for ground, Space, and control networks, and planning tools for commercial assists.

description:
Title:

Operations Integration Department Manager (Supporting NASA at Johnson Space Center)

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!  

 

Around here, we define the future.

 

We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

KBR is seeking to identify a candidate for a Department Manager (DM) position within the Integrated Mission Operations Contract III (IMOC III) at the NASA Johnson Space Center’s Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) located in Houston, Texas.  IMOC III is the operations contract for Human Space Flight Operations and includes the support of mission preparation (Plan); crew, flight controller, instructor, and analyst training (Train); and real-time mission execution (Fly) activities related to the International Space Station (ISS), Orion, Space Launch System (SLS), Gateway, Human Lander System (HLS), EVA and Human Mobility Program (EHP), Commercial LEO Destination (CLD), and Private Astronaut Mission (PAM) operations.

The DM position primarily supports the Operations Integration Division (CO). The DM position reports directly to the Program Manager and is responsible for ensuring support of CO technical services tasked on the IMOC III including development and operations for the ISS, Artemis, Commercial Programs.  This position includes company and competition-sensitive duties related to the IMOC III  and other commercial space endeavors that requires establishing company and program strategies.

The Operations Integration DM is a second-level management position responsible with day-to-day oversight of five first level leaders and their direct reports within the department, including coordinating resource prioritization and allocation, and ensuring that the team completes its responsibilities within budget and schedule.  In addition, the candidate is responsible for handling administrative tasks associated with the department’s leadership and administrative personnel such as performance rating, merit planning, career development, technical and leadership training, disciplinary actions, etc., and other duties as assigned.

Responsibilities:

Lead, manage, and supervise five Technical Area Leads (NASA)
Develop and maintain successful professional relationships with customers, stakeholders, peers, and direct reports
Manage budget, staffing, and personnel performance to ensure all task order requirements are successfully met
Report contract budget and employee performance status to the NASA division and office management on a regular basis
Implement process improvements that benefit the program and customer
Develop and implement strategies for customer and company success

Qualifications/Skills:

Demonstrated leadership skills and the ability to effectively communicate with peers and direct reports in a very dynamic, fast-paced organization
Demonstrated ability to plan, prioritize, and coordinate tasks and resolve issues within a contractor–customer environment.
Demonstrated understanding of the FOD’s overall mission and associated Plan/Train/Fly concepts
Proven experience as a capable contributor to FOD technical tasks and the ability to support assignments associated with IMOC III task orders
Ability to tactfully handle personnel issues
Experience recruiting and interviewing
Demonstrated ability to manage manpower, priorities and customer requirements
Effective at handling multiple tasks, flexible, and responds quickly to changes
Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written
Ability to interact across organizations and all levels of personnel
Experience with the IMOC III Management Information System is desired
Position typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 15 years progressive relevant management experience.

description:
Title:

Special Operations Licensed Clinical Social Worker (75th RR, Ft. Moore, GA)

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!  

KBR is a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers; but we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.  We maintain a highly qualified workforce to help care for service people and astronauts across the world.  We attract the best minds because our expertise thrives on creativity, resourcefulness, and collaboration. That is how we supply our clients with cutting-edge solutions and services. 

 

KBR maintains a highly qualified workforce to help care for service people and astronauts.  We are looking for a Special Operations Licensed Clinical Social Worker to join the team who is responsible for integrating the physical, mental and psychological wellness of our service members and their families.    

 

This Special Operations Licensed Clinical Social Worker will function within an operational unit, as a Behavioral Health Care Provider and is responsible for the application of social work procedures and techniques, including interviewing, behavioral assessment, and evidenced-based therapies, in the evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of psychological and neuropsychological disorders using the following skills: individual, family and group psychotherapy, couple's therapy, alcohol and drug treatment evaluations.  

  

Essential Duties & Responsibilities: 

Engage all quality improvement and staff meetings, conferences  

Conduct applied research and clinical investigations in clinical/behavioral health/organizational social work.  

Consult with medical personnel, legal authorities, military commanders and school districts as required.  

Maintain accurate medical records of all patients seen and produces reports of evaluation and/or treatment.  

Participate in military specific training.  This position may include clinical supervision of unlicensed providers or trainees.  

May be required to perform some, or all, of the following activities: Participates in and successfully completes required DoD or service required training; Contact referred patients to assess treatment adherence; Use validated symptom inventories to assess current symptom severity; Assess barriers to treatment adherence and help patient problem-solve solutions to barriers; Provide patients with education regarding their mental health condition and treatment regimen; maintain patient information in a patient registry; maintain accurate and current notes in the electronic medical records of all patients contacted for review by the managing physician; Routinely staffs difficult cases with the referring provider, behavioral health consultant and/or psychiatry consultant; and Performs case management functions.  

  

Required Education/Experience/Skills/Training:  

Position requires U.S. Citizenship.  

This position requires a Secret Clearance or Top Secret Clearance, or the ability to obtain a clearance. 

Master of Social Work (M.S.W.) or equivalent (MSSW, MSSA) degree from a graduate school of social work fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE).  

Maintain a current, unrestricted clinical license to independently practice social work in any one of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, or the U.S. Virgin Islands.  

Maintain credentialing requirements in good standing at a local MTF.  

A minimum of two (2) years peer-reviewable clinical social work experience in a mental health setting. 

Demonstrate a working knowledge of professional standards and ethics regarding the delivery of clinical social work services.  

Experience in brief behavioral interventions.  

May be required to receive and maintain clinical practice privileges. 

Fluent oral and written communication skills in English.  

Experience working in a Government setting such a DOD or Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) MTF.  

Must maintain current certification in Basic Cardiac Life Support (BCLS) by the American Heart Association; must provide front and back proof of all training/certs/documentation. 

 

Standard Company Requirements:  

Must comply with Safety, Health and Environmental plan, policies and procedures.  

Must comply with the Quality Assurance plan, policies and procedures.  

Must maintain regular and acceptable attendance.  

Responsible for completing all required training.  

Perform other assignments and duties, as required.

title: LCV EUCOM Kosovo: Operations Coordinator DM
description:
Title:

LCV EUCOM Kosovo: Operations Coordinator DM

Program Summary

KBR leads the government services world contingency market by providing responsive, full-service logistics support to forces deployed around the world under the Logistics Civil Augmentation Program contract (LOGCAP). KBR’s enduring mission support of the LOGCAP program dates back to 1992 when we served as the contract’s original prime contractor. Today, we have a workforce of over 6,000 people representing 40 nationalities who perform work on the contract in 14 countries.

Job Summary

This role is responsible for managing and maintaining physical records throughout their lifecycle, including storage, rotation, destruction, and compliance with retention requirements. Key duties include tracking and documenting all record movements, preparing records for destruction using FIFO principles, coordinating shipments and transfers, and supporting audits and RFIs. The position also involves inventory management of records and equipment, assisting with scanning and box preparation, and collaborating with safety and logistics teams as needed.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Maintain project documentation files, including technical data, engineering drawings, and purchase orders.

Scan physical records and upload electronic files to shared folders.

Conduct document management audits to ensure compliance with CAYG requirements.

Assist in lifting and packing boxes of physical records into Triwalls.

Coordinate with internal stakeholders to communicate Document Management objectives, priorities, and schedules.

Collaborate with Environmental, Safety, and other functional areas for logistical functions as directed.

Develop metrics for performance measurement and analyze work processes.

Ensure departments meet turn-in deadlines and are compliant in the document management process for record holders.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Basic Qualifications (Required Education, Experience, Skills, and Certifications)

 Requires a High School Diploma or equivalent

Experience on the document management process.                

Requires at least 1 Year as a part of the Close Out Document Management

Must have a thorough understanding of Document File Plans (DFP).

Requires proficiency in Microsoft Office suite (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint).

A level of English proficiency in accordance with the position

Fluency in Albanian and possessing an unrestricted right to work and reside in Kosovo.

Preferred Qualifications (Preferred Education, Experience, Skills, and Certifications)

Experience in US Government contract closure processes.

Ability to successfully work with various levels of employees and management.

Self-directed with strong attention to detail and ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.

title: Senior Civil Engineer
description:
Title:

Senior Civil Engineer

Our Purpose

We’re here to deliver better infrastructure for a better tomorrow.

By designing smart, sustainable transport solutions, we connect people and places across Australia’s major cities, regional communities, and remote areas. Our mission is to move people more safely and efficiently through innovative rail, road, bridge, and maritime projects—always with sustainability at the forefront.

We design with care for people and the planet, creating vibrant, connected places that respect heritage, support community growth, and shape the cities of the future.

The Opportunity

As a Senior Civil Engineer, you’ll play a key role in delivering some of Victoria’s most complex and high‑profile transport infrastructure projects.

You will contribute as a Civil Lead on multidisciplinary projects—supporting technical direction, driving design development, and solving complex engineering challenges to deliver robust, practical solutions across road, rail, and major transport programs.

You’ll provide technical guidance, support junior engineers, and help manage project delivery to meet quality, safety, budget, and timeline expectations. You’ll work closely with clients and stakeholders, helping to shape design decisions and ensuring engineering outcomes align with project objectives.

This is an exciting opportunity to take on a senior technical role within projects that will define the future of Australia’s transport networks.

Who You Are

You’re an experienced Senior Civil Engineer with strong technical capability and a proven history contributing to complex civil design on major infrastructure projects. You’re comfortable working in fast‑paced environments, coordinating across disciplines, and bringing well‑reasoned engineering solutions to the table.

You understand how to collaborate effectively, support clients and teammates, and deliver integrated, high‑quality civil engineering outcomes.

You Bring:

A degree in Civil Engineering (or equivalent)
Solid experience delivering transport or civil infrastructure projects with consultants, contractors, or government agencies
Demonstrated experience contributing as a Civil Engineer on major road, rail, or transport programs
Advanced technical competency in civil engineering design tools and methodologies
Strong knowledge of relevant Australian and state transport standards, codes, and guidelines
Chartered status (CPEng) or progress toward chartership

What We Do

KBR’s Infrastructure Services team is building a smarter and more sustainable future for Australia. We deliver end‑to‑end solutions across transport, water, defence, and the built environment, partnering with clients nationwide throughout every stage of the project lifecycle.

With more than 1,200 specialists across the country, we combine global expertise with deep local knowledge. We’re digitally connected, agile, and committed to delivering social and environmental outcomes that benefit communities long into the future.

At KBR, We Value You

Our values define how we operate and how we support our people:
We Value Our People, We Deliver, We Are People of Integrity, We Empower, and We Are a Team of Teams.

As you focus on leading high‑impact engineering solutions, we ensure you have the support, flexibility, and autonomy you need to thrive. Enjoy hybrid working options, family‑friendly arrangements, and a culture built on trust, empowerment, and collaboration.

At KBR, you’ll work alongside some of the industry’s most respected experts with the support of a global organisation—and the connected, supportive feel of a local team. Here, you’re not just part of the business; you’re integral to shaping its future.

KBR values an inclusive and diverse work environment, and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply. Our hiring decisions are based on the key requirements of each role and candidates are selected based on their unique strengths and experiences.

Job Summary: KBR is seeking a highly motivated Test Engineer to support the DoD International AIMS Program Office at Robins AFB, GA. This position involves working with a high operational tempo team focused on Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) certification efforts to ensure interoperability between DoD, NATO, and partner nation weapon systems. The Test Engineer will perform various engineering tasks related to IFF certification, including data collection, technical analysis, and communication with external program offices. The role requires travel to government and commercial sites for testing and data collection.

Roles and Responsibilities:

Perform engineering tasks related to IFF certification to establish and maintain interoperability of air, land, and sea weapon systems.

Travel to government and commercial sites to witness bench, platform, and operational testing of weapon systems, collecting data points to evaluate performance against DoD technical standards and test requirements.

Conduct technical data analysis of IFF systems and prepare comprehensive system-level evaluations, including the review and interpretation of supplementary test data (e.g., antenna patterns, EMI/EMC reports, Software Version Description documents, interrogation management schemes).

Communicate with external program offices to collect required test data, coordinate test plans, evaluate test results, and determine if product design and/or integration meets DoD standards and performance expectations.

Monitor the progress of assigned projects from initiation through certification, ensuring continuous communication with all stakeholders.

Identify all failures, deviations, or discrepancies against technical standards and test requirements in a discrepancy report.

Utilize technical writing abilities to prepare final certification packages, enabling government customers to make decisions on system suitability for certification.

Monitor and manage the progress of multiple projects and continually update internal databases.

Move, lift, and carry objects weighing up to 50 lbs.

Travel out of the local area up to 25% of the calendar year if needed.

Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Location: On-site

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field and 4 years of experience in lieu of formal education 8 years of experience with IFF systems and certification process with be required

Strong technical writing and data analysis skills.

Active secret clearance

Experience working with DoD, NATO, or partner nation weapon systems.

Familiarity with DoD technical standards and test requirements.

Excellent communication and project management skills.

description:
Title:

Systems Engineering, Integration and Test (SEIT) Team Lead

Program Summary

KBR strives to create a safer, more secure and sustainable world by bringing together the best and brightest to deliver technologies and solutions that help our customers accomplish their most critical missions and objectives. Our Colorado Springs, CO Cygnet Heights office is an integration, development and sustainment facility that provides solutions for our customers with safety and quality at the forefront of our operations.

· Cutting edge projects, relevant to real world challenges

Job Summary

KBR is seeking a Systems Engineering, Integration and Test (SEIT) Team Lead to join our Electronic Warfare Systems organization in Colorado Springs, CO. In this leadership role, you will oversee a multidisciplinary team responsible for systems engineering, system integration, and end-to-end test activities supporting ground-based mobile satellite communication systems, advanced RF technologies, and software-enabled mission capabilities.

The SEIT Team Lead will guide the definition, development, integration, and verification of complex systems while ensuring engineering rigor, technical quality, and mission-focused execution. This role includes team leadership, planning and coordinating system integration events, directing verification and validation activities, and collaborating with government and industry partners. The selected candidate will work under the Technical Operations Manager while leading SEIT engineers, junior systems engineers, and interns within the Technical Operations functional area.

Roles and Responsibilities

· Lead requirements analysis, decomposition, allocation, and traceability across system and subsystem levels.

· Develop and maintain system architectures, interface definitions, and technical documentation.

· Guide users and stakeholders in formulating technical requirements and evaluating alternative approaches.

· Provide technical direction for the integration of requirements, design artifacts, and emerging technologies.

Integration & Test Leadership

· Plan, coordinate, and execute system integration, verification, and validation activities across multiple teams.

· Confirm system and component capabilities by designing and supervising test methods, test plans, procedures, and events.

· Ensure all interfaces, dependencies, and technical baselines are fully tested and verified.

· Troubleshoot technical issues during integration and test, coordinating solutions with software, hardware, and RF engineering teams.

Team Leadership & Coordination

· Lead, mentor, and grow a team of SEIT and systems engineering personnel.

· Coordinate with cross-functional teams to champion SEIT-informed processes and workflows for product development and engineering standardization across programs.

· Support Program Management with tracking requirements, technical baselines, risks, issues, and configuration management.

· Communicate effectively with customers, government stakeholders, and program personnel regarding SEIT technical considerations.

Basic Qualifications

· Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field.

· Ten (10) or more years of experience in systems engineering, system development, integration, and/or system testing.

· Experience planning and leading system integration and test efforts across multi-disciplinary teams.

· Active Top Secret clearance with eligibility for TS/SCI.

· Moderate understanding of RF engineering fundamentals, antenna design, or related discipline(s).

· Experience supporting ground-based SATCOM terminal operations and related signal generation/processing devices.

· Demonstrated ability to derive, analyze, and manage system requirements in complex programs.

· Experience supporting system integration at the enterprise or system-of-systems level.

· Experience implementing structured processes for integration, interface coordination, and verification.

· Experience with Agile development principles and collaborative engineering environments.

Preferred Qualifications

· Master’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline.

· Experience supporting DoD or federal government programs.

· Experience leading teams in systems engineering or SEIT-focused organizations.

· Hands-on experience with satellite communications, RF systems, or complex mission system architectures.

· Familiarity with MBSE tools (e.g., Cameo, Rhapsody) and digital engineering approaches.

· Experience with test automation frameworks, modeling and simulation, or system performance analysis.

description:
Title:

Space Acquisition Program Element Monitor (PEM) Support Analyst

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.

Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.

Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Key Responsibilities:

KBR is seeking highly qualified and motivated Space Acquisition Program Element Monitor (PEM) Support Analyst in support of the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Space Acquisition and Integration (SAF/SQ) in Arlington, VA. SAF/SQ has overall responsibility for Department of the Air Force (DAF) space systems acquisition and architectures oversight as well as integration of allied, civil, and commercial space capabilities into United States Space Force (USSF) architectures. These responsibilities are carried out in close collaboration with the Chief of Space Operations (CSO) and the USSF staff. SAF/SQ also serves as the Space Service Acquisition Executive (SAE) and oversees and directs the activities of the Space Rapid Capabilities Office (SpRCO), Space Systems Command (SSC), and the Space Development Agency (SDA). SAF/SQ’s guiding objectives are to (1) drive speed into space acquisitions, (2) make our space architecture more resilient, (3) integrate our space architecture with other war fighting domains, (4) drive program management discipline across our acquisitions, and (5) ensure that space and ground acquisitions are time phased to optimize operational availability. Achieving these objectives requires a workforce with broadly diverse and deep skills in system engineering, program management, architecture analysis, program planning and budgeting, and executive level communications and support.

Some of the responsibilities include:

Experience fostering stable and productive working relationships that communicate expectations and promote cooperation. 

Experience communicating effectively and concisely using a variety of styles and techniques appropriate to the audience. 

Ability to work collaboratively with personnel at all levels of the customer organization to deliver results; strong networking, interpersonal, and customer service skills are key.

Familiarity with Defense Space and National Security Space in the areas of strategy, requirements, capabilities, architectures, programs, acquisition, and operations.

Familiarity with civil, commercial, and international space capabilities.

Experience working on a headquarters staff.

Excellent organizational skills; ability to plan, track, and maintain due dates for multiple tasks and products central to the organization’s business processes.

Exemplary writing and editing skills. 

Strong attention to detail.

description:
Title:

FMS Analyst

Program Summary

KBR’s Missile, Aviation, and Ground Systems (MAGS) division delivers mission engineering solutions for critical U.S. Army programs, specializing in aviation and ground systems, integrated air and missile defense, and threat and target systems. As a trusted partner of the U.S. Department of War, MAGS provides innovative, technology-driven solutions to enhance national security. With a global presence and a strong ethical framework, KBR ensures secure, effective, and mission-ready capabilities worldwide.

Job Summary

This position provides technical analysis support for the acquisition, planning, and organizing of a Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Program for the Search, Track, Acquire, Radiate, Eliminate (STARE) Project Office within the Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires. Candidate will monitor and analyze activities throughout all phases of the program life cycle from initiation to close-out to include requirements generation, design, test, production, fielding, and operation.  Candidate will contribute information and recommendations to strategic plans, risk management strategies and reviews; prepare and complete action plans and identify trends. Candidate will conduct substantive analysis and assist in the development of the Integrated Master Schedule, Integrated Management Plan, Engineering Change Proposals, Contract Data Requirements List, Contract Work Breakdown Structure, and Prime Item Development Specifications. Candidate will conduct research into project-related issues to ensure compliance with guidelines as outlined in the Federal Acquisition Regulations and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulations.

Roles & Responsibilities

Candidate must be able to provide technical support for the Program Management FMS Case Integrator, analysis, case development, and management.

Candidate will possess the ability to collect, complete, organize, and interpret technical data and financial information relating to acquisition and development of program plans and milestones.

Candidate will oversee Program Management actions for FMS programs by analyzing, planning, coordinating, developing, directing, and reviewing program performance.

Candidate will coordinate updates for FMS program status, progress, and develop forecast reports.

Candidate will develop acquisition planning requirements for Letter of Request (LOR) for Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOA) and Price and Available (P&A). Review and development of Statement of Work, contract development and technical evaluations, briefings, and general support.

Candidate will develop and maintain tracking techniques to monitor program execution, using existing information and reporting systems like DSAMS, CISIL, and SCIP. Candidate must demonstrate the ability to research and analyze data to identify and resolve problems in a timely manner; ability to write clearly and informatively and present numerical data effectively is required. 

Candidate will prepare for and support meetings, working groups, and conferences with analysis, reports, briefings, and minutes associated with potential and current FMS programs. 

Candidate will track project milestones and deliverables and conduct project After Action Reviews to identify areas for internal improvement.

Basic Qualifications

Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen and possess (and be able to maintain) a Secret Security Clearance.

Bachelor’s degree with 5+ years’ experience in Foreign Military Sales and/or Weapons Systems Program Management and business analysis or 8+ years’ experience in lieu of a degree. 

Preferred Qualifications 

Experience in FMS acquisition and contracting is highly desired.

Master’s degree is highly desired.  

10% travel may be required to include international locations.

Title:

APS-3: Automotive Worker (Mech II)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

KBR maintains and manages Army prepositioned stocks at the Army Field Support Battalion - Charleston (AFSBn-CHS) land site and aboard ship to include all logistics and maintenance operations. The KBR APS-3 Program is managed and executed at Goose Creek in support of the Army’s power projection doctrine and resources.  The contract provides maintenance of APS-3 stocks (Class II, IIIP, IV, VII, IX) to ensure that unit sets stored aboard marine vessels are configured and maintained at optimal readiness. KBR provides limited maintenance and supply support aboard ship to ensure that equipment sets are maintained in a ready condition for emergency download and issue to operating units at the direction of the US Army. KBR also provides maintenance services and logistical support for other Army programs IAW individual scope of work contract requirements.

Job Summary

The Automotive Worker (Mech II) performs a variety of minor repairs and services to maintain motor vehicles. The Automotive Worker places and maintains decals on vehicles, checks and replaces batteries, rotates, repairs, and replaces tires, washes, polishes, and cleans interiors and exteriors of vehicles, drains, flushes, and replaces engine, transmission, and differential grease and oils, checks, cleans, calibrates, and replaces spark plugs, cleans and replaces oil and air filters. The Automotive Worker adjusts brakes, replaces windshield wipers, and similar minor parts, assists on major overhaul jobs by disassembling and cleaning parts, repairing components such as generators and water pumps, and replacing thermostats, points, electrical wiring and other items, maintains tools and equipment, and cleans work areas.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Perform a variety of minor repairs and services to maintain motor vehicles.

Place and maintain decals on vehicles

Check and replace batteries.

Rotate, repair, and replace tires.

Wash, polish, and clean interiors and exteriors of vehicles.

Drain, flush, and replace engines, transmissions, and differential grease and oils.

Check, clean, calibrate, and replace spark plugs.

Clean and replace oil and air filters.

Adjust brakes.

Replace windshield wipers, and similar minor parts.

Assist on major overhaul jobs by disassembling and cleaning parts.

Repair components such as generators and water pumps.

Replace thermostats, points, electrical wiring and other items.

Maintain tools and equipment and cleans work areas.

Use personal tools along with government furnished special tools to perform preventative maintenance and general repairs on all automotive tactical and combat equipment assigned or work loaded to the APS-03 program.

Perform field level maintenance on U.S. Military automotive equipment, including inspection, parts identification and requisition, servicing and repair in accordance with technical specifications and specified repair times.

Maintain maintenance records and documentation in accordance with government regulations and local policies.

Properly use, store, account for, and disposal of hazardous materials and waste used and generated in the performance of duties.

Comply with all federal, state, and local regulations and procedures for handling and disposal of hazardous materials.

Handle movement of materiel and assets with forklifts and dollies.

Upon notification from the government, deploy to support issuing or receipt of equipment.

At times wear personal protective equipment such as, hearing and eye protection, hard hat and steel-toed boots as well as Individual Protective Equipment (IPE) which may include but not limited to Level III plus/IV Individual Body Armor with both front and back ballistic plates, ACH helmet, clothing (undergarments, shirts and pants and/or coveralls), reflective vests/belts, sound suppression devices, etc.

description:
Title:

Diego Garcia: Electronic System Maintenance

DESCRIPTION OF JOB TASK AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Plans, organizes, coordinates, and monitors the performance of the maintenance technicians in the Maintenance Section to ensure compliance with the maintenance and material management (3M) program. 
Ensures compliance with operational procedures and technical standards.
Assigns all technical and non-technical tasks to section lead technicians as necessary to ensure optimum performances. 
Provides technical assistance and supervision to subordinate personnel.
Supervise and provide technical assistance and training to all section personnel on the operation, maintenance, testing, and troubleshooting of NCTS communications equipment.
Determine requirements for repair parts, on-hand spare parts, and other support equipment necessary for maintenance and operations, coordinate with supply tech to assure timely logistic support. 
Originate all required PMS schedules and monitor schedule compliance.
Performs frequent random inspections (Spot Checks) to ensure timely and proper completion of scheduled PMS requirements.
Maintains all records relating to PMS schedules, maintenance actions, additions, deletions, modifications of equipment, and any authorized modifications to existing Maintenance Requirement Cards (MRC) IAW OPNAVINST 4790.4 and NAVSEAINST 4790.8 series 3M Manuals and supporting NCTSFE Det Diego Garcia 3M Instruction as applicable.
Conducts a continuing review of all phases of the local preventive maintenance program (PMS) to ensure adequate accuracy of PMS coverage, administrative procedures, and 3M/PMS training.
Oversee operational Personnel Qualification Standards (PQS) and technical training; conduct annual technical performance evaluations of assigned personnel; conduct performance spot-checks; provide all required operational and maintenance reports, ensures current operational and maintenance status of equipment is within contract requirements and available for use; continually reviews and updates standard operating procedures, and provides technical assistance to all maintenance personnel in resolving complex technical or communications problems. 
Performs other duties as assigned.

 BASIC JOB QUALIFICATIONS: (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs):

Must hold an active DoD secret clearance or be able to obtain this clearance prior to deployment and must maintain such clearance for the duration of employment in this role.
Must possess administrative, organizational, and computer skills to include proficiency with Microsoft Office suite including (MS Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
Ability to work quickly and in a potentially high-stress environment.
Must have good oral and written communication skills which enable to effectively liaise with clients, other departments within the organization, subcontractors, and clients, and report directly to the Senior Management.
Must pass overseas medical screening and be in good health.

JOB SPECIFICATIONS:  SPECIAL CERTIFICATIONS OR TRAINING

Personal Qualification Standard (PQS) training for Maintenance Supervisor (3-M 304) is required within three (3) months of contract award or upon hiring. 

EDUCATION:

High school graduate or successful completion of a two (2) year resident course at a technical institute specializing in electronics or communications technology or the equivalent military training in communications electronics. 
Specialized electronic experience of more than three (3) years may be substituted for educational requirements. U.S. Navy Electronics Technician SATCOM "C" school for the AN/FSC-78/79 and AN/GSC- 52B Heavy Earth Terminal and the U.S. Navy Maintenance and Material Management (3M) System is desired, but not required.

EXPERIENCE:

Ten (10) years of general experience in communications, of which within the last four (4) years, two (2) years specialized experience directly related to Tactical Support Communications operations.

OR

Eight (8) of which have been in progressively responsible technical or craft experience in electronics, electricity, engineering, communications, physics, or in a similar field that provided technical knowledge and background that could be applied in the testing, evaluation, installation, maintenance or repair of electronic systems and equipment. 
Within the last six (6) years, four (4) years specialized experience in the theoretical and practical knowledge of electronic theory and characteristics, functions, diagnosing, isolating and correcting malfunctions, and performing organizational level maintenance on communications and electronic equipment including but not limited to: AN/GSC-52B, AN/FSC-78 SATCOM earth terminals, or equivalent, including but not limited to, High Power Amplifiers, Low Noise Amplifiers, Signal Converters. 
Measurement Switching Translation Assembly, Cryptographic equipment; Audio and DC patch panels; Receivers and transceivers; Antenna couplers and patch panels; Multiplex/de-multiplex equipment; Line amplifiers; Frequency standards; Power supplies; Order wires; Radiotelephone (R/T) communications equipment; Defense Information Infrastructure (DII) Communications Channel Server System (DCCS), Signal converters; Ultra-High Frequency (UHF) and High Frequency (HF) voice and data communication ancillary equipment and devices, and all ancillary equipment and test equipment.

Job Posting Description

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.

Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.

Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

KBR is seeking a Modeling And Simulation Engineer with in-depth knowledge of satellite relevancy to Department of War and the Intelligence Community unique missions to be part of our team supporting our customer in Chantilly, VA that delivers mission-critical capabilities directly supporting intelligence-gathering missions from overhead systems.  We lead architectural assessments and report recommendations to senior US Government personnel guiding acquisition and execution of next-generation SIGINT systems needs for the next 10-20 years.  These systems deliver collected data distributed to US Government Intelligence Community and Military users.

The Modeling And Simulation Engineer serves as a technical advisor to support the Government with performing analysis on complex space systems needs for the intelligence and DoD communities.  The SIGINT leadership team embraces innovation in a relentless effort to meet intelligence needs and shorten the timelines to provide actionable critical information to US Government decision-makers.  This is a position of trust advising the US Government and supporting critical missions in SIGINT, COMINT, FISINT, and ELINT. 

Key Responsibilities:

Supports mission analysis assessments and studies for the Program Office

Coordinates assessments HIVE architecture impacts, architecture trades, and architecture performance assessments with the Enterprise, Chief Architect, Chief Engineer, and Program Office

Manages development, test, and validation of systems assessment methodologies and tools such as STK, SOAP, MATLAB, and potentially organically developed software

Analysis of space systems, performance metrics, timelines, and models

Support orbital analysis, including threats assessments/impacts, trades, and analyses

Communicate technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences

Interface with customers, directorate/office representatives, and across system engineering groups to drive resolution plans and strategies for complex technical challenges

Generate and maintain technical documentation and reports

Work Environment:

Location: On-site

Travel Requirements: Up to 10%

Working Hours: Core hour support required

Qualifications:

Required:

Active TS/SCI with polygraph clearance

Bachelor's degree (Master's degree preferred)

5+ years of Customer experience

Detailed understanding of government satellite systems

Insight into SIGINT mission fundamentals, and ability to perform analysis on complex space systems

Knowledge of satellite relevancy to Department of War and the Intelligence Community unique missions

Solid understanding of Signals Intelligence satellite systems and architectures

Experience in Matlab, Python or similar

Understanding of operational environment and corresponding mission user needs

Knowledge of system engineering

Desired:

Advanced degree in STEM (science, technical, engineering, math) or related discipline.

location:
locations

description:
Title:

DG BOSS: Fire Crew Chief (FN)

Program Summary:

KBR provides integrated Base Operations Support (BOS) services to the Commanding Officer, Navy Support Facility Diego Garcia (NSF DG), supporting its mission as a forward logistics base in the British Indian Ocean Territory (BIOT). Through this comprehensive support, KBR ensures continuous operations, enhances quality of life, and enables mission readiness for NSF Diego Garcia and its tenant commands, directly supporting U.S. Indo-Pacific Command objectives in this strategically vital location.

Job Summary:

Responsible for the supervision of an assigned aircraft or structural firefighting crew on an alternating shift, supervising all assigned crew members in fire ground situations as well as the performance of care and maintenance of apparatus and equipment as defined in the current task order, Performance Work Standard (PWS), and as directed. Responsible for implementing and maintaining all fire protection services-related functional standards within their assigned department IAW the Statement of Work. Implements the Fire Chief’s comprehensive firefighting program at the assigned installation to ensure compliance with NFPA 1201 and staffed and equipped to meet the fire and emergency standards as outlined in OPNAVINST series 11320.23. tComply with accepted industry safety standards, applicable safety precautions, and guidelines listed in NFPA 1500 and local safety instructions.

Roles and Responsibilities: 

Reports to the Assistant Chief of Operations and functions under their direct supervision.

Supervises a shift and crew for response readiness.

Supervises a structural and/or aircraft firefighting crew at the assigned fire department to ensure compliance with PWS and that all local requirements are met.

Assigns directs and reviews the work of assigned subordinate employees who assist in carrying out program activities.

Ensure timely submittal of CRPL, deliverables, and work product reports about the operations section as required.

Ensure the scheduling of required fire protection equipment inspections to comply with and meet PWS requirements for the department.

Prevents loss of life and minimizes damage to property and the environment from fire by directing fire attack, confinement, salvage, overhaul, ventilation, and rescue activities, including performing emergency medical care and CPR.

Protects and preserves evidence at a fire scene and may participate in the investigation of fire incidents.

Assures that procedures are affected; station logs and other records pertinent to reports, activities, drills, equipment inspections, etc., are maintained properly and submitted within time limits if required.

Maintains current knowledge of the base, its structures, and all systems related to fire protection.

Ensures related firefighting duties are accomplished and documented as outlined in the PWS and department work instructions.

When aircraft/facility pre-fire plans are outdated, develop, and provide updates.

Performs required operators' maintenance and tests on rescue tools and saws, ground ladders, fire hoses, ropes, harnesses, and hardware; serviceable inspections of firefighters’ protective firefighting clothing; and enforces mandated standards for a respiratory protection program for self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA).

Participates in career and proficiency training programs designed to increase the technical proficiency of firefighters.

Provide and conducts scheduled training as prescribed by the Fire Chief’s Annual Training Plan and as scheduled by the Assistant Fire Chief.

When first to arrive on the scene, serves as the incident commander of a fire/crash scene until relieved by the Assistant Fire Chief.

Determines the best course of action to minimize loss or damage from fires or explosions.

Directs the placement of firefighting equipment and personnel to ensure maximum utilization in fire control of aircraft crash/rescue operations.

Assesses the fire scene/emergency to facilitate fire/rescue operations and to brief the Assistant Fire Chief upon arrival.

Leads and directs assigned firefighting crew to provide safe and proper rescue operations for endangered persons.

Ensures rescue operations are performed IAW established policies and procedures and minimized the risk of additional danger to firefighting personnel and endangered persons.

Employs firefighting measures to minimize the loss or damage as a result of fire or explosions.

Responds to hazardous material incidents; leads operations level actions, as directed by the

Assistant Fire Chief, to establish control of the affected area with minimal risk to the response.

As required and/or assigned, oversees fire alarm communication center operations to ensure all firefighting equipment and personnel are dispatched as required.

Oversees the checkout of communications equipment at the beginning of the shift.

As necessary, details additional personnel in case of short staffing.

Maintains constant contact with the communications center during real-world emergencies or fire drills.

Ensures the maintenance of reference materials such as the NFPA Standards, and Lesson Plans, and reviews and provides input to work instructions about the operations, training, and communications sections of the department.

Performs mid-level supervisory personnel management responsibilities.

Advises and provides counsel to employees regarding policies, procedures, and directives of management. Explains performance expectations to employees and provide regular feedback on strengths and weaknesses.

Holds employees responsible for satisfactory completion of work assignments.

Appraises subordinate workers’ performance ensuring consistency and equity in rating technique.

Performs other duties and assignments as required or as directed by the Assistant Fire Chief or Fire Chief.

Basic Qualifications (Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs):

Knowledge of fire protection mission and organization; fire safety requirements and objectives; firefighting and rescue procedures and techniques, firefighter training requirements, firefighting apparatus and equipment, alarm, and suppression system operation; water supply

Requires excellent organizational skills; with the ability to work under fast-paced and adverse conditions.

Possess the ability to demonstrate firefighter knowledge and skills professionally.

Ability to work effectively with fellow employees and management personnel at all levels including multinational staff, and military officials.

Strong ability to exercise professional discretion and good judgment and to understand the effect of decisions made.

Exhibit strong interpersonal skills and ability to communicate in English both verbally and in writing and must have good computer skills in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and Outlook.

Must pass overseas medical screening and be in good health.

Ability to obtain and maintain a valid Government Motor Vehicle Operator’s License and Country of Origin Vehicle Operator’s License.

Must be CAC eligible and/or able to obtain a Common Access Card (CAC)

Must be able to pass the annual firefighter Occupations Health Exam and SCBA Fit Testing IAW NFPA 1500, 1582, and 1583 including but not limited to the physical strength and ability to perform heavy and strenuous tasks for extended periods under dangerous and uncomfortable conditions, often while wearing bulky protective gear, including self-contained breathing apparatus.

DG BOSS: Painter/Chipper (FN)

Provides preservation services including but not limited to painting and cleaning services to the prepositioned ships in Diego Garcia.
Performs exterior painting of surfaces that have been hydro blasted to include priming and necessary cleanup of all trash, paint spills, and debris generated.

DG BOSS: Sheet Metal Worker

Under the supervision of the Superintendent/Site Supervisor, the position is responsible for leading a group of   Sheet metal workers in the maintenance and repair of facilities Metalwork systems.
Sheet metal workers fabricate or install products that are made from thin metal sheets, such as ducts used in heating and air conditioning systems.
Utilize and interpret blueprints to determine how and where to fabricate, assemble and install sheet metal products.
Measure, mark dimensions and lay out material to be installed using tools such as scribes, rulers, calculators and squares.

Install assemblies, including pipes, HVAC ducts, flashings, rain gutters and furnace casings in supportive frameworks.
Ensure that efficiency is maximized while fabricating and installing HVAC systems.
Perform routine and unplanned maintenance on roofing and cladding and on the ducting and piping of air conditioning systems, carrying out repair work using hammers, drills, welding equipment and other tools.

Ensure safety is a priority on the job during all activities, including using tools and installing and fabricating metal.
Clean work area and restock supplies and materials as necessary.
Completes records, maintains tools and equipment, and performs various clean-up and housekeeping activities.

Job Title 

Supervisor, Accounting

Summary Section  

The Statutory Audit Coordinator will be responsible for managing the end-to-end statutory audit process, ensuring timely and accurate financial statement preparation, and coordinating effectively with external auditors and internal stakeholders. This role is critical to maintaining compliance with regulatory requirements and meeting audit deadlines.

Responsibilities:  
Prepare and review financial statements in accordance with applicable accounting standards and statutory requirements.

Coordinate with external auditors to provide necessary documentation and clarifications.
Liaise with internal teams (tax, treasury, operations) to gather required information for audit purposes.
Ensure all audit schedules, reconciliations, and supporting documents are accurate and complete.
Monitor audit progress and proactively address issues to ensure completion on or before the due date.
Maintain compliance with local laws, regulations, and company policies.
Assist in implementing recommendations from audit findings to improve processes.
Prepare the tax audit schedule and coordinate with external auditors to complete the review on or before the due date.
Complete annual tax filing accurately and within statutory timelines.
Prepare transfer pricing documentation, review with auditors, and ensure timely TP filing.
Prepare advance tax workings, coordinate with tax consultants for review, and ensure timely deposit of advance tax.

Qualifications including Required Education, Experience, & Skills:

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field and CA.
7–10 years of experience in statutory audit or financial reporting.
Strong knowledge of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and Companies Act requirements.
Proficiency in MS Excel and ERP systems MSD, SAP
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working with Big 4 or large audit firms.
Ability to manage multiple priorities under tight deadlines.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Timely Completion of Audit – 100% statutory audits completed on or before regulatory due dates. Accuracy of Financial Statements – Zero material misstatements or audit qualifications. The successful candidate will utilize their expertise in developing and analyzing systems and cybersecurity engineering artifacts used to support the integration of advanced avionics systems and subsystems at the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) C-130 Program Office at Robins Air Force Base. Conduct analysis on components that comprise integrated weapons systems such as data environments, software, data, and hardware to identify the cybersecurity requirements and risks
Analyze and identify component and subsystem vulnerabilities and risks to determine potential solutions and safeguards including system survivability and interoperability
Analyze systems to ensure cybersecurity controls, risk mitigations, and testing are in compliance as they relate to RMF

Travel Requirements: Minimal 
Working Hours: Standard

Bachelor's degree and minimum of 5-7 years of Information Systems Security experience.  In lieu of the degree an additional eight (8) years related professional experience is required.
DoD 8570.01-M IAM Level I certification is required
Experience in:

  Weapon system/airborne platform software, avionics or networking desired

C-130 or other similar fixed wing or military aircraft experience

Program Summary

KBR’s Missile, Aviation, and Ground Systems (MAGS) division delivers mission engineering solutions for critical U.S. Army programs, specializing in aviation and ground systems, integrated air and missile defense, and threat and target systems. As a trusted partner of the U.S. Department of War, MAGS provides innovative, technology-driven solutions to enhance national security. With a global presence and a strong ethical framework, KBR ensures secure, effective, and mission-ready capabilities worldwide.

Job Summary

Are you ready to embark on a journey where your expertise meets meaningful impact? As a Senior Software Architect, you'll dive into modular software design and architecture for Mission needs across multiple customers in the Department of War. Join our team in Huntsville and be at the forefront of Open Systems Architectures, contributing directly to our success story. You'll collaborate closely with a diverse team, fostering innovation and excellence every step of the way. If you're ready to make a difference and thrive in a dynamic environment, apply now and let's shape the future together

Roles and Responsibilities:

Candidate will be responsible for the planning, development and execution of Software Aspects of an Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) System to achieve successful integration with an existing Aviation Platform.
Candidate will engage with DoW clients to include Army Aviation, NAVAIR and Air Force as well as sub-tier suppliers to ensure that the software solution is architected in accordance with the Modular Open System Approach (MOSA) principles
Candidate will contribute to an overall Modular Mission Software Strategy to speed Technology Upgrades and Capability insertion to various platforms.

Basic Qualifications:

Us Citizenship and Security Clearance
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Computer Engineering or Computer Science,
10+ years direct and relevant experience with RTCA/DO-178 processes including experience with Real Time Operating Systems for Safety Critical Design Assurance Level Software.

Title:

Senior Advisor - Integrated Fires

Program Summary

KBR’s Missile, Aviation, and Ground Systems (MAGS) division delivers mission engineering solutions for critical U.S. Army programs, specializing in aviation and ground systems, integrated air and missile defense, and threat and target systems. As a trusted partner of the U.S. Department of War, MAGS provides innovative, technology-driven solutions to enhance national security. With a global presence and a strong ethical framework, KBR ensures secure, effective, and mission-ready capabilities worldwide.

Job Summary

The candidate will serve as a Senior Advisor supporting Army Integrated, Defensive, and Offensive Fires weapon system portfolios, and OSD equities. This role spans the full acquisition lifecycle, integrating engineering, program control, testing, fielding, training, deployment and logistics. The candidate will play a critical role in coordinating multi-disciplinary efforts essential to major defense acquisition programs, as well as other-than-major systems and subsystems. The candidate will help to ensure that acquisition decisions are driven by operational needs, reducing delays, and creating tighter alignment between requirements and delivered capabilities. Key stakeholders will include the Joint and Army Staffs, OSD, HQDA DAMO-Fires, Space and Missile Defense Command (SMDC), Missile Defense Agency (MDA), Fires Center of Excellence (FCoE), Army Transformation and Training Command, Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires, and Army Air and Missile Defense Commands (AAMDCs).

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Acquisition Execution:
Lead development and implementation of acquisition strategies that align with customer overarching capability delivery goals. Candidate will serve as a KBR Senior Adviser for strategic acquisition pursuits for Army Fires, Integrated Air and Missile Defense, MDA, SMDC, Army Transformation & Training, and appropriate subordinate commands and elements.  Candidate will develop strategic visions and plans and set objectives for new and existing government customers.  Candidate will work with Senior Leaders to develop and implement strategic and tactical action plans in support of combat developments, materiel development, HQDA integration, and modernization initiatives. 

Program Integration & Oversight:
Support cross-functional integration of program elements—operational, technical, and logistical—to enable effective acquisition and sustainment of Fires systems. Work with stakeholders to ensure that Army Fires programs are no longer “system-centric” but capability-centric, with the warfighter’s operational requirements driving decisions.

Stakeholder Engagement & Governance:

Collaborate with stakeholders to align acquisition with operational concepts to enable faster and more accurate translation of warfighter needs into delivered systems. Key stakeholders will include Joint and Army Staffs, OSD, HQDA DAMO-Fires, SMDC, MDA, FCoE, Army Transformation and Training Command, PAE Fires, and AAMDCs to better posture the Army to deliver capabilities our Soldiers need without delay. These engagements will help to ensure the warfighter’s voice is central for acquisition, fielding and ensuring responsive adaptation of programs to real-world needs.

Strategic Growth & Business Development:
Serve as a KBR Senior Advisor for Integrated Fires pursuits with Army PAE Fires, MDA, SMDC, OSD and AAMDC business pursuits. Shape strategic direction, engage with new and existing government customers, and support solution development aligned to Army modernization priorities. Candidate will also serve as a liaison with other peers on KBR cross-business unit opportunities.

Leadership Development & Mentorship:
Contribute to the KBR Leadership Program through development and deployment of training, mentoring, and enrichment activities designed to develop future leaders and improve retention and engagement.

Basic Qualifications:

Clearance: Active Top Secret security clearance
Education: Master’s degree preferred, bachelor’s degree required
Experience: 25+ years of experience supporting Warfighter mission and requirements (e.g. Air and Missile Defense / Fires, Army, MDA, SMDC, and/or OSD systems)

Preferred Qualifications:

Proven success integrating programs and providing acquisition support for PAE Fires, SMDC and MDA related organizations
Deep familiarity and established relationships with Army Staff, Fires Center of Excellence, AAMDCs and key acquisition offices
Hands-on experience with Foreign Military Sales (FMS) execution
Strong leadership in planning, executing, and managing large-scale DoD programs
Excellent briefing and communication skills, with experience delivering content to senior Army, SMDC and MDA leadership
Demonstrated ability to operate in high-tempo environments with competing priorities and diverse stakeholders

Huntsville, AL (Government Site or Contractor Site) with periodic travel to Washington, D.C.; El Paso, TX and other CONUS locations as required.

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Position Summary:

KBR National Security Solutions is seeking a motivated and talented Senior Radar Payload Systems Engineer to join our team in Chantilly, Virginia. The selected candidate for this position will contribute to the design, development, implementation, integration, testing and delivery of radar hardware, software, and systems solutions for Government contracts.

Responsibilities

Radar Hardware Development: Define and document the RF front-end electronics and architecture of an advanced space-based SAR radar system, including the antenna arrays, receivers, and digital electronics.
Engineering Tasks: Perform engineering tasks to develop systems capable of meeting operational requirements within imposed constraints.
Acquisition Modeling Support: Perform rigorous link-budget modeling and analysis and conduct trade studies for hardware components to ensure mission success.
Algorithm Development. Support algorithm and analytical development using a variety of scientific programming languages (e.g., Python, MATLAB, etc.) to process synthetic aperture radar data (SAR) and Moving Target Indicator (MTI).
Test Data Assessments: Analyze and assess integration and test data at the component, subsystem, payload, and space vehicle segments to identify and resolve issues with hardware design and manufacturing.
V&V Processes: Assess the verification and validation of system vendor testing at all levels to ensure the radar system meets its requirements.
Vendor Performance Monitoring: Monitor the system provider’s performance in designing, documenting, and verifying all interfaces within the system.
Functional Analyses: Perform functional analyses to ensure systems meet performance criteria.
Operations and Procedures: Formulate, recommend, and direct operations and procedures to resolve engineering and/or technical problems.
Conduct Studies: Conduct special studies and investigations related to projects.
Technical Assistance: Provide technical assistance and instruction related to design problems.
Project Requirements Analysis: Analyze project requirements and provide information and instruction for designing, operating, maintaining, and modifying systems.
Solutions Integration: Ensure that solutions can be integrated into viable, complete systems.
General: Perform all other duties as assigned.

Work Environment

Location: On-Site
Travel Requirements: Moderate (20% to 50%) travel to contractor facilities, test sites, or launch locations.
Working Hours: Flexible. Standard Government work hour support and surge support during integration and launch phases.

Required Qualifications:

Clearance: Active TS/SCI clearance (with current polygraph).
Education: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, applied physics, or a related STEM technical discipline. Specific contract requirements regarding education and experience will prevail.
Relevant Radar Hardware Experience: Demonstrated 8+ years of experience supporting radar space system hardware development, integration, and test.
Remote Sensing Knowledge: Knowledge of remote sensing technologies including active and passive sensor systems which operate in the RF regime, and the concepts, signal and image processing algorithms and software architectures that enable these systems.
Prototyping Experience: Engineering software (prototyping) experience in MATLAB and/or Python.
Established Client Relationship Skills: Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain trusted client relationships.

description:
Title:

Sr. Security Specialist - SSO

Program Summary:

KBR’s Product and Technology Solutions Division specializes in rapid prototyping and advanced technology solutions for directed energy, electronic warfare, and security applications. With expertise in electronic warfare systems, critical infrastructure protection, and product R&D, KBR delivers cutting-edge innovations to meet mission-critical needs. Backed by a global presence and a strong ethical framework, KBR collaborates closely with customers to develop secure, effective, and forward-thinking solutions.

Job Summary:

KBR is seeking to hire a Sr. Security Specialist to support a US Government customer located at the Naval Research Laboratory (NRL) located in Washington, DC. Typical security related responsibilities may include enforcing and monitoring security procedures; ensures compliance with all aspects of the government and company security policies and procedures related to: physical access to buildings, room, couriers, clearances, packages, documentation and debriefings. May develop and implement security procedures in coordination with management personnel. May conduct security briefings and maintain security education programs. Investigates losses and security violations; may recommend corrective action. Maintains liaison with outside agencies and keeps upper management informed of all security activities. Ensures destruction of classified and company proprietary information in accordance with policies and procedures. Assists in revision of procedures manuals.

 

Roles and Responsibilities:

- Experience primarily in physical security for SCI

Generating Construction Security Plans (CSP), including reviewing design files for new and existing SCIF construction
Fixed Facility Checklist (FFC)
SCIF TEMPEST Checklist
Compartmented Area (CA) Checklist - Including general knowledge of SAP and SAP security policy
Co-Use Agreements (CUA) and Memorandums of Understanding (MOU)
SCIF Co-Use Requests
Completing annual SCIF inspections
Intrusion Detection Systems (alarm systems) and access lists - Including alarm testing procedures and alarm response drills with security forces

- Experience using DISS

Sending and receiving Visit Requests (or via email, fax with memo, etc.)
Confirmation of clearances (including Scattered Castles)
Foreign travel notifications

- Use of other IT systems and database applications

M3 messaging system
Scanning documents (unclassified and classified networks)
DoD Safe – for sending/receiving unclassified encrypted emails/files
DOTS Web Transfer Portal and Intelink Secure Access File Exchange – for moving files up to higher classified networks

- Filing/maintaining SCIF records

- Reviewing and approving equipment requests

- Submitting Medical device requests for approval by SSO Navy

- Reading and following / interpreting policy and guidance: IC Tech Spec – for ICD/ICS 705, DoDM 5105.21, Vols. 1-3, DoDM 5200.01, Vol. 1, and DoDM 5205.07, Vols 1-4

- Create step by step guidance / standard operating procedures

- Create training slides and give training briefs to SCIF custodians

- Create and manage a task schedule

- Communicate to SSO Navy on behalf of NRL SSO

- Coordinating and scheduling meetings (including VTC and Microsoft Teams) and sending out e-mail invites / notifications

- Create designation letters

 

Basic Qualifications:

Requires a college or university degree. Minimum 4-6 years of relevant experience (mid-level). In lieu of degree, an additional 8 years of relevant experience is acceptable.
Experience with ICD/ICS 705
Experience primarily in physical security for SCI
Experience using DISS.
US Citizen. Top-Secret / SCI clearance (or SCI eligibility) Required.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

- Customer service mentality. Good communication skills (oral and writing), including clearly informing SCIF custodians and customers of Department of Defense (DoD), Department of Navy (DoN), and NRL security requirements.

- Very good organizational skills

- JWICS e-mail and familiarity with DIA Security, SSO Navy, M3, Scattered Castles, and other JWICS websites

- Pro-active tactical and strategic thinker and problem solver

- Willing to learn other SCI related security functions:

Personnel security – SCI pre-screening, nomination packages, reporting security infractions/violations, etc.
Information security – proper labeling of media, packaging classified materials for mailing, security classification guides (SCG), etc.
Cyber security – reviewing file transfers to other networks

Additionally, the candidate shall support the group’s overall sales effort through proposal/tender preparation, contract negotiation, and other client interfacing activities.
