Lead cybersecurity and AI/ML consulting engagements for defense, intelligence, and critical infrastructure clients

Assess vulnerabilities in AI-enabled defense platforms, autonomous systems, and mission-critical networks

Advise on secure system architecture and threat modeling for national security applications

Support developments in AI governance, cyber resilience strategies, and compliance with industry recognised standards

Integrate AI security frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 23894) into system design and operational workflows

Evaluate risks in neural networks, deep learning, and reinforcement learning models used in sensitive environments

Provide technical guidance on secure deployment of AI platforms in hybrid cloud, edge, and embedded environments

Ability to conduct technical due diligence for M&A, infrastructure and energy transition type projects an advantage

Deliver bespoke consulting solutions by coordinating with cross-functional teams across cybersecurity, engineering, and data science

Lead and mentor technical teams in high-stakes, interdisciplinary environments

Drive project execution and ensure delivery of secure, scalable, and mission-aligned solutions

Deep understanding of AI/ML technologies, including neural networks, deep learning, and reinforcement learning.

Strong knowledge of software development, system architecture, and network architecture.

Passionate about cybersecurity and AI, with a curious, hands-on mindset and eagerness to explore vulnerabilities across diverse technologies.

Proven track record in leading and mentoring technical teams and working in cross-functional, interdisciplinary environments.

Excellent analytical, conceptualization, and problem-solving skills.

Strong communication and interpersonal abilities, capable of translating complex technical concepts for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Well-versed in security principles, policies, industry standards, and best practices.

title: Research Psychologist
description:
Title:

Research Psychologist

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers and dreamers and we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

Around here, we define the future.

On the Human Health and Performance Contract we are at the forefront of safeguarding astronaut health, ensuring human performance, and advancing technologies for human space exploration. We are seeking a Research Psychologist at the NASA Johnson Space Center (JSC) in Houston, TX.

What You’ll Do: 

In this role, you will be a key scientist for helping NASA achieve its goals for human spaceflight exploration. You will perform this work in the Behavioral Health & Performance (BHP) Laboratory at NASA’s Johnson Space Center. The Research Psychologist will facilitate ongoing studies; write proposals for directed studies and grant solicitations; and complete data analyses and prepare reports, journal articles, and presentations regarding the study results. You will assist in the management and execution of multiple BHP Lab tasks to ensure the team produces high quality, implementable, and timely deliverables that help to reduce the risks associated with the behavioral health and performance of astronauts. You will work on a highly collaborative team, interfacing routinely with our NASA customer, laboratories in the Biomedical Research and Environmental Sciences Division, external PI teams, and provide timely deliverables to stakeholders for BHP Lab products such as Human Research Program, Space Medicine Division, Extravehicular Activity and Human Surface Mobility Program (EHP), and Mars Campaign Office.

You will:

Work with the NASA BHP Lab Lead to implement research activities related to behavioral health and performance risks
Develop grant proposals in response to research calls from NASA or external funding organizations
Develop directed research proposals and support directed research in space flight analogs, available flight opportunities, and with medical and mission operations personnel
Conduct and coordinate data collection, cleaning, and organization
Analyze and interpret research and operational data, consulting with NASA statisticians for complex issues
Draft interim and final reports, literature reviews and summaries, and project summaries
Provide subject matter expertise for research design, methodologies, technologies, and assessments related to behavioral health and performance
Disseminate research findings through presentation to NASA program management, presentations at various national and international meetings and working groups, scientific conferences and publishing in peer-reviewed journals
Participate in presenting project updates, interim and final results, as well as program objectives and direction to scientists, engineers and managers
Collaborate with a variety of contributors and stakeholders including BHP Operations personnel, flight surgeons, mission managers and a multidisciplinary team of personnel to effectively plan and execute the research plans
Monitor multiple research project schedules, deliverables, and discuss status of projects with lab project manager
Provide inputs to weekly and monthly status reports for NASA technical monitor review
Assist NASA technical monitors with updates to NASA standards, and periodic review and update of human spaceflight risks especially relates to behavioral health and performance
Advise and assist in the development of protocols and processes that promote efficient and effective management of the BHP Laboratory projects and personnel.
Maintain data quality practices and standards established within the laboratory
Liaise with internal and external collaborators to effectively plan, track, and complete collaborative research
Assist the BHP Laboratory Lead with other duties as assigned to ensure the efficient operation of the lab, or due to NASA’s program requirements changes

What You Bring:

You bring experience leading research design and execution to help answer applied human spaceflight questions.  You use your experience and judgment to develop innovative solutions to problems that will inform NASA’s future spaceflight mission planning and preparation. As a key part of our safety culture, you will comply with KBR’s Safety, Health and Environmental Plan, Quality Plan, and all safety policies and procedures, and complete all assigned training.

Your Qualifications:

REQUIRED:

Ph.D. and at least 3 years of experience in one of the following areas of psychology: Neuropsychology, Clinical, I/O Psychology, Space Psychology, Physiological, Health Psychology, Behavioral Medicine
Experience conducting behavioral health and performance research, conducting literature reviews, and collecting and analyzing behavioral health and performance data

DESIRED:

Prior experience in managing, coordinating, and directing research projects.
Prior experience with NASA, Aerospace, Military, or operational environments

Your Skills:

REQUIRED:

Proficient with software tools used by the lab including MS Office, R, and RMarkdown
Proven ability to apply research methodology for evaluating proposals and research design
Demonstrated technical and scientific writing ability, completing all levels of writing, such as research reports and summaries, briefings, technical reports, and project plans, etc.
Possess broad understanding of behavioral health and performance outcomes required for individuals required to function effectively in an isolated, confined environment during long-duration exploration missions (e.g., performance, cognition, mood)
Highly ethical and respectful of human research data confidentiality, protections, and intellectual property
Demonstrated excellence in effective communication and presentation skills with varied audiences, including various levels of management, internationals, scientists, medical professionals and engineers
Demonstrated organizational skills for coordinating complex activities and schedules, and managing tasks per a defined timeline
Successful project management experience
Ability to be flexible and adapt quickly to changing requirements
Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary setting where there is frequently divergent or competing goals for the project implementation and outcome
Demonstrated ability to interpret requirements for real-time implementation
Demonstrated interpersonal effectiveness and professionalism in working with others in a collaborative, team-oriented environment.

DESIRED:

Demonstrated ability to evaluate proven or developing technologies for measuring and assessing behavioral health outcomes as well as evaluating and applying countermeasures in a spaceflight environment.

What to Expect

This position is expected to be 100% on site and a minimum of 60% in person. Occasional travel may be required.

Explore Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) approaches for defense applications

Title:

APS-3: Specialist, Logistics Administration

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

KBR maintains and manages Army prepositioned stocks at the Army Field Support Battalion - Charleston (AFSBn-CHS) to include all logistics and maintenance operations. The KBR APS-3 Program is managed and executed at Goose Creek in support of the Army’s power projection doctrine and resources.  The contract provides maintenance of APS-3 stocks (Class II, IIIP, IV, VII, IX) to ensure that the land-based unit sets stored are configured and maintained at optimal readiness. KBR provides limited maintenance and supply support to ensure that equipment sets are maintained in a ready condition for emergency issues to operating units at the direction of the US Army. KBR also provides maintenance services and logistical support for other Army programs IAW individual scope of work contract requirements.

Job Summary

KBR executes a contract for the US Army to provide Maintenance and Logistics services for the Army’s War Stock set #3 (APS-3) at the Army Field Support Battalion - Charleston, located on Joint Base Charleston Naval Weapons Station.  The Maintenance Department consists of 180-210 employees in nine maintenance shops across 12 facilities and provides Field Level Maintenance on the full spectrum of combat and tactical equipment assigned to the program.

The Maintenance Technical Analyst serves as the contractors MTR (Maintenance Technical Representative) who receive assignments or technical direction from the Maintenance Manager and abides with guidance provided by the U.S. Army / local government sources.  This person performs in-depth research and analysis of workload requirements to assist with forecasting and planning of warranty, safety message, and modification work order parts and other compliance needs.  This person will periodically observe and critique maintenance activities and associated documentation for verification of compliance with the application of provided procedures to ensure proper, accurate, and consistent data reporting.  This person vigorously enforces the standards for validation of disposition turn-in documents, and using applicable forms, prepares deviation and waiver submissions to be presented to the customer as required.  This person will coordinate and schedule maintenance actions with external contractors to facilitate warranty repairs as required.

The Maintenance Technical Analyst is the curator for all technical information and administrative publications relating to maintenance support requirements not readily available through the Technical Librarian.  This person standardizes cataloging of reports, manuals, and related technical material concerned with work methods, procedures, installation, operation, and maintenance of equipment.  This person will actively monitor relevant publication sites and is responsible for providing timely notification of changes in technical direction.

Additionally, this individual will participate in drafting materials regarding recommended improvements of work methods and procedures.

Technical Research – Access and utilization of multiple Apps, websites, documents and SOP’s.

title: Technical Safety Engineer
description:
Title:

Technical Safety Engineer

KBR’s Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) group is looking for a Technical Senior Safety Engineer to support the Abadi LNG project, one of the largest projects in Asia.  This project will provide front-end design (FEED) for onshore liquefied natural gas facilities & will have a peak production capacity targets of 9.5 million tons per annum of LNG and 150 million standard cubic feet per day of pipeline gas.  The Abadi LNG project has been designated a project of national strategic importance by the Indonesian government.

The Technical Senior Safety Engineer will develop Design Safety Philosophies, Specifications for fire protection systems (active & passive), data sheets for firefighting systems independently or with minimum supervision. 

 Responsibilities:  

Develop UFDs, P&IDs for the fire protection systems and perform Fire water/foam demand calculations (incl. Gas suppression system), and Firewater system Hydraulic check analysis
Prepare Hazardous Area Classification Source release schedule and Drawings, Fire Zone drawings, Fire & Gas Detection Layouts, Safety & Fire Fighting equipment layouts, , Escape route drawings, Firefighting Nozzle coverage shadow drawings. Etc
Participate in Process Hazard reviews and analysis including HAZOP/HAZID/SIL/Bowtie/ALARP studies (when needed) and support in Actions close-out
Under minimum supervision or independently, carry out the design of Active and Passive Fire Protection packages (including preparing requisitions, datasheets, TBE, etc) and PFP schedule documents
Support in reviewing/consolidating comments and coordinating third party studies, including FERA, dispersion analysis, EERA, ESSA, QRA studies, etc. (not limited to)
Support preparation of TBE and vendor document reviews for Mechanical/Electrical/Instrument packages on safety / HFE aspects
Provide inputs, including Human Factors Engineering, for projects as required
Interface/coordinate with other Engineering disciplines to resolve technical matters related to safety aspects & with Designers and provide inputs for safety layout preparations for projects as required

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in chemical engineering or related field
2-4 years HSE Engineering experience (Process Safety/Risk Analysis/Loss Prevention Engineering), with average experience ranging from 2-4 years in the Hydrocarbon industry
LNG facilities experience in design projects is required
Strong knowledge of International Codes and Standards, Regulatory codes and standards (DNV/ ABSNFPA) and the ability to influence designs to achieve optimal HSE outcomes
Familiar with plot plan reviews, HAZID, HAZOP, SIL classification/ verification and other safety reviews (e.g.SIMOPS, ALARP)
Good working knowledge of PIPENET, Flaresim & other consequence modelling software such as DNV PHAST etc
Need to be a good team engineer and have proactive inter-discipline communication skills

As a trusted partner of the U.S. Department of War, MAGS provides innovative, technology-driven solutions to enhance national security. Job Summary

description:
Title:

Electrical & Instrumentation Engineer

As an Electrical & Instrumentation Engineer, you will perform advanced engineering techniques, makes decisions on engineering problems and methods, and interfaces with the client to define project scope. Required to perform electrical engineering and design assignments associated with production, maintenance, process, capital projects, R&D, and power distribution involving the application of established electrical technology and principles, including performing all electrical calculations, and often requiring coordination with other engineering design, and cross-functional competencies to provide economical and expedient task implementation. The assignment will include participation in all electrical functions associated with projects including assistance with front end loading, production design, electrical construction management, commissioning, startup, and troubleshooting activities. Provides technical guidance to designers and less experienced engineers and is consulted extensively by the associates and others with a high degree of reliance placed on scientific interpretations and advice. Job role is responsible for a measurable asset including but not limited to forecasting & budget. 

***Must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident***

This is a long-term position located in Parlin, NJ. 

Responsibilities

Functions as a project lead for a small project or an area lead for larger projects.

Scope definition from receipt of basic data to Issue for Design process deliverables

Interface with the clients’ cross functional teams to define all operating requirements.

Responsible for study, design, specification, and services related to electrical systems including power generation, power systems performance and control, cabling and wiring, lighting, motor control centers, communication systems, cathodic protection, grounding, lightning protection, heat tracing, etc. 

Responsibility for assessing the quality, robustness, and capability of newly designed and installed Capital Projects.

Industrial electrical power distribution ranging from high voltage (greater than 35kV), medium voltage (1kV through 35kV) through low voltage (120V through 1kV)

Electrical power distribution equipment such as generators, substations, switchgear, transformers, motor control centers, distribution panels

Electrical utilization equipment such as motors (AC and DC), controllers, electrical process equipment

Electrical drawing knowledge (reading and generation via MicroStation V8):

Single Line Diagrams

Three Line Diagrams

Schematic Diagrams

Wiring Diagrams

Physical Drawings

Involved in discussions around the control of the process.  Frequently pulls in additional technical resources for making decisions about the project viability and resolve any safety concerns or hazards.

Provides engineering, Checkout and Qualification for the Capital Project process control systems, such as distributive control systems and components, instrumentation technology, and programmable logic controllers.

Overall responsibility for design, specification, selection, and services relating to instrumentation and control systems including basic process control systems, safety systems, control panels, analyzer systems, field instrumentation, valves, etc.

May self-perform or lead other engineers to complete project scope and provide technical guidance to less experienced engineers. On some occasions, will also plan, schedule, and conduct work requiring independent judgment and adaptation of engineering techniques.

Participation in Process Hazard Analysis for project-related work.

Define the process design basis for other disciplines, specifically Electrical Systems, conduit sizing, and Instrumentation and interface with these groups throughout detailed design. Leading multidisciplinary small project teams across several different businesses and site infrastructure.

Develop project estimates, scopes, and schedule.  May lead estimate reviews.

Work with Construction Manager during FEL as well as to oversee project execution in the field.

Forecasting and project cost tracking, monthly.

Manage scope change technically and commercially.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or Control Systems

Must have a good understanding and knowledge of industry codes and standards (NFPA 70E/NEC, OSHA, IEEE, ANSI, NEMA, API, and ASI.

8+ years of qualified related experience

Experience in the chemical, refining, or biofuels industry required.

Experience with P&ID Development, equipment sizing, electrical calculations, and instrumentation.  Demonstrated leadership of process design on capital projects, including responsibility for budget, schedule, and change management.

Professional Engineering (P.E.) license preferred but not required.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

· Work is located at a chemical plant and requires exposure to ambient temperature extremes

· Work may require using and wearing personal protective equipment such as fire-retardant clothing, hearing and eye protection, hard hat and steel-toed boots

· Day-to-day physical requirements involve standard office activities including sitting/standing for extended periods of time, attending meetings, use of keyboard and mouse repetitively, lifting and carrying less than 20 lbs frequently, etc

· Work requires moderate physical exertion including walking to operating areas and walking up stairs

· Assignments may require conducting plant walkdowns and wearing chemical plant or refinery PPE to include an H2S monitor, escape respirator, and FP coveralls.

title: Subcontracts Administrator
description:
Title:

Subcontracts Administrator

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! 

Program Summary

KBR's Readiness and Sustainment (R&S) division is the Team Behind the Mission®. We deliver mission critical services to the U.S. military and coalition partners around the world. Our key capabilities include base operations; contingency and expeditionary support; next generation asset management; digitally focused logistics; prepositioned stock; and integrated supply chain management.

Specifically, this role will be supporting the Marine Corps’ Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) and Marine Corps Prepositioning Program (MCPP), who have been operationally invaluable in supporting our Nation’s interests across the world. Located at the Marine Corps Support Facility Blount Island in Jacksonville, Florida, the program ensures that combat-ready equipment and supplies are pre-positioned to support rapid deployment and sustainment of Marine forces worldwide.

Job Summary

The Subcontracts Administrator plays a crucial role in managing all procurement and administrative activities related to subcontracting. The administrator will oversee the full range of procurement and subcontract management, from pre-award activities through close-out. Under general supervision, this role will require problem-solving skills, industry knowledge, and the ability to navigate both field and best practices in subcontract administration.

 **This role will be onsite the Blount Island military installation in Jacksonville, FL 

Roles and Responsibilities 

Effectively manage the subcontracts lifecycle as associated with procurement activity.

Issue requests for proposals, evaluate proposals, and qualify suppliers.

Maintain accurate subcontract files in compliance with established procedures.

Utilize problem-solving skills and industry knowledge to steer best practices for the group.

Display expertise within the subcontracting focus and seek continuous improvement within both processes and individual skills.

Basic Qualifications 

Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.

At least 2+ years of experience in subcontract administration or related procurement activities.

Strong understanding of procurement processes, proposal evaluation, and subcontract management.

Excellent negotiation and communication skills.

Minimum 5 years of experience with large-scale Cisco-based WAN/LAN environments.

Proven experience configuring and troubleshooting security configuration issues with MS Exchange, WWW, DNS, and NT Domain Controllers are required.

description:
Title:

UABOS Turkey LN: Water Treatment Plant Mechanic Operator

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! 

Program Summary

KBR supports the operational needs of U.S. armed forces at Morón Air Base in Spain and several bases in Turkey. Our services ensure smooth operations, allowing Air Force and government personnel to focus on their missions. We provide program management, civil engineering, morale, welfare, and recreation support, among other essential services. Awarded by the Air Force Installation Contracting Center, our contract spans a five-year base period with three one-year options, reflecting our commitment to excellence and operational support.

Job Summary

Incirlik Air Base Water Treatment Plant operator has the responsibility to operate, maintain, inspect, repair and overhauling Water treatment system, Ground water wells, Filtration process, Reverse Osmosis system, Disinfection and Fluoridation processes, base swimming pool and associated equipment and system components. The candidate should be familiar with hazardous chemical work environments to include corrosive acids and toxic gases. The operator is also responsible for ensuring all facilities equipment operate in the most efficient manner possible to ensure that the facility meets safety, efficiency, quality, and environmental targets that exceed KBR and UABOS standards.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Ensure compliance with all operational guidelines, standards, and regulations to guarantee that treated water entering the distribution system is safe and meets quality requirements.
Monitor, operate, repair, and maintain plant processes and associated equipment system components to ensure optimal performance and reliability.
Conduct routine inspections and operational rounds for treatment systems, water wells, main pump stations, water storage tanks, and swimming pools to verify functionality and compliance.
Operate and monitor the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system to control and assess plant operations.
Collect, inspect, test, and evaluate water samples to ensure compliance with regulatory limits and operational standards.
Maintain and adjust chemical feed pumps to achieve proper chemical dosage rates, ensuring effective treatment.
Monitor chemical dosage tank levels and perform timely refills to sustain uninterrupted operations.
Perform preventive maintenance on plant equipment, including calibrations, basic mechanical and electrical repairs, lubrication, and replacement of worn components.
Maintain accurate and complete records, including daily operating logs, Air Force (AF) forms, inspection checklists, chemical usage logs, and parts inventory reports.
Support facility upkeep by performing general building and grounds maintenance, grass cutting, cargo hauling, trash removal, and contractor escort duties.
Operate hand and power tools safely and effectively in the execution of assigned duties.
Attend required training sessions to maintain compliance and proficiency in plant operations and safety procedures.
Perform additional related duties as assigned to meet operational needs.
Daily use of mechanical, electrical, and automation systems, with the ability to troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair instrumentation malfunctions.
Daily use of common hand tools and related equipment in a safe and correct manner.
Daily use of Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) to complete reports, tasks, and communicate with customers and co-workers.
Responsible for the complete operation and maintenance of the water treatment plant.
Read, write, compile, and analyze technical data and reports daily.
Work collaboratively and respectfully with colleagues in close-quarters operational environments.
Maintain operational readiness through regular equipment inspections, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
Work may involve noise exposure, chemical fumes, and hazardous chemicals in liquid, vapor, or solid forms.
Daily use of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) to include but not limited to chemical coveralls, full-faced mask, and SCBA when performing assigned tasks.
Demonstrate sound judgment in safe work practices and proper equipment usage.
Frequent entering of confined spaces (manholes, reservoirs, filters, water storage tanks) and climbing elevated structures up to 40–50 meters.
Work on rotating shifts (days, nights, evenings), including weekends and holidays.
Available for emergency on-call duty and overtime on a 24-hour basis.
Maintain punctuality and a reliable level of attendance.
Work with minimal supervision while meeting performance expectations.

Basic Qualifications 

Turkish Citizen
Possess a valid Class B driver’s license.
English Level I
High school diploma

Preferred Qualifications

2- or 4-year degree in Electrical, Control and Automation, Industrial Automation, Mechanical Trade, or a related technical field.
English level II
Experience working in industrial systems maintenance, including water pumps, electric and diesel-driven motors, mechanical systems, motorized and pneumatic valves, chemical dosing systems, control panels, and automation systems.
Experience in the maintenance, repair, and operation of mechanical and electrical pumping systems and related machinery within a municipal water or wastewater treatment plant environment.
PLC/SCADA programming and instrumentation experience, or equivalent control systems certification.

Mission and Scope

This opportunity is located in Canberra. 

The End User Compute (EUC) Engineer is responsible for the support, maintenance, and continuous improvement of endpoint and server environments across client ICT systems. This role ensures that users have secure, reliable, and performant access to computing resources by managing endpoint configurations, server infrastructure, application packaging and patch compliance.

Operating under the direction of the Service Delivery Manager (SDM), the EUC Engineer works closely with both infrastructure and service delivery teams to support platforms such as MECM, WSUS and MDT. This position involves hands-on support, advanced troubleshooting, system optimisation and adherence to best practices in user device management and standard operating environment (SOE) design.

Responsibilities

The key responsibilities of the role will include, but are not limited to:

Service Operations

Provide day-to-day sustainment of EUC platform services.

Monitor and maintain endpoint performance, patch compliance, and availability.

Administer EUC services across several government networks with varying sizes and classifications.

Respond to and resolve incidents and service requests.

Work within SHIs and in alignment with SOW-defined service boundaries.

Incident & Change Management

Act as a primary escalation point for complex EUC-related incidents and problems.

Conduct root cause analysis for recurring issues and implement corrective actions.

Plan, test and implement changes in accordance with established change management processes.

Participate in change advisory board (CAB) meetings where required, ensuring EUC-related changes are risk-assessed and documented.

Ensure changes are rolled out with minimal user disruption and in line with service level expectations.

 

SOE & Endpoint Management

Maintain and enhance Standard Operating Environment (SOE) images for desktops and servers using tools such as MDT and SCCM.

Manage and deploy operating system updates, security patches and configuration baselines.

Ensure consistent application of group policies and compliance with configuration standards.

Application Packaging & Deployment

Package, test, and deploy applications to endpoints and servers using SCCM and/or Tanium.

Manage application updates, version control, and compatibility with the SOE.

Liaise with application owners and business stakeholders to ensure successful packaging and deployment of new applications.

User File Storage & Profile Management

Support enterprise user file storage solutions and ensure availability and recoverability of user data.

Implement and maintain profile management and redirection solutions.

Support migration and consolidation of user data during SOE refreshes or system transitions.

Incident Response & Crisis Management

Act as an escalation point for technical ICT incident, working closely with internal teams and external partners to restore services quickly and effectively.

Participate in post-incident reviews to analyse root causes and implement preventive measures.

3+ years’ experience in an EUC, Desktop Engineering or Systems Administration role.

Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops (or equivalent VDI platforms).

Endpoint management via SCCM, Tanium or similar platforms.

SOE development and management with MDT or other imaging tools.

NV1 Security clearance (with the ability to upgrade to NV2).

Background supporting secure or classified environments with compliance requirements.

description:
Title:

Lead RF Engineer

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR seeks a Lead RF Engineer with expertise in signal processing, embedded systems, and cybersecurity to advance our mission-critical programs. The ideal candidate will combine hands-on experience in real-time software development (C/C++, Python), digital signal processing (DSP), and RF engineering with technical leadership skills to mentor teams delivering solutions for environments at the tactical edge.

Ideal candidates are eager to build on their expertise in SIGINT applications, real-time SWaP-constrained systems, and AI development to address high-stakes national security challenges. They should demonstrate proven leadership in delivering mission-critical defense solutions and possess hands-on experience in prototype development, from design through implementation, testing, and user transition. 

Why Join Us? 

Innovative Projects: At KBR, you'll be working on prototype projects that support the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory’s most mission-critical objectives. The Air Force Research Laboratory is the primary scientific research and development center for the Department of the Air Force. AFRL plays an integral role in leading the discovery, development, and integration of affordable warfighting technologies for our air, space, and cyberspace force.  
Collaborative Environment: KBR fosters a dynamic and collaborative atmosphere where cross-functional teams of product managers, engineers, developers, and defense experts work in unison. We practice Agile and DevOps principles, ensuring rapid iteration, continuous feedback, and integration across all projects. Our team is passionate, forward-thinking, and united by a mission-first mindset that encourages knowledge sharing, innovation, and problem-solving at every level. 
Impactful Work: Your work here won’t just be limited to software development—it will directly support the Air Force in expanding current national capabilities. As the Air Force's leader for National-to-Tactical capability development, AFRL collaborates with leading experts across the Intelligence Community, Department of Defense, National Laboratories, industry, inter-agency, academia, and partner nations. 

Key Responsibilities:

Lead full-cycle development of real-time, resource-constrained systems (e.g., SDR-based adaptive filtering, GPS spoofing mitigation) using AI/ML and DSP techniques
Architect and prototype cybersecurity capabilities to counteract SIGINT threats, jamming interference, and target tracking challenges
Collaborate with stakeholders to design functioning prototypes aligned with operational constraints
Mentor junior engineers in software development methodologies, technical problem-solving, and embedded software lifecycle management
Communicate complex concepts clearly to senior leadership and non-specialist audiences

Work Environment:

Location: Colorado Springs, CO – 100% Onsite
Travel Requirements: Minimal
Working Hours: Standard

description:
Title:

Research Scientist

BELONG. CONNECT. GROW. with KBR.

Around here, we define the future. We are a company of innovators, thinkers, creators, explorers, volunteers, and dreamers. But we all share one goal: to improve the world responsibly and safely.

Job Description:
 

The Intelligent Systems Research and Development Support (ISRDS) contract supports NASA Ames Research Center in developing and infusing advanced technology into NASA missions. Our scientists, engineers and technologists support research and development of critical enabling technologies for all of the NASA Mission Directorates. This KBR-led team has supported technology development for NASA space exploration missions such as LADEE, VIPER, Biosentinel, Starling and TESS, supports payload development for the International Space Station, and develops robotics and autonomous operations technologies for lunar and planetary exploration, and performs research in materials modeling (including quantum materials) and quantum computing.


KBR is looking for a Research Scientist to support the Quantum Artificial Intelligence Lab (QuAIL) at NASA Ames.  This person must have a strong expertise in development and analysis of quantum and quantum-inspired algorithms, quantum simulation, quantum error-correction and quantum error mitigation and a deep understanding of the physics behind quantum algorithms. We are looking for a candidate with at least 3 years of experience in exploring quantum computing including hardware and software experience.


This person will lead independent research through numerical and theoretical analysis, exploring quantum error-correction, quantum algorithms, and quantum “inspired” classical algorithms for near-term applications on quantum devices, including but not limited to quantum machine learning, quantum simulation and optimization. This person must be skilled in both numerical and analytical evaluation of the performance of quantum and classical algorithms, comparing different quantum and quantum-classical hybrid approaches with each other and with state-of-the-art classical alternatives.


This individual must have demonstrated experience leading a team of researchers in quantum computing, and in leading technical proposal efforts.

Responsibilities:

Will support development and analysis of quantum and quantum inspired algorithms
Will support resource estimation and benchmarking of architectures and algorithms
Will support research and software engineering on quantum error-correction and quantum algorithms
Will lead research on fundamental quantum mechanisms and their use in quantum computation
May support and lead other related tasks in quantum sciences, data sciences and AI-based technologies

REQUIRED Skills and Traits:

Ph.D. in Physics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
3+ years of experience in quantum computing
Experience in developing, benchmarking
Demonstrated ability to lead small teams
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Ability to develop and execute technical proposals

The KBR Metrology team supports manufacturing, engineering & test, repair & overhaul, and aftermarket service centers globally in support of Aerospace & Defense, Automotive, Medical, Safety, Semiconductor and other industries.  Our support includes services such as complete management of embedded metrology systems, calibration and repair, test & inspection, metrology engineering, preventive maintenance, NADCAP special process support, and AMS2750 Heat Treat pyrometry services and more.  Our teams are located across the globe working in KBR and customer embedded laboratories as well as performing onsite visits with our field service operations and mobile laboratory platforms.  Our teams work to ensure our customer systems are maintained to high standards through calibration, preventative maintenance, automation and programming, calibration recall system management, and audit support.  We ensure great customer experience by tracking and providing performance and delivery metrics through digital dashboards, as well as routine customer service surveys and direct customer meetings.

Metrology Technician II is responsible for performing routine calibrations, tests and/or inspections in-lab or on-site using accredited standards, taking care of the day-to-day escalations and priority requests, maintaining traceability and calibration of laboratory standards.   Calibrations, tests and inspections may be performed with and/or without automation.  The position requires knowledge and fluency in basic and advanced calibration, test, and/or inspection procedures and processes, and hands-on experience with setting up advanced test equipment calibration systems.  This position also requires the ability to review, validate, create, and/or modify calibration, test, and/or inspection procedures. Uses all hand tools and sets up and uses standard machine tools. Uses common laboratory measuring, calibrating, and test equipment.

Title:

LCV APS-2 Germany: Maintenance Technician (COMSEC/C5ISR)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! 

Program Summary

KBR leads the global government‑services contingency market by providing responsive, full‑service logistics support to forces deployed worldwide under the Army & Strategic Programs. Under APS‑2, KBR supports the Army Prepositioned Stocks program by delivering maintenance, readiness, and logistics solutions that enable the rapid deployment of combat‑ready equipment and materiel across Europe in support of U.S. Army missions. Our APS‑2 workforce is composed of skilled professionals from diverse backgrounds who work together to ensure all equipment is properly stored, maintained, and mission‑ready for issue whenever required.

Job Summary

As a Maintenance Technician COMSEC/C5ISR, you will provide technical expertise in the maintenance, installation, and troubleshooting of Communications Security (COMSEC) equipment and Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) systems. This role ensures secure communications and operational readiness of mission-critical systems in compliance with Department of Defense (DoD) standards and security protocols.

This position is designated as a TESA (Technical Expert Status Accreditation) role. Candidates must meet all TESA eligibility requirements as defined by the U.S. Army and applicable SOFA regulations. Final approval is subject to government review and issuance of TESA status. Employment is contingent upon successfully obtaining and maintaining TESA accreditation for the duration of the assignment.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Perform field and sustainment-level maintenance on COMSEC and C5ISR systems, including cryptographic devices, Controlled Cryptographic Items (CCI), radios, and associated electronic subsystems.
Install, configure, and verify communication systems in tactical vehicles and fixed facilities.
Conduct troubleshooting and diagnostics using specialized Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, and signal generators.
Implement Modification Work Orders (MWO) and ensure compliance with technical manuals, Army Regulations (AR), and security directives.
Maintain accountability and secure storage of COMSEC material in accordance with DoD and NSA policies.
Perform key management operations using EKMS/KMI systems and devices like SKL AN/PYQ-10 and KIK-30.
Document maintenance actions, prepare reports, and update system records in GCSS-Army or equivalent platforms.
Adhere to safety protocols and promote a culture of zero accidents during high-voltage and sensitive equipment handling.
Provide technical training and guidance to junior technicians and supported units

Basic Qualifications (Required Education, Experience, Skills, and Certifications)

U.S. Citizen with ability to obtain and maintain a Secret clearance.
Must have a bachelor’s degree plus 3 years of recent specialized experience, OR; An associate’s degree plus 7 years of recent specialized experience, OR; A major certification plus 7 years of recent specialized experience, OR; 11 years of recent specialized experience.
Minimum 3–5 years of experience in COMSEC or C5ISR systems maintenance and installation.
Proficiency in reading and applying Army Technical Manuals (TM), Technical Bulletins (TB), and wiring diagrams.
Familiarity with cryptographic key management systems (EKMS/KMI) and COMSEC handling procedures
Must be able to work in non-climate-controlled environments, outdoors in all weather conditions.
Must be able to grasp or handle objects, use finger dexterity, bend elbow/knee and reach above/below shoulders.
Must be able to lift and carry up to 40 pounds unassisted.
Must be able to team lift up to 50 pounds in a two-person carry.
Must be able to speak, read and write English fluently.
Must be free of medical restriction/ limitations that prevent the wearing and utilization of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Must be able to pass pre-employment and background checks related to the position.
Must be able to climb in and out of military vehicles and related equipment.
Must be able to work in cramped areas for at least two continuous hours.
Must be able to work in all types of weather conditions to include intense heat, heavy wind, blowing sand, heavy rain, and snow and sleet.

Our APS‑2 workforce is composed of skilled professionals from diverse backgrounds who work together to ensure all equipment is properly stored, maintained, and mission‑ready for issue whenever required.

Job Summary

As a Maintenance Technician COMSEC/C5ISR, you will provide technical expertise in the maintenance, installation, and troubleshooting of Communications Security (COMSEC) equipment and Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Combat Systems, Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) systems. This role ensures secure communications and operational readiness of mission-critical systems in compliance with Department of Defense (DoD) standards and security protocols.

This position is designated as a TESA (Technical Expert Status Accreditation) role. Candidates must meet all TESA eligibility requirements as defined by the U.S. Army and applicable SOFA regulations. Final approval is subject to government review and issuance of TESA status. Roles and Responsibilities 

Perform field and sustainment-level maintenance on COMSEC and C5ISR systems, including cryptographic devices, Controlled Cryptographic Items (CCI), radios, and associated electronic subsystems.
Install, configure, and verify communication systems in tactical vehicles and fixed facilities.
Conduct troubleshooting and diagnostics using specialized Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, and signal generators.
Implement Modification Work Orders (MWO) and ensure compliance with technical manuals, Army Regulations (AR), and security directives.
Maintain accountability and secure storage of COMSEC material in accordance with DoD and NSA policies.
Perform key management operations using EKMS/KMI systems and devices like SKL AN/PYQ-10 and KIK-30.
Document maintenance actions, prepare reports, and update system records in GCSS-Army or equivalent platforms.
Adhere to safety protocols and promote a culture of zero accidents during high-voltage and sensitive equipment handling.
Provide technical training and guidance to junior technicians and supported units

Basic Qualifications (Required Education, Experience, Skills, and Certifications)

Must have an Active U.S. Government issued Secret Security Clearance and maintain it for the duration of your employment on this contract. Due to this, you must be a U.S. Citizen to be eligible for this position.
Must have a bachelor’s degree plus 3 years of recent specialized experience, OR; An associate’s degree plus 7 years of recent specialized experience, OR; A major certification plus 7 years of recent specialized experience, OR; 11 years of recent specialized experience.
Minimum 3–5 years of experience in COMSEC or C5ISR systems maintenance and installation.
Proficiency in reading and applying Army Technical Manuals (TM), Technical Bulletins (TB), and wiring diagrams.
Familiarity with cryptographic key management systems (EKMS/KMI) and COMSEC handling procedures
Must be able to work in non-climate-controlled environments, outdoors in all weather conditions.
Must be able to grasp or handle objects, use finger dexterity, bend elbow/knee and reach above/below shoulders.
Must be able to lift and carry up to 40 pounds unassisted.
Must be able to team lift up to 50 pounds in a two-person carry.
Must be able to speak, read and write English fluently.
Must be free of medical restriction/ limitations that prevent the wearing and utilization of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Must be able to pass pre-employment and background checks related to the position.
Must be able to climb in and out of military vehicles and related equipment.
Must be able to work in cramped areas for at least two continuous hours.
Must be able to work in all types of weather conditions to include intense heat, heavy wind, blowing sand, heavy rain, and snow and sleet.
Employees shall utilize all proper lifting procedures and practices associated with all lifting and material handling tasks that are assigned and associated with this job description
Requires a valid passport with at least 12 months of validity and 6 blank pages.

Preferred Qualifications (Preferred Education, Experience, Skills, and Certifications)

Certified COMSEC Technician (CCT) or equivalent certification.
Certified C5ISR Technician (CC5ISR-Tech) or related credentials.
GCSS-Army certification and experience with DoD maintenance systems.
Advanced knowledge of IP networking, LAN/WAN troubleshooting, and secure communications protocols.
Experience with Type 1 cryptographic devices and associated loaders.
Experience and ability to work effectively with non-native English speakers strongly preferred.
Prior overseas professional experience.

Title:

Project Overview

KBR is recruiting full-time Radar Graphical User Interface Tester Intern for the spring 2026/summer 2026 semester. The intern will work through the software development lifecycle to help design and test a graphic user interface to control a radar system composed of an Arduino and ultrasonic sensors. This project will utilize agile test cycles, and the test intern will work side by side with the developer intern on identifying and documenting bugs, peer reviewing test cases, closing out New Feature tickets and deciding when a new build may be warranted. By the end of this project, interns will gain valuable experience working through the software development lifecycle to deliver a working radar system.

Key Responsibilities

Define system and user requirements.

Develop and Execute Test Cases.

Produce Test Reports.

Learning Outcomes & Impact

The Radar Graphical User Interface (GUI) Application project aims to provide an opportunity for an intern to demonstrate basic radar principles by developing a sonar radar application. The intern will work through the software development lifecycle to design and build a python graphic user interface to control a radar system composed of an Arduino and ultrasonic sensors. The intern will work with a team member to understand the desired functionality, performance criteria, and constraints in order to define system requirements. Based on the requirements, the intern will design and build a radar system using off the shelf components such as an Arduino and ultrasonic sensors. The radar system requires the intern to develop a GUI to serve as the primary interface for user to interact with the radar system, providing them real-time data visualization, control options and intuitive functionalities. The intern will work closely with testers to provide test procedures and user manuals to validate the functionality and performance of the radar system. Interns will be responsible for providing ongoing maintenance and support for the radar system, including bug fixes, updates, enhancements. title: ESP Downhole Reliability Engineer
description:
Title:

ESP Downhole Reliability Engineer

ESP Downhole Reliability  Engineer

EMNR30 - Sr. Technical Professional Maintenance & Reliability Engineer

KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets.

The ESP Reliability Engineer is responsible for improving the reliability, performance, and integrity of all Electrical Submersible Pump (ESP) systems throughout their operating life. The main focus is to extend ESP run life, reduce unplanned failures, and support production goals by applying sound reliability engineering practices and data driven analysis.

As the number of ESP operated wells in the field continues to grow, the reliability function becomes increasingly critical to sustaining performance and managing operational complexity. The ESP Reliability Engineer ensures that every system performs to design expectations and that lessons from the field are systematically turned into improvements in design, operation, and maintenance.

The role involves working closely with operations, maintenance, subsurface, and vendors to understand equipment behaviour, identify reliability risks, and recommend practical solutions. Typical responsibilities include analysing ESP performance trends, leading Dismantle and Inspection (DIFA) and Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA) activities, maintaining failure records, and tracking reliability KPIs to measure performance improvements over time.

Based on findings from field investigations and lessons learned, the ESP Reliability Engineer works with vendors and field teams to raise alerts and document any manufacturing, quality, or procedural issues, recommending design or process changes to prevent similar problems in the future. This helps close the feedback loop between field operations, engineering, and manufacturers, ensuring lessons are turned into lasting improvements.

Performance data from PI Vision and other monitoring tools is used to spot anomalies early and support evidence-based investigations during DIFA and reliability reviews. The ESP Reliability 

Engineer also works closely with the Data Scientist and Reliability Advisor in designing, maintaining, and continuously improving ESP reliability dashboards in Power BI, ensuring data is effectively transformed into actionable insights that drive better decisions and field performance.

The ESP Reliability Engineer in close coordination with the Reliability Advisor, ensures alignment on reliability priorities, shares technical findings, and jointly drives improvement actions to enhance ESP performance across the field. Both roles collaborate as partners within the reliability function, combining field insight and analytical expertise to achieve safer, more efficient, and more reliable operations.

Responsibilities
Reliability & Technical Assurance
Lead and coordinate ESP failure investigations, including Dismantle and Inspection (DIFA) and Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA).
Analyze operating parameters, well histories, and performance trends to identify emerging reliability issues.
Maintain and update the ESP failure database, ensuring data integrity, traceability, and proper documentation of all incidents.
Review and validate contractor failure reports and warranty cases, ensuring corrective actions are effectively implemented.
Provide technical recommendations to enhance ESP system design, installation practices, and operational standards.
Develop and maintain reliability dashboards and reports to track KPIs such as MTBF, run life, recurring failure modes, and reliability trends.
Analyze ESP failure data and historical performance to identify patterns, risks, and opportunities for reliability improvement.
Conduct preliminary assessments of reported anomalies or incidents and recommend further investigation or corrective actions.
Support RCFA and DIFA investigations by verifying technical findings and ensuring appropriate follow-up actions.
Review reliability metrics and maintenance reports to provide actionable recommendations to improve ESP life and reduce failures.
Advise on reliability risks associated with planned changes or maintenance activities, ensuring alignment with design limits and safety standards.
Document findings, lessons learned, and recommendations in formal reliability reports and databases.

Operational Support
Provide technical expertise on ESP systems to identify, analyze, and resolve performance deviations or anomalies highlighted through DIFA findings.
Support site teams in assessing and managing reliability risks to minimize potential production impacts.
Review operational data and DIFA insights to recommend improvements in ESP performance, efficiency, and longevity.
Collaborate with Operations and Maintenance teams to ensure ESP systems operate within safe and design parameters.
Lead investigations into recurring equipment failures identified through DIFA or operational performance trends and recommend preventive actions.
Contribute to reliability-centered maintenance strategies and continuous improvement efforts based on failure analysis findings.

Recommend monitoring, control, and mitigation measures to prevent reliability failures from escalating into safety incidents.
Integrate lessons learned from ESP failures into process safety management programs to enhance risk reduction.
Maintain documentation of reliability assessments, risk analyses, and failure investigation outcomes for compliance and future reference.

Continuous Improvement
Lead or support Continuous Improvement (CI) initiatives focused on increasing ESP availability, reducing failure rates, and lowering lifecycle costs.
Analyze recurring failure trends and recommend design, operational, or process modifications to eliminate root causes.
Document and share lessons learned, reliability alerts, and best practices across internal teams and contractors.
Evaluate and support adoption of new technologies, predictive maintenance tools, and data analytics to strengthen ESP reliability monitoring.

Collaboration & Coaching (Reliability Focus)
Collaborate with vendors, engineering, operations, and maintenance teams to align reliability strategies with system design and performance objectives.
Act as a central point for sharing reliability insights, failure analyses, and technical recommendations across stakeholders.
Facilitate cross-functional discussions to prioritize reliability improvements and ensure consistent implementation of best practices.

description:
Title:

AFCAP V Japan BOS: SCS Maintenance - Electrical/HVAC Technician

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! 

Program Summary

In support of the U.S. Air Force, KBR provides security, base operations, maintenance, and repair at Kyogamisaki and Shariki Communications Sites in Japan​. Our team is focused on providing continued mission-critical support in the INDOPACOM area of responsibility. In addition to base life support and facility and equipment maintenance and operations, KBR provides food services and other quality of life support. Our team was able to meet an accelerated transition timeline and ensure these mission essential sites ran without disruption throughout the contract transition.

Job Summary

Responsible for inspecting, maintenance, repairing and preventive maintenance on sites Power Quality, Ground Support Equipment, Fire and Safety Hazards, Lighting Standards, Comprehensive Electrical System Surveys, Electrical System Inspections.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Maintains, inspects, and repairs the site’s electrical system automatic transfer switches for all sites, and monitors electrical connections on site generators.
Maintains and repairs low voltage (600 volts and below) real property electrical systems to the code that it was installed.
Maintains and repairs the electrical systems (600 volts and below) on feeder circuits from the main lugs (secondary bushings) on the load side of pad mounted transformers for underground systems, and the standard utility connection point of an overhead riser or meter loop, transformers, streetlights, grounding equipment, electrical manholes, and other systems on-site.
Install, repair, replace, modify, test, and maintain fire alarm systems, the disaster warning system, and intrusion alarm systems to maintain proper operational capability IAW UFC 3-601-02, NFPA, and the original equipment manufacturer's instructions.
Performs installation, operation, maintenance, repairs, and disposal of heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC/R) systems.
Must have mandatory knowledge on the principles of HVAC/R systems, controls, and components.
Must be highly proficient in the troubleshooting, repair, preventive maintenance and rewiring of the site’s fleet of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) equipment, in particular the 5-Ton Environmental Control Unit (ECU) built by Alaska Structures Incorporated.
Should have the ability to interpret drawings and schematics.
Must know and be able to apply the fundamentals of HVAC/R equipment and troubleshooting techniques, and environmental regulations for fuels, refrigerants, and hazardous materials. May explain instructions and documentation to plan work activities.
Completes and reviews records, maintains tools and equipment, and performs various cleanup activities. Job may require moderate to heavy lifting.
Observes and follows all safety rules and procedures, including wearing required personal safety equipment.

Additional general duties:

Acts as Alternate Maximo and Alternate Hazardous Material (HAZMAT) and Hazardous Waste (HAZWASTE) key person.
Performs general preventative maintenance tasks on assigned heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) units, power generation equipment, permanent and temporary structures including doors, windows, sinks and toilets.
Performs corrosion control measures on site structures such as entry control points, force protection points, fences, gates, and signs.
Maintains and operates the assigned material handling equipment (MHE) such as the Bobcat multipurpose handler and associated attachments, 2.5K and 10K forklifts and manlift.
Maintains and operates the assigned grass cutting equipment such as riding and push type lawnmowers, Bobcat lawnmower attachment and weed trimmers.
Maintains and operates the assigned snow removal equipment such as the tracked and wheeled snowblowers and the Bobcat snowplow and snowblower attachments.
Participates in the bimonthly Morale Welfare and Recreational (MWR) schedule.
Operates and drives the company vehicles to perform twice weekly (Tuesdays and Thursdays) mail pick-up and delivery runs to Misawa AB, Japan Air Post Office (APO).
Concurrently, completes shopping requirements at the Misawa AB commissary and exchange for the site-operated kiosk.

Basic Qualifications 

At least 5 years of experience.
Requires a high school diploma or equivalent 
Must possess active secret security clearance
Possess an EPA Section 608 Universal Refrigerant Handling Certification or be able to obtain the certification within 30 days of arrival at the job site. 
Prefer an electrical technician certification required by contract and laws (to include DoD and U.S. Army directives and regulations.

title: Lead Process Engineer - LNG
description:
Title:

Lead Process Engineer - LNG

KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets.

KBR is seeking a Lead Process Engineer - LNG for its Houston office. Under broad direction, this role provides technical and people leadership for a team of engineers, including responsibility for performance management, coaching, and professional development. The position oversees and directs a significant segment of a large, complex engineering program—or an entire program of moderate scope—encompassing planning, budgeting, organization, and execution. The role carries accountability for measurable assets, including assigned staff and budget, and requires extensive experience typically gained through an undergraduate engineering degree and a minimum of ten (10) years of relevant experience, with most incumbents possessing 15 or more years of industry experience.

Functional job responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

Execute process engineering work for large‑ and medium‑sized projects, or defined scopes within major projects, in accordance with applicable industry codes, standards, and best practices.
Lead and perform key process engineering activities, including licensor evaluation and selection; process modeling and simulation; development of heat, material, and utility balances; preparation of process flow diagrams (PFDs, process safeguarding flow diagrams (PSFD), Safe Chart, piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&ID), development of the project Basis of Design; definition of system design parameters; and design and/or rating of process equipment such as vessels, columns, heat exchangers, pumps, and related systems.
Conduct and support a wide range of process studies, including process optimization, flare and relief systems, blowdown and depressurization, vent system design, cooling and heating media studies, utility system sizing, condensate handling, produced solids management (including sand handling), and produced water treatment evaluations.
Participate in process safety activities, including HAZOP, HAZID, and other process safety assessments.
Provide technical guidance and expertise on complex engineering issues requiring independent analysis, sound judgment, and professional decision‑making.

REQUIREMENTS:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Chemical Engineering.
Minimum of eight to ten (8–10) years of relevant process engineering experience.
Demonstrated experience executing and leading FEED (Front End Engineering Design) projects; LNG project experience is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated design engineering experience gained within a major EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction) organization rather than an operating or production facility.
Proficiency in industry‑standard process engineering and simulation tools, including Aspen HYSYS, Aspen Plus, and PipeSim.
Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and multiple stakeholders.

title: Donor Specialist (SAT)
description:
Title:

Donor Specialist (SAT)

Belong. Connect. Grow. With KBR

KBR is seeking a Donor Specialist to support our SPARC Program for KBR’s Science and Space division. The SPARC program (Service Personnel Advancing Research on CTE) seeks to: 1) Provide education to service members, veterans, and their families on brain donation; 2) Register individuals for participation in the Brain Donation Awareness Registry; and 3) Recover whole specimens, process, and prepare for shipping using appropriate methods. The goal of this program is to support research that is ongoing at the Uniformed Services University’s Brain Tissue Repository related to military brain injury and chronic traumatic encephalopathy. This is an onsite position, rotating between various partner locations each day.

The Donor Specialist will be on-call on a rotating and regular basis and must be available to work nights, weekends, and holidays with previously scheduled on-call shifts.


The preponderance of duties and work time of the Peer Family Educator will be focused on:

Approaching and educating medically competent military members and veterans about the potential to become a brain donor at time of their death, and about the opportunity for them to participate in the Brain Donation Awareness Registry.

Lead and implement all aspects of community partner engagement, stakeholder coordination, and direct interactions with service members and veterans for assigned commands.

Establish and support regional community partnership and outreach events initiatives to strengthen engagement efforts.

Approaching and educating families of potential donors about brain donation at the time of death of their military or veteran family member.

Serving as the primary point of contact to be notified about potential donors and answering questions from families, healthcare workers, funeral home workers, or individuals who would like to know more about the donation program.

Screening donors, registering study participants, and coordinating with local coroners, medical examiners, tissue transport providers, to facilitate brain donation for research.

Collaborating with Peer/Family Educators on recruitment activities.

Performing this work under general supervision where discretion is required, such as in the homes of military members, veterans, and their family members; in the rooms of patients in healthcare facilities; and in funeral homes.
 

On an as needed basis, ancillary duties in tissue recovery will also be performed.  Such tissue recovery duties will generally be performed in mortuaries, funeral homes, medical examiner’s facilities, and healthcare facilities. The Peer Family Educator may perform such duties in a solo role with no direct onsite supervision.  Examples of duties will typically include:

Verifying donor identity

Reviewing next of kin consent and chain of custody documentation

Assisting local dieners, coroners, and pathologists with donated specimens

Completion of documents and records for each donation

Sectioning and processing the tissue according to the protocols of the project

Preparing the specimens for shipping

Coordinating the transport of the body following tissue recovery.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Protecting the rights and welfare of all human research participants involved in research in accordance with federal regulations and sponsoring agency policies and procedures

Adhering to and supporting all Federal regulations and DoD policies and procedures instituted to safeguard protected health information (PHI)

Assuring that all key personnel involved in human research have completed the required education for the protection of human research participants

Developing materials and tools necessary to appropriately train individuals involved in the conduct of the study around issues related to (but not limited to) protocol requirements, schedule of visits, execution of research plan

Attending investigator meetings as required or requested

Preparing other study materials as requested, including but not limited to, informed consent document, case report forms (CRFs), enrollment logs, and study data

Assuring that the study complies with all terms and conditions

Coordinating participant tests and procedures, including interviewing families about the medical history of the tissue donor

Maintaining adequate inventory of study supplies

Maintaining effective and ongoing communication with sponsor, research participants and supervisor during the course of the study

Preparing and submitting any modifications to the scientific protocol

Day-to-day activities of the study including problem solving, communication and protocol management

Promptly reports any unanticipated problems

REQUIRED EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE:

To qualify, candidates must have:

 A bachelor’s degree plus at least 2 years of experience in human subject research, tissue donation, professional clinical laboratory work, nursing, paramedic/military medic, or related similar experience, or 

An associate’s degree in a related field plus at least four years of job-related substantive experience in human subject research, tissue donation, professional clinical laboratory work, nursing, paramedic/military medic, or similar related experience.

In lieu of a degree, 10 years of related experience may be considered.

PREFERRED EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE:

 Prior experience working in military environments and interacting with service member personnel and their families.

 Ability to speak, read, and write in Spanish.

 Experience in the field of tissue or organ donation.

description:
Title:

Senior Operations Research Analyst

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

KBR is seeking a Senior Operations Research Analyst (ORSA) to join our team at Schriever SFB in Colorado Springs, CO. Active TS/SCI clearance required.

Successful candidates should have a strong understanding of the development and implementation of mathematical and statistical models to solve various problems across multiple domains.  Experience and familiarity with the space domain is preferred.

Responsibilities:

Technical leadership responsibility with oversight of projects which use: applied mathematics, operations research, data analytics, modeling and simulation, and decision analysis
Determining the level of analytic rigor required for analysis based on the complexity of the mission area being assessed and the uncertainties of the supporting data
Understanding customer requirements, adjusting analytical efforts to meet those requirements, and effectively communicating results
Ability to coordinate with senior managers and decision makers to identify and solve a variety of problems and to clarify management objectives
Work as part of a contractor team working alongside a broader team of government and contract staff

 Required Skills and Experience:

Bachelor of Science degree in operations research, systems engineering, or related technical field
10+ years of experience
Design of experiments experience
Ability to lead a team of highly skilled analysts on projects with notable risk and complexity.
Develops and implements new processes/procedures as needed. Provides direction/guidance as required.
Strong quantitative and analytic abilities to integrate and analyze data
Technical skill in operations research, modeling and simulation, computer science, big-data analytics, or similar disciplines
Ability to effectively communicate complex concepts to audiences of varying backgrounds
Willingness to learn new technical and management domains

This role includes representing KBR in technical discussions, conferences, and meetings to address critical technical questions and to engage with key engineers and officials from client, partner, and regulatory organizations.

Functional job responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

Serve as a Process Engineer supporting grassroots and revamp engineering projects for LNG production facilities, including utilities, liquefaction, and pre-treatment units.
Execute process engineering work for large- and medium-sized projects, or discrete areas within major projects, in compliance with applicable industry codes, standards, and best practices.
Develop and deliver core process engineering outputs, including process simulations and modeling; heat, material, and utility balances; process flow diagrams (PFDs); piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs); hydraulic calculations; flare and relief analyses; and process design parameters.
Perform equipment design and/or rating for process equipment such as vessels, columns, heat exchangers, pumps, and related systems.
Conduct process studies, including process optimization, flare and relief systems, blowdown and depressurizing systems, vent systems, cooling and heating media studies, utility system sizing, and produced water treatment evaluations.
Participate in and support process safety activities, including HAZOP, HAZID, and other process safety assessments.
Provide technical leadership and guidance on complex process engineering issues, applying independent analysis and professional judgment.

Required Education, Experience, & Skills:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Chemical Engineering (Mechanical Engineering considered with relevant process engineering experience).
Minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in process engineering, preferably within a major EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction) organization rather than an operating/production facility.
Demonstrated experience executing FEED (Front End Engineering Design) projects; prior LNG project experience is strongly preferred.
Proficiency in industry-standard process engineering software, including Aspen HYSYS, Aspen Plus, and PipeSim, for process simulation, analysis, and design.
Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary engineering teams and with project stakeholders.
