description:
Title:

Classified Systems Administrator

KBR — Delivering Solutions, Changing the World.

KBR is a global leader in delivering technology-driven, mission-critical, and sustainable solutions that truly matter. For over a century, we have powered bold missions across defense, space, industry, and government through our two core business lines Mission Technology Solutions and Sustainable Technology Solutions. With nearly 38,000 talented people operating in more than 80 countries, we thrive on a culture built on safety, integrity, and teamwork. At KBR, we empower our people to solve the world’s toughest challenges and create lasting value for communities and the planet. We don’t just deliver results, we deliver game-changing solutions, innovative technology, deep domain expertise, and cutting-edge technologies.

KBR is seeking a Classified Systems Administrator to join our Corporate IT team in Huntsville, AL. This role is responsible for supporting the administration, configuration, and sustainment of classified information systems within a secure classified environment. You will oversee and maintain hardware, software, operating systems, and peripheral equipment including servers, desktops, zero clients, storage devices, network gear, and virtualization infrastructure while ensuring system availability, data integrity, and compliance with basic security and recovery procedures such as backups and restorations. Working closely with cross-functional IT teams, you will apply standard system administration concepts to analyze issues, troubleshoot systems, and implement effective solutions. This is a full-time, on-site position.

Key Responsibilities

Administer, maintain, and support classified computer systems hardware, network gear, software, information systems, and peripheral equipment including servers, desktops, zero clients, storage devices, and virtualization infrastructure
Install, configure, upgrade, and maintain data systems and operating environments including Windows, Linux, VMware, and SQL Server while performing routine system maintenance such as patching and system backups
Administer infrastructure components including servers, zero clients, databases, malware protection solutions, HBSS, and syslog servers to ensure secure and reliable operations
Troubleshoot and resolve complex technical issues under general supervision, applying detailed knowledge of system administration principles and industry best practices
Utilize experience and problem-solving skills to develop, document, and improve system administration processes, and implement system and process upgrades to enhance functionality and address security findings
Prepare, author, and review configuration change requests and actively participate in configuration change review board meetings to ensure effective change management
Identify potential risks, vulnerabilities, or inefficiencies within system configurations and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies
Ensure compliance with data security policies, applicable legal and regulatory requirements, and DoD cybersecurity program implementation plans in accordance with DoD directives and Risk Management Framework requirements

Basic Qualifications

Education & Experience:

B.S. Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Systems Engineering, or related field and 2+ years of prior relevant experience. Additional relevant experience may be accepted in lieu of a degree
Citizenship & Clearance: Must be a US Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret clearance.
Certifications: Must have CompTIA Security+, CASP, or CISSP certifications or be able to obtain and maintain

Technical Expertise:

Knowledge of operating system functions, security policies, and technical security safeguards
Knowledge of NIST 800-53, DoD 5205.07 Series, Risk Management Framework, and Joint SAP Implementation Guide requirements
Knowledge of performance monitoring and tuning, system upgrades and patching, backup and recovery, as well as troubleshooting and problem resolution
Experience with Active Directory and Group Policy Objects
Experience working independently and as part of a team in researching data and developing analytical techniques and methodologies
Ability to move, rack, stack, and install physical equipment by lifting up to 25 lbs

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Windows user account management, administration, and access controls
Systems Administration experience supporting United States Government classified environments
Experience applying DISA STIGs and resolving security vulnerabilities
Experience with PowerShell scripting
Fundamental understanding of the OSI model
Fundamental understanding of authentication mechanisms including Kerberos, LDAP, and NTLM, and use of necessary tools to troubleshoot them
Understanding of technology areas including Active Directory, DHCP, DNS, Group Policy, and WSUS
Knowledge of network protocols including TCP/IP, UDP, SMTP, NFS, FTP, Telnet, and SSH
Installation and configuration experience of Microsoft Windows 10 or 11 workstations and peripherals
Experience with network-attached storage or storage area networks
Experience performing audits of key IT components to ensure compliance with established standards, policies, and configuration guidelines

Additional Compensation: KBR may offer bonuses, commissions, or other forms of compensation to certain job titles or levels per internal policy or contractual designation. Additional compensation may be in the form of a sign-on bonus, relocation benefits, short-term incentives, long-term incentives, or discretionary payments for exceptional performance.

Benefits: KBR offers a selection of competitive lifestyle benefits, which could include a 401K plan with company match, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, flexible spending account, disability, paid time off, or flexible work schedule. Maintain oversight of all supported events and provides recommendations for manning, integration of simulations and simulators, and overall exercise design and training environment.

Provide technical and tactical expertise in implementing the 32d AAMDC Commander’s training guidance by helping to develop strategies and supporting the JELC through planning, preparing, executing, and assessing training exercises. 

Provides Knowledge Management expertise and develops procedures to capture and archive lessons learned, best practices, and pertinent data developed throughout the JELC, including exercise design and execution documents and support information.

Develop, refine, and maintain standard operating procedures and best practices that support 32d AAMDC LSCO exercises.

Title:

Environmental/Energy Manager (Contingency Hire)

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary

KBR will help support the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps at Naval Station Mayport and the Marine Corps Support Facility at Blount Island (MCSF-BI). Our goal is to help their missions run smoothly and successfully. Let’s work together to make a positive impact and achieve results.

Naval Station Mayport is located along the St. Johns River in Duval County, Florida. It covers 3,409 acres and is the third-largest naval surface fleet area in the U.S. Since it opened in 1942, it has become a key hub with a harbor for 34 ships and a runway for most Department of Defense aircraft.

MCSF-BI covers 911 acres on the eastern side of Blount Island, plus an extra 333 acres nearby. This facility is vital for keeping Marine Air-Ground Task Forces ready. MCSF-BI has a deep-water slipway and direct access to the Atlantic, allowing for quick loading and unloading of the largest Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) ships. This helps deploy combat vehicles and supplies.

Support and/or perform sensitivity analyses, trade-off studies, and risk assessments using simulation outputs.
Provide technical review and validation of M&S results against doctrine, historical data, and/or real-world operations.
Author and deliver technical reports, white papers, and decision briefs for senior military and civilian leaders.

To promote KBR brand awareness and technology leadership, exercise active thought leadership through speaking, writing, and personal communications.

Title:

Account Manager

KBR’s Mission Engineering Division partners with the U.S. Navy and Joint Forces to address their most complex and time-sensitive operational challenges. Our teams integrate mission engineering, rapid prototyping, and digital transformation to accelerate the delivery of decisive capabilities that strengthen the Nation’s defense posture.

Through our focused collaboration with NSWC Crane Division, we align our efforts with the Division’s strategic vision and evolving mission priorities to advance innovation across critical technology domains. Through close collaboration with the NavalX Midwest Tech Bridge, WestGate@Crane Technology Park, the Applied Research Institute (ARI), and the Crane Regional Defense Group (CRDG), we help connect the region’s innovation ecosystem with KBR’s global engineering and integration expertise — turning emerging technologies into operational advantage.

The Account Manager will play a pivotal role in driving strategic growth and mission alignment for KBR’s Mission Engineering Division, leading engagement and capture efforts focused on NSWC Crane Division and its regional innovation ecosystem. This leader will identify, shape, and secure opportunities that advance Crane’s priorities, develop and execute integrated account strategies, and expand KBR’s presence across Crane’s technical organizations and technology transition initiatives. Serving as a trusted connector and advocate, the Account Manager will bridge NSWC Crane’s mission objectives with KBR’s engineering, prototyping, and digital-integration capabilities. Success in this role requires close collaboration with Crane leadership, regional innovation partners, and internal KBR technical, capture, and operations teams to deliver timely, mission-ready solutions that enhance the Navy’s and Joint Force’s operational advantage.

This position requires a minimum of 25 % travel.

Roles and Responsibilities

Serve as the voice of the customer: Act as the primary liaison between NSWC Crane and KBR’s internal teams, ensuring Crane’s mission needs and priorities are fully represented in KBR’s engineering and capture strategies.
Engage the regional innovation ecosystem: Build and sustain relationships with organizations that drive Crane’s innovation mission — including the NavalX Midwest Tech Bridge, WestGate@Crane Technology Park, the Applied Research Institute (ARI), and the Crane Regional Defense Group (CRDG) — to strengthen collaboration and accelerate technology transition.
Shape and capture opportunities: Identify, shape, and pursue opportunities under Other Transaction Authorities (OTAs) such as S²MARTS, EMC², and LEAN Power, as well as through traditional NAVSEA contracting authorities.
Promote innovation and prototyping: Support the development of white papers, CSOs, and technology demonstrations that advance KBR’s role as a rapid problem-solving partner to Crane.
Maintain an internal engagement plan: Track leadership changes, organizational shifts, and department-level focus areas across Crane’s expanding structure; ensure contact management, visit schedules, and engagement reporting are current.
Engage NSWC Crane leadership: Proactively engage senior leaders across NSWC Crane to validate priorities, refine problem statements, and shape opportunities and prototypes aligned to the Division’s evolving needs.
Coordinate KBR internal alignment: Translate NSWC Crane leadership guidance into concrete actions — synchronizing KBR’s investments, R&D activities, and technical capabilities with capture and delivery plans.
Develop and execute account strategy: Create customer-specific plans that integrate business development, engineering, and operations to deliver a consistent message and measurable results.
Lead market awareness efforts: Coordinate with industry and consortium members to gather insight on upcoming acquisition strategies, program timing, and contracting pathways.
Assess customer trends: Provide senior leadership with 3–5-year horizon analysis on customer direction, technology priorities, and partnership opportunities to inform capture campaigns.
Monitor and strengthen performance: Conduct customer assessments on current contract and task performance, ensuring internal teams maintain responsiveness, quality, and customer trust.
Achieve measurable outcomes: Drive growth in pipeline quality, awards, and partnerships that advance KBR’s NSWC Crane account objectives and Mission Engineering Division growth targets.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a technical, business, or related discipline.
Minimum of 10 years of experience supporting the Department of Defense or U.S. Navy; direct experience with NSWC Crane Division or other NSWC divisions strongly preferred.
Demonstrated understanding of government acquisition processes, OTAs, and NAVSEA contracting authorities.
Proven ability to build and sustain relationships with government, industry, and academic partners across complex organizations.
Familiarity with federal budget, investment, and technology-transition processes that shape Crane’s innovation and research, development and acquisition initiatives.
U.S. citizenship with ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a technical or business discipline — or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Established network within the NSWC Crane Division enterprise, particularly among technical departments, Tech Bridge leadership, and regional innovation partners.
Demonstrated success leading capture, program development, and partnership initiatives within DoD R&D or systems engineering environments.
Strong communication and influencing skills, capable of articulating complex technical capabilities in operationally relevant terms.
Proven ability to integrate internal teams and external stakeholders to deliver mission-driven, innovative solutions.
Track record of growth achievement — developing qualified pipelines, securing new awards, and expanding customer relationships over time.
Experience working with multiple Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) divisions, demonstrating familiarity with their missions, stakeholders, and operational environments.

Travel: This position requires a minimum of 25 % travel.

KBR’s Missile, Aviation, and Ground Systems (MAGS) division delivers mission engineering solutions for critical U.S. Army programs, specializing in aviation and ground systems, integrated air and missile defense, and threat and target systems. Job Summary

The STARE Lead Threat Systems Engineer identifies and assesses threat system characteristics, capabilities and tactics that drive sensor requirements and operational performance within an integrated air and missile defense force. In this case “threat” refers mainly to the systems the sensors must detect/track (e.g. tactical ballistic ballistic/aeroballistics missiles, cruise missiles, unmanned aerial systems, and tactical air-to-surface missiles to include anti-radiation missiles). Threat also includes aspects of the operational environment such as electronic attack and countermeasures.  The Threat Lead will routinely interface with STARE Functional Staff elements, STARE Leadership, and the various Product office threat leads/key engineers. This position also requires the STARE Lead Threat System Engineer to have/develop an understanding of the role, functions and capabilities of STARE products within the operational architecture of Army air and missile defense force. The STARE Threat Lead is the primary coordination point with external Threat SMEs within the other PEO Component Project Offices including but not limited to the Integrated Fires Threat System Engineering Group. The STARE Threat Lead external interfaces include Army Threat Support Agencies, threat and target model/simulation development teams, test agencies, and National Intelligence Agencies.

Roles and Responsibilities 

Coordinating with STARE SE and Functional staff and Product Office threat leads to identify and define threat support requirements
Support Test planning including identification of relevant threat and test target characteristics and test scenario development
Communicate current and evolving threat status/operational capabilities as it relates to STARE product development strategies and requirements at STARE and Product levels, function as the threat SME
Assess and identify efficiencies for threat product development and actions across the STARE/PEO portfolio
Participate in working groups with Integrated Fires or other offices within the AMD Portfolio to develop and coordinate threat modeling and simulation (M&S) requirements; Represent STARE in Integrated Fires (IF) Systems Engineering Threat Group and other IF threat related meetings/working groups
Work with STARE SE/T&E to establish Threat/Target M&S need dates and ensure prioritization and integration in IF level threat M&S tools or data sets production/delivery schedules
Responsibilities include working/guiding verification, validation, and accreditation between STARE products and intelligence production centers/Army Threat agencies
The STARE Lead Threat Systems Engineer provides STARE level interface with designated Army Threat Support Agencies as well as the National Intelligence Centers and Warfighter community
Facilitate/advise Product offices development of critical intelligence parameters, VOLTs and Life-Cycle Mission Data Plans.

Basic Qualifications 

Must have an active SECRET clearance with ability to obtain a TOP SECRET/SCI clearance
A Bachelor of Science in engineering, physics, or mathematics from an ABET accredited institution is required.
Experience in using/developing high fidelity threat models (e.g. kinematic performance, signature characteristics, and lethality modeling
5+ years’ experience required; Must be a self-starter with the ability to work independently with minimal direction

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Air and Missile Defense Systems and/or related sensors
Experience in high fidelity threat/target model development or air defense high fidelity performance assessment process
Active or very recent TS/SCI access
Threat analysis experience in support of requirements development, test design or force-on-force operational assessment

description:
Title:

SATCOM Systems Integration Strategist

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

KBR (formerly LinQuest) is the prime contractor on the MSEIT contract. By applying to this position, you are in consideration for KBR employment. However, you also have the option to be hired by one of our subcontractor teammates.

KBR is seeking a SATCOM Systems Integration Strategist to support the MSEIT contract at Space Systems Command (SSC). This role bridges the gap between users, stakeholders, architects, and software development teams to define, prioritize, and integrate future satellite communications (SATCOM) capabilities across the U.S. Space Force enterprise.

The SATCOM Systems Integration Strategist focuses on understanding mission and user needs, translating them into architecturally consistent and operationally relevant capabilities, and ensuring that new developments align with the Space Force’s north-star vision for integrated SATCOM operations. This position emphasizes user-centered design and mission effectiveness, ensuring future capabilities improve operational agility and enterprise coherence across space and ground segments.

The MILSATCOM Systems Engineering, Integration, and Test (MSEIT) effort provides leading edge Systems Engineering & Integration (SE&I) for the US Space Force’s Space Systems Center (SSC). We support the Space Force’s acquisition of state of the art satellite communications systems, providing global secure, survivable, and protected communications for our nation’s warfighters. We seek technical individuals who will thrive in a highly collaborative work environment of small teams, using the most modern tools and methodologies to tackle the challenges of integrating complex space and ground communications systems.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Key Responsibilities:

Capability Definition & Integration: Identify, refine, and document stakeholder and user needs; define capabilities and integration pathways that align with enterprise SATCOM architecture and modernization efforts.

Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with operators, mission owners, and program sponsors to identify operational gaps and shape requirements into feasible, impactful solutions.

Strategic Alignment: Ensure proposed capabilities are consistent with SSC’s SATCOM enterprise architecture, data strategies, and digital modernization goals.

User-Centered Design: Lead discussions that move from user-driven requests to user-centered, mission-focused solutions that enhance interoperability, efficiency, and resiliency.

Cross-Discipline Coordination: Partner with SE&I, cyber, DevOps, and software teams to ensure technical feasibility, traceability, and integration across space, ground, and network layers.

Program Integration: Translate high-level capability objectives into actionable program deliverables compatible with Agile or incremental development cycles.

Communication & Roadmapping: Develop and present SATCOM capability roadmaps, strategy briefs, and integration concepts to government and contractor leadership.

Work Environment:

Location: On-site
Travel Requirements: Minimal
Working Hours: Standard

Qualifications:

Required:

Ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret clearance required for this position
Bachelor’s degree in a technical field (e.g., Engineering, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or related discipline).
8–12 years of professional experience in systems engineering, integration strategy, or capability development.
Demonstrated experience within SATCOM, space systems, or mission operations domains.
Proven ability to translate operational needs into structured, technically aligned, and strategically prioritized capability definitions.
Excellent communication, facilitation, and analytical skills, with experience interfacing across government, contractor, and operational teams.
Familiarity with DoD acquisition, SE&I, and space enterprise integration environments.

Desired:

Experience supporting Space Systems Command (SSC), Space Operations Command (SpOC), or other U.S. Space Force or DoD programs.
Familiarity with Agile frameworks (Scrum, SAFe, Kanban) and Agile program environments.
Understanding of Agile scoping and MVP definition techniques such as MoSCoW, BORIS, Framing and Discovery, or similar prioritization methodologies.
Exposure to DevOps, cloud-native, or Kubernetes-based architectures and modern SATCOM software ecosystems.
Experience applying user-centered design and human-systems integration principles in mission software or command-and-control environments. Proficiency with collaboration and visualization tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Miro, or equivalent).
Systems Engineering Professional (INCOSE CSEP), SAFe certification, or comparable credential.
TS/SCI eligibility preferred

Title:

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! 

Program Summary

KBR will help support the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps at Naval Station Mayport and the Marine Corps Support Facility at Blount Island. Our goal is to help their missions run smoothly and successfully. Let’s work together to make a positive impact and achieve results.

Naval Station Mayport is located along the St. Johns River in Duval County, Florida. It covers 3,409 acres and is the third-largest naval surface fleet area in the U.S. Since it opened in 1942, it has become a key hub with a harbor for 34 ships and a runway for most Department of Defense aircraft.

MCSF-BI covers 911 acres on the eastern side of Blount Island, plus an extra 333 acres nearby. This facility is vital for keeping Marine Air-Ground Task Forces ready. MCSF-BI has a deep-water slipway and direct access to the Atlantic, allowing for quick loading and unloading of the largest Maritime Prepositioning Force (MPF) ships. This helps deploy combat vehicles and supplies.

Job Summary

The Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO) is a Level 1, mandatory Key Personnel position whose primary duty is to prepare, implement, and enforce the Contractor's safety program, specifically the Accident Prevention Plan (APP), for all work performed at NAVSTA Mayport, MCSF-BI, and outlying areas. The SSHO must be on-site at all times when work is being performed to administer the safety program and accepted APP. This role ensures full compliance with the US Army Corps of Engineers Safety and Health Requirements Manual, EM 385-1-1, and 29 CFR 1926.16

Please note: This position is contingent upon award.

Roles and Responsibilities   

The SSHO is responsible for producing, implementing, and enforcing an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) for assigned program, in accordance with the Company’s Safety and Health Program.

Attend pre-work meetings and produce job-specific APP and Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs), in accordance with Company’s Safety and Health Program.

The SSHO is on-duty when work is being performed, overseeing and managing project construction crews, and ensuring that all personnel are following proper safety rules and regulations.

Work as member of the project team, including subcontractors, to ensure implementation and continuous monitoring and enforcement of the provisions of the project EM385-1-1, APP and AHA’s.

Provide professional support to federal government contracts through health and safety inspection and oversight.

Prepare comprehensive reports daily of safety inspections and complete all safety related documentation and paperwork.

Coordinate response to on-site emergencies and interface with off-site and on-site emergency response entities.

Conduct safety training, including new employee orientations or refresher trainings, and on-the-spot training to all personnel.

Work with management team to develop new safety policies, refine existing policies, and modify design requirements and draft construction-related specifications.

Ensure that the requirements of 29 CFR 1926.16 are met for Contract requirements.

Ensure that they themselves or an equally qualified Designated Representative/alternate shall always be on-site when work is being performed to implement and administer the Contractor's safety program and government-accepted Accident Prevention Plan.

Conduct and report mishap investigations and complete required accident reports.

Use and maintain OSHA's Form 300 to log work-related injuries and illnesses occurring on the project site for Prime Contractors and subcontractors and make them available to the Contracting Officer upon request.

Establish a Safety and Occupational Health (SOH) Deficiency Tracking System that lists and monitors outstanding deficiencies until resolution.

Maintain a list of hazardous chemicals on-site and their material Safety Data Sheets (SDS).

Maintain a weekly list of high-hazard activities involving energy, equipment, excavation, entry into confined space, and elevation, and be prepared to discuss details during QC Meetings.

Provide and keep a record of site safety orientation and indoctrination for Contractor employees, subcontractor employees, and site visitors.

Basic Qualifications  

Fulfill all pre-requisite qualifications, training, and experience as described in EM 385-1-1.

Ability to serve as primary SSHO for NAVSTA Mayport and MCSF-BI, with flexibility to act as alternate for sister sites.

5 years of Construction Industry safety experience on similar DOD or BOS projects in supervising or managing general industry or construction programs (managing safety programs, processes or conducting hazard analyses and developing controls).

A minimum of an OSHA 30-hour Construction Safety Certification (within past 5 years)

Current First Aid/CPR/AED Training

Must be able to pass DOD security clearance for base access

High School Diploma

Must have a Bachelor’s degree in Safety, Engineering (any field), Industrial Hygiene, Health Physics, Fire Prevention, or other related scientific fields, based on a four-year course of study from a U.S. or U.K. accredited college or university.

Must be fluent in English

Must be a U.S. Citizen.

Must possess passport book with at least 15 months of remaining validity AND with at least 6 blank visa/stamp pages remaining

Must possess driver’s license with at least 6 months of remaining validity

Extensive knowledge and experience of the USACE Safety Manual EM385-1-1;

Must pass drug screen, criminal and background check.

Must maintain competency in IAW EM385-1-1 requirements.

Must be trained and qualified to conduct Mishap Investigations per OPNAVINST 5100.23 series and OPNAVINST 5102.1 series.

Preferred qualifications:

CSP or CHST certification preferred

The Hazardous Material (HAZMAT) Coordinator is responsible for managing, tracking, and ensuring compliance of all hazardous materials and waste operations on a U.S. military installation. Roles and Responsibilities

Maintain accountability and inventory control of all hazardous materials and waste throughout their lifecycle—from procurement through disposal.
Conduct inspections and audits of hazardous materials storage areas, accumulation points, and satellite collection sites to ensure compliance with applicable regulations (EPA, OSHA, RCRA, DOT, and DoD directives).

Develop, implement, and maintain Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS/SDS) systems and ensure accessibility to all personnel handling hazardous materials.

Support waste minimization programs and pollution prevention initiatives to reduce environmental impact and operational cost.
Conduct and document spill response activities, investigations, and corrective actions.
Coordinate with the EHS Manager to prepare and submit environmental compliance reports as required by DoD, EPA, or state agencies.

High school diploma or equivalent required; associate or Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Safety, or related field preferred.
Minimum of 3–5 years of experience in hazardous material or waste management, preferably within a military or industrial environment.

Demonstrated proficiency with the Hazardous Material Management System (HMMS) database for waste tracking and documentation.
Working knowledge of EPA, OSHA, RCRA, DOT, and DoD 4160.21-M requirements.
Strong understanding of spill prevention, response procedures, and environmental reporting requirements.
Excellent organizational and communication skills with the ability to interface across multiple functional areas.
Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and data entry/reporting tools.

HAZWOPER 40-Hour Certification

US Citizen

Root cause analysis and corrective action on database issues.

Project Planner

Position Summary

The Project Planner is a key member of the Task Planning and Controls Office (TPCO), which is responsible for the planning and execution of all ​task order-based projects under the Technical Support Services Contract (TSSC). The Project Planner collaborates with task managers to build resource‑loaded schedules, manage resource allocation for forecasting and cost reporting, and ensure accurate data, deliverable tracking, and variance analysis for leadership decisions. Scheduling & Planning

Provide regular status updates to task managers and stakeholders
Support scope definition and baseline management
Apply resource‑loaded scheduling to forecast labor, materials, and cost performance

Cost & Financial Reporting

Prepare and deliver monthly financial reports and variance analysis
Assist task managers with task plan preparation and modifications
Track monthly deliverable status and project performance
Track travel and non-labor costs

Support change control and compliance with agency standards and regulations

Excellent communication and organizational skills

About Company

"Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

The KBR team delivers future-forward science, technology and engineering solutions and mission-critical services that help governments and companies around the world accomplish their most important objectives, while also helping achieve their sustainability goals.

KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design and engineering capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets."

Job Purpose


The Facilities Maintenance Manager is responsible for the planning, leadership, and execution of preventive and corrective maintenance across all facilities supporting the KBR-Majnoon Project in Basra. This role ensures reliable, safe, and cost-effective operation of buildings, utilities, and technical systems (mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and structural), manages maintenance teams and contractors, oversees asset management and compliance, and collaborates with project leadership to support uninterrupted site activities.

Job Responsibilities

Develop and implement the facilities maintenance strategy, including preventive maintenance programs, predictive maintenance where applicable, and lifecycle planning for all plant and site infrastructure.
Lead, mentor, and manage maintenance teams (technicians, electricians, custodial staff, and contractors); assign work, monitor performance, and ensure a safe and compliant work environment.
Manage maintenance budgets, spare parts inventory, procurement, and vendor contracts; optimize cost efficiency while maintaining high service quality.
Oversee building systems (HVAC, lighting, electrical distribution, water supply, wastewater, fire protection, security systems, elevators/escalators, and other site utilities) for reliability and compliance with local regulations and company standards.
Plan and supervise facility upgrades, refurbishment projects, and expansions; coordinate with project management, logistics, and security.
Ensure adherence to Health, Safety, Environment and Quality (HSE/QA) standards; conduct risk assessments, incident investigations, and implement corrective actions.
Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for maintenance activities, inspections, and emergency procedures; drive continuous improvement initiatives.
Monitor and report on key performance indicators (uptime, mean time between failures, maintenance cost per square meter, energy consumption, and safety metrics); prepare regular management reports.
Manage utility consumption and energy efficiency programs; identify opportunities for savings and sustainability improvements.
Ensure compliance with local labor laws, visa/work permit requirements, and company policies; coordinate with authorities as needed.
Maintain accurate records for asset inventories, maintenance histories, warranties, permits, and compliance documentation.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Facilities Management, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, Civil/Building Services, or a closely related discipline).
Minimum 15 years of experience in facilities maintenance, preferably within large-scale industrial, construction, or multinational environments.
Proven experience managing maintenance operations for complex facilities, including mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems; strong vendor management and contract administration skills.
Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, assets, and maintenance programs in challenging or remote locations.

Technical Skills

Facilities Maintenance Planning and Preventive/Mpredictive Maintenance
Building Services (HVAC, Electrical, Plumbing, Fire Protection, Water/Wastewater)
Asset Management and Lifecycle Planning
Vendor Management and Contract Administration
Budgeting, Cost Control, and Spare Parts Management
Safety, Health, and Environmental Compliance
Maintenance Scheduling Software and Data Analytics
Energy Management and Efficiency Initiatives
Emergency Response and Incident Management

Location and Baseline Context

Onsite role based in Basra, Iraq. The Facilities Maintenance Manager should operate effectively in a dynamic, multi-national industrial setting with adherence to KBR-Majnoon project safety and security standards.

Title:

Image Scientist - Journeyman

KBR is seeking a Image Scientist to support government customers in the Washington Metropolitan Area. The Image Scientist (Journeyman) provides expertise in imagery science, imagery analysis, and photogrammetry that enables the detailed technical analysis of GEOINT product quality. The journeyman imagery scientists will provide oversight and continuity of knowledge to the team, as well as support the broad range of assessments and assessment tasks both independent and with senior guidance. This individual will also support algorithm development and validation related to imagery science tasks.  

 

Responsibilities: 

 

Provide imagery scientist support through accomplishment of technical reviews, consultations, oversight of proposed and executed GEOINT product quality assessments and studies, and strategic level product quality direction.  

Provide image processing algorithm validation and verification in support of GEOINT product quality assessments or ad hoc customer requests.  

Provide imagery science services and analysis in support of GEOINT product quality assessments for the full range of traditional and non-traditional imaging systems, products, and data formats; sensor fidelity assessment, pixel registration assessment, Tonal Transfer Curve assessments, Relative Edge Response assessment, MTF and Signal to Noise Ratio assessment, and other product quality parameters.  

Support algorithm development in support of imagery science tasks and assessment of various product quality parameters.  

Provide photogrammetric services and engineering in support of the full range of traditional and non-traditional imaging systems and products; assessment of product geolocation accuracy using verified geolocation of a known features, verifying mensuration accuracy through measurement of known objects, calculating ground sample distance, and other photogrammetric analyses as directed.  

Provide imagery analyst support through technical review, consultation, and oversight of proposed and executed product quality assessments and studies, and strategic level product quality direction.  

Provide imagery analyst services in support of GEOINT product quality assessment planning, execution, and results analysis; imagery review, artifact analysis, NIIRS evaluations (absolute NIIRS, delta NIIRS, and ENS NIIRS evaluations), display performance assessments, etc. 

Required Education, Experience, & Skills: 

A minimum of 3 years of experience and a Bachelor of Science degree in image science, remote sensing, earth science, physical science, engineering, or similar engineering/science field.  

Strong Experience with SAR, IR, Spectral, LIDAR, ArcGIS, RSI ENVI, and photogrammetry. 

Experience in applied image processing and scientific analysis of imagery (SAR, IR, Spectral, Lidar, photogrammetry), knowledge of image formation, and associated discipline phenomenology. 

Experience in scientifically processing imagery (SAR, IR, Spectral, Lidar) from Civil and Commercial imaging systems, proficiency with techniques, algorithms, and scientific analysis of associated discipline data processing using RSI ENVI. 

Experience with GOTS applications such as FSTK and AGITK. 

Ability to work in a very dynamic and demanding work environment. 

Must be a self-starter, able to operate with little guidance. 

Must be a self-starter, able to operate with little guidance.

title: Senior Acquisition Analyst
description:
Title:

Senior Acquisition Analyst 

KBR’s Mission Engineering Division delivers complex technical solutions and expert support to the U.S. Department of War, specializing in modeling and simulation, cyber transformation, air vehicle mission integration, and lifecycle support. As a trusted partner with a proven history in mission technology, KBR collaborates closely with clients to develop innovative and effective solutions. With a strong ethical framework, KBR prioritizes data security, privacy, and responsible information management to ensure mission success.  

We are seeking a Senior Acquisition Analyst with an expert understanding of Department of War (DoW) acquisition and program management procedures and policies and a basic understanding of Counter-Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-sUAS) technologies to support the DoN’s Office of the Chief of Naval Operations (OPNAV) in Arlington, VA (Pentagon).

  

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Analyst will support the OPNAV N4I C-UAS Team, and may directly interact and support OPNAV Installations and Logistics (N4) Director, Deputy Director and other N4 staff members by applying acquisition subject matter expertise to the OPNAV planning, programming, budgeting, and execution of C-sUAS/CuXS developmental projects. Analyst will also apply program management subject matter expertise to conduct regular program management reviews of active developmental projects and to conduct reviews of new project proposals and to staff those proposals through the process for approval. The analyst will coordinate directly with stakeholders in the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Joint Staff, the Services, and other DoD and U.S. Government organizations.
Working closely with OPNAV N4 military and civilian leads and executing their guidance.    Maintaining situational awareness of current and developing UAS threats and C-sUAS solutions and understanding and following DoD standard operating procedures (SOPs) and policies.  Maintaining situational awareness of and following applicable DoD acquisition and program management procedures and policies.  
Coordinating and leading regular program management reviews of active (currently funded) research, development, test, and evaluation (RDT&E) projects to develop C-sUAS solutions.  Coordinating and leading corrective actions for underperforming projects.  
Coordinating and leading annual reviews of proposals for RDT&E projects to develop C-sUAS materiel solutions.  Identifying acquisition courses of action (COAs) for new RDT&E proposals and staffing them through the process for approval.   Coordinating with the DON Resource Management team and the supporting acquisition organization for accurate and timely reporting of project budget execution for the current fiscal year (FY) and planning for future FYs.  
Providing project management coordination and leadership for DON-led projects.  Coordinating operational planning teams and working groups with staff and external stakeholders as needed for special subjects/issues.  
Coordinating staffing actions and taskers in accordance with OPNAV SOPs and policies.  Preparing written products (emails, presentations, info papers, reports, and executive summaries) based on military and civilian lead guidance in accordance with OPNAV procedures and policies.  Support the Project Objective Memorandum (POM) and budget formulation process as directed by the resource sponsor.Prepare, process, and respond to tasking received via Enterprise Task Management Software Solution (ETMS2) as well as generate tasking assignments to subordinate commands as required.
Displaying oral and written communication skills and proficiency in Microsoft Office products (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word).  Possess a working understanding of the relationships and responsibilities of the DON, to include the offices of the Secretary of the Navy and Chief of Naval Operations. Answering requests for information from a variety of key stakeholders, including Congress, OSD, and the Services.    

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:  

Must be a US Citizen.
Active Secret level security clearance with the ability to obtain a Top Secret clearance.  
4 years of related work experience.  
Bachelor’s Degree in a STEM or business field, or equivalent experience.   

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

8+ years of related work experience
Active Top Secret security clearance
Master’s Degree is an applicable field

Scheduled Weekly Hours: 40 hours/week

Title:

Field Service Automation Engineer  (Contingency Hire)

Belong, Connect, Grow with KBR! 

Program Summary

The KBR Field Service Automation team installs and maintains automated systems used in industrial or manufacturing settings. They ensure material handling automated equipment, controllers, and software operate efficiently to optimize production processes. Their work often involves troubleshooting on-site, programming PLCs (Programmable Logic Controllers), and integrating new technologies. Additionally, they collaborate with engineering teams and clients to tailor automation solutions to the specific operational needs of our clients.

Job Summary

A Field Service Automation Engineer installs, maintains, and repairs automated equipment at customer sites. They troubleshoot hardware and software issues to ensure systems operate efficiently and with minimal downtime. The role involves frequent travel, hands-on technical work, and direct customer interaction. Regular inspections and system updates are also part of the job to maintain optimal performance.   Job is on site and not remote.

We are seeking flexible, project-ready professionals to join our talent pool for  on-call assignments.  Selected candidates will be engaged on a project-by-project basis. This opportunity is ideal for individuals looking to stay connected, contribute as needed, and be considered for contract or long-term roles as client needs arise.  Assignment times may vary from a few days to several weeks. 

Roles and Responsibilities 

Generate electrical schematics, P&IDs, and sequence of operations.

Conduct SOPs, risk assessments, validation reports, FAT/SAT documentation.

Root cause analysis for equipment and controls failures.

Program, test, and troubleshoot PLCs, HMIs, SCADA systems, and robotics.

Conduct system integration, calibration, and validation of automation equipment.

Monitor the software platform and analyze the data to facilitate efficiency and readiness.

Use dashboards or analytics platforms for downtime/OEE tracking.

Lead control system projects from concept of task to commissioning.

Analyze system data and diagnostics to improve reliability, efficiency, and productivity.

Ensure compliance with safety standards, industry regulations, and internal quality procedures.

Basic Qualifications 

Bachelor’s or Master's degree in electrical engineering, Mechatronics, or related field

Willingness to travel for commissioning and support.

PLC programming (Siemens, Allen-Bradley/Rockwell, Beckhoff, Omron) -- five years field experience.

HMI/SCADA configuration (Wonderware, Ignition, WinCC, FactoryTalk View) -- three years or more experience.

Motion control systems (servo motors, VFDs, stepper systems).

PID tuning and loop control.

Proficiency in industrial Ethernet (EtherNet/IP, Profinet, Modbus TCP/IP).

Fieldbus protocols (CANopen, DeviceNet, Profibus, AS-i).

Network design and diagnostics (VLANs, switches, routers).

Integration with robotic systems (Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, Yaskawa).

Automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS).

Conveyor systems, sorters, pick-to-light/put-to-light systems.

Experience with goods-to-person (GTP) and shuttle systems.

Electrical panel design and wiring (AutoCAD Electrical, EPLAN).

Familiarity with NFPA 70/NEC, UL, CE standards.

Safety systems (Safety PLCs, light curtains, emergency stops, interlocks).

Experience with MES/WMS/WCS integration.

SQL and data logging for performance monitoring.

Preferred Qualifications

Degree or work experience Mechatronics, or related field work

5–8+ years in automated warehouse material handling systems.

Experience in e-commerce or high-throughput logistics environments (e.g., Amazon, Ocado, DHL)

Familiarity with cloud-based automation monitoring or BBMS platforms.

title: Operations Readiness Advisor
description:
Title:

Operations Readiness Advisor

Operations Readiness Advisor
ETEN40 - Technical Professional Advisor

KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets.

The Operations Readiness Advisor (ORA) is a key position in the operational readiness and start up organization. This role will be required to manage several major, and Mods projects readiness and make sure the operational readiness activities are well-identified, managed, and progressed in order to make sure safe and smooth start up takes place within the target dates as per each project timeline. 

This role is responsible for managing various interfaces with multiple teams within projects, operations, and other supporting functions within the organization. 

This is a site-based role which will require frequent travels to work sites. Travel from one worksite to the other is also part of the role. 

Operations Readiness Advisor (ORA) to provide technical support and operating guidance for equipment and systems prior to and after handover to Operations from Projects. This includes accountability for operations support contracts, assurance on completion of risk management studies and action closure, handover of engineering information (data and documents).
The operations Readiness Coordinator (ORC) reports directly to the ORA position.
The role will work closely with stakeholders to deliver Operational Readiness Plan ORP, Commissioning, and safe Start-up of the facility and timely resolution of any issues which might arise. 

Responsibilities:

Leadership
Always demonstrate strong safety leadership and exemplary safety behaviours, ensuring that safety expectations are communicated and reinforced.
Carry out self-verification activities, participate in incident investigations if required.
Coaching and development of their direct reports to support the nationalisation agenda.
Lead the development of Operational Readiness Plans ORP and ensure inputs from stakeholders incorporated.
Ensure Lessons Learned from previous projects are included in ORP.
Lead pre-start-up workshops with relevant stakeholders.

Risk / Operating Discipline
Lead interface with stakeholders to ensure support is in place for the new facility in a timely fashion, and stakeholders understand project timeline & requirements.
Review HZOP Report and ensure the implementation of all HAZOP actions / Recommendations
Manage handover of engineering information (Data & documents) required for operations support in accordance with requirements for information.
Develop operational risk register for start-up covering different aspects of risks (start-up delay, HSE risks, Process safety risks, enduring risks carried over to operational phase, future vulnerabilities, etc.) 
Set up and lead risk review sessions with relevant parties, keep document updated, and ensure mitigation plans in place.
Ensure enduring risks to operational phase and vulnerabilities are well-documented and handed over to start up team.
Lead the development of COW strategy based on project execution plan & facilities operating model.

We help ensure mission success on land, air, sea, space and cyberspace for the Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, NASA and other federal agencies. KBR’s areas of expertise include engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity.  KBR strives to create a safer, more secure and sustainable world by bringing together the best and brightest to deliver technologies and solutions that help our customers accomplish their most critical missions and objectives.

The Mission Ahead

This role is within KBR/NSS Intel division.  At KBR Government Solutions, we don't just envision a world that's safer, more secure, and sustainable - we create it. Our legacy of delivering advanced full life cycle professional and technical solutions is matched only by our commitment to operational readiness and innovation. As stewards of critical missions for the Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, NASA, and other key federal entities, we excel in engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT, and cybersecurity. United in our quest for excellence, KBR stands at the vanguard, ready to transform possibilities into impactful realities for a better tomorrow.

Who YOU Are

You’re a skilled Generator Technician with a strong background in the installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of generator systems. Your expertise ensures that critical power solutions are reliable and ready to support mission success for our customers. You excel at diagnosing issues, performing repairs, and conducting preventative maintenance, ensuring that generators operate at peak performance in any environment.

At KBR, you bring a detail-oriented approach and a commitment to safety to every project. Known for your problem-solving skills and technical proficiency, you work effectively both independently and as part of a team, collaborating with other professionals to ensure that power systems are always operational and compliant with industry standards. Your proactive mindset and dedication to continuous improvement contribute to KBR’s mission of delivering innovative solutions that enhance operational readiness and security.

What You WILL DO

In the role of Generator Technician, your duties will include:

Troubleshooting: Capable of troubleshooting engines, fuel systems, controls, and generators using prints, diagrams, and specifications.

Maintenance and Repairs: Capable of maintaining and operating megawatt rated high amperage and high voltage generators.

Monitoring: Knowledge of working with and monitoring contracted maintenance services.

Oversight: Provide guidance and oversight for any person under your supervision.

Schedule: Willingness to work on-call, rotational shifts, and nights, weekends, and holidays as required.

Safety Compliance: Implement and uphold safety protocols during all operations, ensuring a safe work environment for yourself and others.

Collaboration: Work closely with cross-functional teams to coordinate activities and ensure seamless operations during power outages or emergencies.

Continuous Improvement: Stay updated on industry trends, technologies, and best practices to enhance generator performance and operational efficiency.

Emergency Response: Respond promptly to generator failures and emergencies, providing on-site support to restore power quickly and efficiently.

This is a contingent position based upon contract award and will be located OCONUS

REQUIREMENTS:

Must have a US SECRET clearance, and be eligible for upgrade to TS/SCI with Poly level Clearance.

High school diploma, Vocational or Trade school Graduate or equivalent apprenticeship.

Eight (8)+ years of professional Generator experience, three (3) of which are in a lead or supervisory role.

Experience troubleshooting engines, fuel systems, controls, and generators using prints, diagrams and specifications.

Experience maintaining and operating megawatt rated high amperage and high voltage generators.

Knowledge of working with and monitoring contracted maintenance services.

Willingness to work on-call, rotational shifts, and nights, weekends, and holidays as required.

Title:

Associate Systems Integrator

Belong. Connect. Grow. with KBR!

KBR’s National Security Solutions team provides high-end engineering and advanced technology solutions to our customers in the intelligence and national security communities. In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

KBR (formerly LinQuest) is the prime contractor on the MSEIT contract. By applying to this position, you are in consideration for KBR employment. However, you also have the option to be hired by one of our subcontractor teammates.

KBR is seeking a motivated Associate Systems Integrator to support the MSEIT contract at Space Systems Command (SSC). This position provides critical day-to-day coordination and program management support to the systems engineering and integration (SE&I) and Agile delivery teams.

The successful candidate will help organize multi-contractor activities, support software and tool procurement, manage status tracking and communication workflows, and ensure integration awareness across program teams. This role is ideal for someone seeking to grow into systems integration or program management leadership within a high-visibility Department of Defense (DoD) software and systems engineering program.

The MILSATCOM Systems Engineering, Integration, and Test (MSEIT) effort provides leading edge Systems Engineering & Integration (SE&I) for the US Space Force’s Space Systems Center (SSC). We support the Space Force’s acquisition of state of the art satellite communications systems, providing global secure, survivable, and protected communications for our nation’s warfighters. We seek technical individuals who will thrive in a highly collaborative work environment of small teams, using the most modern tools and methodologies to tackle the challenges of integrating complex space and ground communications systems.

Why Join Us?

Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

Key Responsibilities:

Program Coordination: Support planning, facilitation, and documentation of recurring working groups, technical reviews, and stakeholder meetings. Manage meeting logistics, agendas, and follow-up actions to ensure closure and accountability.

Integration Support: Assist the SE&I and program leadership teams in coordinating technical and programmatic activities across development, cyber, DevOps, and operations disciplines.

Procurement Coordination: Support tracking and coordination of software-related procurement actions, including license renewals, subscription management, and purchase requests.

License & Asset Tracking: Maintain visibility into software licensing, seat utilization, and expiration schedules to ensure uninterrupted tool availability across teams.

Status & Reporting: Collect, organize, and synthesize program status inputs; develop summary charts, dashboards, and other visual materials for internal and external reporting.

Cross-Team Collaboration: Coordinate among software, systems, and mission stakeholders to maintain alignment and awareness of dependencies.

Stakeholder Engagement: Interface with users, mission partners, OA representatives, and other government and contractor stakeholders to facilitate communication and coordination.

Tool & Workflow Adaptability: Operate effectively within heterogeneous collaboration ecosystems—MS Teams, Slack, Mattermost, Jira, Confluence, and others—bridging communication across diverse technical and organizational environments.

Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline coordination processes, improve document traceability, and enhance overall program communication efficiency.

Work Environment:

Location: On-site
Travel Requirements: Minimal
Working Hours: Standard

Qualifications:

Required:

An active DoD Secret clearance or the ability to obtain one required for this position
Technical Bachelor’s Degree
3–5 years of experience in program coordination, systems integration, or project support within a technical or defense environment.
Strong organizational, documentation, and analytical skills with attention to detail.
Familiarity with Agile practices and terminology (Scrum, PI planning, backlog management).
Proficiency with collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, MS Teams, Slack, Mattermost, and SharePoint.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience preparing presentation materials for leadership audiences.

Desired:

Prior experience supporting DoD acquisition, SE&I, or Space Systems Command (SSC) programs.
Knowledge of SATCOM systems, networks, or mission operations. Exposure to SAFe® or other scaled Agile frameworks.
Familiarity with DevOps, cloud-native, or Kubernetes-based environments.

Project Management Professional (PMP), SAFe Agilist, or other relevant certification (or willingness to pursue).

They have good commercial acumen to help in delivering secure optimal, compliant, and competitive, risk-managed category outcomes.

Becomes a trusted advisor and critical partner to stakeholders.  Builds relationships with the procurement teams globally, understanding stakeholder feedback and proactively working to build procurements reputation and ROI. 
Maintains close connectivity with FB&T ensuring appropriate prioritization and resourcing. 

Transformation and Change Management: Delivers modernization & transformation activities, leading optimization of regional category delivery, and creating incremental value, aligned to the broader category, procurement and business transformation agendas.

description:
Title:

Integrated Master Scheduler

Program Summary

Kord, a wholly owned subsidiary of KBR, is a leader in advanced defense solutions with a strong focus on directed energy and High Energy Laser (HEL) technologies. Our HEL programs support the U.S. Department of Defense in developing, integrating, and fielding cutting-edge laser weapon systems that enhance national security and provide decisive battlefield advantages. These programs demand precise planning, coordination, and execution to meet aggressive schedules and technical milestones.

Job Summary

The Integrated Master Scheduler serves as the primary authority for developing, maintaining, and analyzing Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) across multiple HEL programs. This role ensures that all contractual, technical, and program requirements are met as they pertain to the schedule, while maintaining alignment with resource constraints and delivery objectives. The scheduler partners closely with program management, engineering, finance, and supply chain teams to deliver accurate forecasting, identify risks, and provide schedule-driven insights that enable informed decision-making and timely corrective actions.

Roles and Responsibilities

· Develop and maintain Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) using Statement of Work (SOW) and Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) elements for initial program baselines and proposals.

· Modify and update program schedules during re-baselining efforts and ensure compliance with contractual requirements.

· Operate within the established program business cadence by leading monthly schedule status reviews, communicating schedule performance to Finance, and preparing Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) deliverables.

· Maintain resource-loaded program schedules through regular analysis of schedule status, critical path and variance metrics, network logic validation, and baseline maintenance.

· Utilize Gantt charts, driving path analysis, milestone tracking, Earned Value Management, and other project management techniques to monitor progress, identify performance variances, and enable timely intervention on critical areas.

· Ensure IMS compliance with Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) 14-point assessment guidelines and KBR standards.

· Support ad hoc customer requests for scenario modeling and impact assessments of schedule changes.

· Responsible for configuration management of the program schedule and associated subcontractor schedules.

· Coordinate with program leadership to align schedules with contractual deliverables, milestones, and technical objectives.

· Integrate subcontractor and supplier schedules into the overall program IMS.

· Support program Earned Value Management (EVM) requirements and deliverables by ensuring schedule data integrity and alignment with cost baselines.

· Provide regular schedule status reports, metrics, and briefings to program leadership and government customers.

· Drive IMS engagement during internal and external status sessions, including Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBRs).

· Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure accurate resource loading and forecasting.

Basic Qualifications

· Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Project Management, or related field.

· 5+ years of experience in program scheduling within defense or aerospace industries.

· Proficiency with scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project and/or Primavera (P6).

· Strong knowledge of Integrated Master Scheduling (IMS) practices and Earned Value Management (EVM).

· Experience with DCMA 14-point schedule analysis.

· Excellent communication and presentation skills for both technical and non-technical audiences.

· U.S. Citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Secret clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

· Master’s degree in Project Management, Engineering, or related discipline.

· 8+ years of experience in defense program scheduling, preferably with directed energy or advanced weapon systems.

· Prior experience supporting Army or DoD high energy laser programs.

· Familiarity with Agile program management practices.

· Advanced proficiency in Primavera P6 and Microsoft Project Server/Enterprise tools.

· Active DoD Secret or Top Secret clearance.

· Working knowledge of EVMS Standard (EIA 748-D) and Integrated Program Management Report (IPMR)

· Strong analytical skills with demonstrated ability to manage complex, multi-program schedules.

The role ensures timely response and resolution to technical issues related to systems, software, hardware, and network infrastructure, maintaining operational continuity and high user satisfaction.

Provides telephone, remote, and on-site technical support to employees on assigned systems, applications, and products. Answers questions about installation, configuration, operation, customization, and usage of IT systems and software.

Collect and analyse user feedback to identify problem trends and areas for process improvement or risk mitigation.

Support system updates, deployments, and standardization of desktop environments under guidance from the IT Management Team.

Strong troubleshooting skills with the ability to apply diagnostic techniques to identify problems, investigate causes, and recommend effective solutions.

Self-motivated, accountable, and customer focused.
Strong problem-solving and organizational abilities.
Excellent communication skills and good command of written and spoken English.
Ability to follow established processes and maintain performance under pressure.

description:
Title:

Principal Sustainability Advisor

Designing a Smarter, Greener Future 

At KBR, we’re passionate about creating infrastructure that’s smarter, safer, and truly sustainable. Our team brings together bold thinkers and technical experts to deliver environmental solutions that make a real difference—for our clients, our communities, and the planet. 

With over $2 billion in Green Star and ISCA-certified projects, we lead the way in sustainability strategy and innovation. From concept to construction and beyond, we help clients tackle critical challenges—integrating environmental considerations into every phase of delivery. 

Whether it’s improving energy efficiency, modeling emissions, assessing climate risks, or delivering whole-of-life analyses, we provide the insight and expertise to help projects meet and exceed sustainability targets. 

The Opportunity 

We have an exciting opportunity for a Principal Sustainability Advisor to join our National Sustainability team. In this senior role, you’ll lead sustainability input, advice, and expertise across major infrastructure projects—including water, rail, and road—as well as global Net Zero initiatives and defence projects. 

You’ll work closely with project teams to embed sustainability strategies from design through construction, delivering frameworks, management plans, and innovative solutions that leave a lasting legacy. 

What You’ll Do 

Lead sustainability strategies and provide technical advice on complex, large-scale projects. 

Drive adoption of sustainability initiatives during design and construction phases. 

Collaborate with multi-disciplinary teams to deliver positive environmental and community outcomes. 

Manage project planning, cost estimates, tender submissions, technical documentation, and client reporting. 

Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, authorities, and internal stakeholders. 

Mentor and guide junior consultants while advising senior management. 

Contribute to business development through proposals, budgets, and stakeholder engagement. 

Who You Are 

You’re a seasoned sustainability professional with a proven track record in infrastructure projects. You thrive on collaboration, leadership, and innovation, and you’re motivated by the success of your team. You bring integrity, accountability, and strong communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and deliver results. 

What You Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in sustainability, environmental engineering, or similar. 

Extensive experience in sustainability consulting within the infrastructure sector. 

Familiarity with Green Star or ISC rating tools (highly regarded). 

Strong stakeholder management and business development experience. 

Ability to manage complex projects, budgets, and deadlines. 

What We Do 

KBR’s Infrastructure Services team delivers projects that shape a smarter, more sustainable future for Australia. From transport and water to defence and buildings, we partner with clients nationwide to provide innovative solutions across every stage of the project lifecycle. 

With over 1,200 skilled professionals, we combine global expertise with local insight. Our teams are digitally connected, agile, and committed to social and environmental sustainability—driving innovation that benefits communities and the planet. 

Together, we deliver infrastructure for a better tomorrow. 

At KBR, We Value You 

While you’re busy delivering world-class engineering solutions, we make sure you have the flexibility and support to thrive. Enjoy family-friendly work arrangements, options for hybrid working, and a culture that prioritizes trust and collaboration. 

You’ll have access to ongoing professional development and the chance to work alongside some of the industry’s most respected experts. With the resources of a global organization and the close-knit feel of a local team, you’ll never be just a number. 

Help shape tomorrow by applying today! 

Don’t miss out on this opportunity to leave your impact on our society with one of Australia’s leading infrastructure businesses. Apply now and follow us on LinkedIn to stay up to date with all the latest news and job opportunities. 

Our people are the heart of everything we do. We are dedicated to creating work environments where every member of our team feels safe, supported, respected, trusted, and valued—and where everyone has opportunities to belong, connect, and grow.

An Associate Degree in a related field, such as environmental science or chemistry.

A minimum of 5 years’ experience in water treatment

Must possess excellent communication skills.

Experience treating HVAC Chillers

Location:                             Basra, Iraq

Required:                            Expats

About Company

"Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

The KBR team delivers future-forward science, technology and engineering solutions and mission-critical services that help governments and companies around the world accomplish their most important objectives, while also helping achieve their sustainability goals.

KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design and engineering capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets."

Roles and Responsibilities:

The Cost Engineer will report to the Project Control Manager. 

Specific responsibilities include:

•    Full understanding of the commercial aspect of the project contract and the application to the cost management

•    Understand contract specific cost procedures and carry out all work in accordance with these,

•    Study and understand all relevant project documents relating to the cost management of allocated project(s)

•    Work with all relevant projects and discipline personnel to ensure that cost control procedures are followed,

•    Set Up project/projects within Cost System to agreed format,

•    Establishing project control budgets based on the client approved Project Control Estimate,

•    Reviewing cost commitment and expenditure information (for all cost elements), for input to the computerized cost control and reporting system on a weekly basis and ensuring that all information received is accurate and correctly input,

•    Producing regular cost reports and advising management of any forecast cost overruns as soon as possible to allow corrective actions to be taken in a timely manner. Highlighting areas of concern and suggesting areas of improvement,

•    Maintaining comprehensive accessible registers of financial approvals, variations and change orders,

•    Review project man-hours and the allocation of man-hours in conjunction with Planning on a regular basis

•    Liaising with the Project Management, Finance, Contracts and Procurement departments with regards to establishing monthly evaluation of work done, goods received and services rendered for invoice preparation and verification

•    Ensure that all cost related work is in compliance with the contract,

•    Maintain rates within Computerized Cost System, ensuring they are up to date and all rate uplifts are implemented. Advise Project Management of additional costs involved and assist in obtaining additional approval from client,

•    Check that all estimates meet contract requirements and all relevant cost information is fed back to the estimates,

•    When Project specific Cost Procedures are in place ensure they have been implemented in full,

•    Maintain a good working knowledge of relevant corporate cost software,

•    Ensure that adequate control of commitment is in place,

•    Supervise and encourage junior and assistant personnel, including checking their work,

•    Participate in schedule risk analysis as required,

•    Ensure that the Corporate and Project Specific Change Control procedures are being adhered to

Education, Skills & Experience:

Education

•    Bachelor’s Degree in an engineering discipline

Experience and Skill set

•    Minimum 8 years experience in Oil and Gas Industry in Cost Engineering roles.

•    Minimum 5 years experience in Oil and Gas related project delivery related projects

•    Minimum 5 years experience in Oil and Gas Project Delivery as a Umbrella Contract Senior Cost Engineer

•    Ability to work and manage in a multi-cultural environment with good understanding of cost estimation parameters to be considered in Middle East.

•    Skill to actively engage with different project disciplines

•    Ability to work and manage in a multi-cultural environment
